findings.title: Cycle arm marks variants stale on INSTALLED, not on CHANGED — voids the 15.1% recovery
findings.claim: Palette_Compose's .cycling arm sets PAL_ACT_VARIANT_STALE unconditionally on every frame a cycle script is merely installed, so any section combining a cycle script with a bound variant pays the full ~19,332-cycle variant re-derive every single frame — the exact 15.1%-of-frame regression the stale gate (PAL_ACT_VARIANT_STALE) was built to remove.
findings.evidence: palette.emp:353-357: `.cycling: btst #1, Pal_Active / beq .fade / ori.b #PAL_ACT_VARIANT_STALE, Pal_Active   // rotation moves lines 1-3 / jbsr Palette_DoCycle`. The comment claims 'rotation moves lines 1-3', but the ori runs BEFORE Palette_DoCycle decides whether any rotation happens: DoCycle rotates only when a channel timer hits 0 (palette.emp:419-421, `tst.b (a3,d5.w) / bne .wait`), and OJZ_ShimmerCycle's period 8 means 8 of every 9 frames rotate nothing. Concrete walk on shipped content: OJZ_Preset_Sec3 (ojz_effects.emp:574) binds cycle: OJZ_ShimmerCycle AND variants: [Variant_Water_Deep, 0], so Pal_Active carries CYCLE|VARIANT. Every frame: the .cycling arm sets STALE -> DoCycle decrements a timer and touches nothing -> the .variants arm (palette.emp:383-386) sees VARIANT&&STALE and runs Palette_DoVariants, recomputing a bit-identical 48-entry staging image at the measured 19,332 cyc = 15.1% of frame (palette.emp:106-110), whose output section 3 never even streams (its raster channel is Raster_Program_None). Even on the 1-in-9 rotation frame the rotated span (line 2 entries 8-11) is disjoint from the only spans any shipped OP_PAL_REGION reads (line 2 entries 4-6), so the useful recompute fraction is zero. The .fade arm (line 363) has the same shape at smaller scale: STALE is set on every fade frame though Palette_DoFade steps the buffer only on even parity (palette.emp:502-504).
findings.fix_sketch: Move the staleness decision to where change is actually known: Palette_DoCycle already accumulates a touched-line mask in d7 (line 422, `bset d0, d7`) — set PAL_ACT_VARIANT_STALE there only when d7 != 0 (or, sharper, when d7 intersects any bound variant's v_lines). Same for DoFade: set STALE only on the parity frames that step. One-instruction moves; no format or RAM change.

findings.title: Variant derive granularity: 48 entries recomputed to feed build-time-known 3-word spans
findings.claim: Palette_DeriveVariant derives every entry of every covered line (default v_lines %1110 = 3 lines x 16 = 48 entries, the measured 19,332 cyc), but every consumer of the staging image reads spans the comptime encoder already knows exactly — OP_PAL_REGION carries (slot, line, entry, count<=3) and the ship trailer carries the same — so ~94% of the derive work computes bytes nothing can ever read.
findings.evidence: The only readers of Pal_Variant_Stage are Raster_HInt's .op_region (raster.emp:741-762, streams `count-1<=RASTER_CRAM_MAX` words from a comptime offset) and Raster_BuildShipEntry (raster.emp:1038-1056, DMA of the trailer's `colour count` <= 3). Both spans are authored constants flowing through stream_pal_region()/ship_trailer() (raster_dsl.emp:204-219, 1633-1666). Shipped content references exactly one span: pal_stage_off(0,2,4) count 3 (OJZ_TC_HAND word 72, ojz_effects.emp:645-658). Yet the derive walks 16 entries x every line in v_lines (palette.emp:686-741, `moveq #16-1, d7` per covered line), and Variant_Water_Deep uses the default lines: %1110 (ojz_effects.emp:507), so 48 entries derive to feed 3. At ~400 cyc/entry (19,332/48), the referenced-span derive is ~1.2k cyc vs 19.3k — a 16x cut on every frame the stale bit legitimately fires (every other fade frame, every rotation frame once finding 1 is fixed).
findings.fix_sketch: The encoder can pre-resolve the demand set: patched/static program install (or Palette_SetVariant) registers per-slot (line, entry, count) spans — the same words the program already carries — into a small RAM demand list; Palette_DoVariants derives only those spans into the unchanged pal_stage_off layout (partial fill, same addressing). Alternatively the cheap 3x cut with zero mechanism: author Variant_Water_Deep with lines: %0100 since nothing reads its lines 1 and 3. Also note Pal_Variant_Stage's line-0 quarter (32 bytes x 2 slots) is unwritable by construction (pal_stage_off ensures line>=1) — 64 bytes of RAM bought purely for the *32 addressing.

findings.title: Install protocol: two disjoint paths with hand-ordered fences instead of one staged consume
findings.claim: The install/publish protocol has more phases than the problem: static programs use a clean staged-pointer protocol (Raster_Install -> Raster_Pending, consumed atomically at Raster_VBlank), while patched programs mutate five RAM cells directly from the main loop (Raster_Patch_Tab, Raster_Active_Buf, Raster_Program, Raster_Pending, Effects_Offscreen_Entry), and correctness now rests on four separately-reasoned write orderings spread across three procs — each one the residue of a race that was found and fixed individually.
findings.evidence: The fences, each with its own hazard essay: (1) Raster_InstallPatched:931 `move.l a1, Raster_Patch_Tab // table first` — 'the race the builder's VBlank timing would otherwise expose' (raster.emp:920-927); (2) raster.emp:955-968 the Effects_Offscreen_Entry clear-then-publish-last dance — 'a VBlank landing in that window shipped the PREVIOUS program's source/destination/length ... a VBlank lands in this window ROUTINELY'; (3) Effects_InstallPreset (preset.emp:208-227) must clr Raster_Patch_Tab and Effects_Offscreen_Entry BEFORE seeding anchors or 'a visible one-frame boundary jump at every crossing'; (4) Raster_VBlank's own install path clears Patch_Tab + Offscreen_Entry on BOTH branches (raster.emp:554-572). Five cells, three writers, two execution contexts — where the static path already proves one staged pointer suffices ('it takes effect at the next Raster_VBlank, so an install can never tear a frame mid-walk', raster.emp:486). Every documented window exists only because the patched path publishes derived state from the main loop instead of staging the template and letting VBlank derive.
findings.fix_sketch: Unify on the staged shape: Raster_Pending carries any template (plus a kind word, or stage the whole raster channel of the preset: {template, anchors}); Raster_VBlank's consume derives Patch_Tab, Active_Buf, the ship DMAEntry, the Dense_Lines clear and the anchor seed in one place that is atomic w.r.t. HInt by position. All four fences and their six defensive clears become structural instead of remembered; Raster_InstallPatched reduces to one move.l. Cost: Build_DMA_Entry (~small) moves into VBlank.

findings.title: Dispatch compare chain has crossed the table breakeven at 5 rungs
findings.claim: At 5 rungs the compare-chain dispatch charges the fall-through op (OP_SET_REG — present in every shipped program via reg_sh_on) 80 cycles of a ~60-cycle-budget handler, versus ~22 flat for the pc-indexed jump table the format was explicitly designed to drop back into, and each new opcode now costs a re-measure ritual (F1/F5), a depth-pin edit, and a byte-cliff Bcc audit — O(opcodes) maintenance for a mechanism the data made O(1)-ready from day one.
findings.evidence: raster.emp:708-713: 'at this few opcodes it is fewer cycles than the table setup ... The opcodes stay byte offsets so a table can drop back in without touching the program format.' The 'few opcodes' premise has expired: five rungs (OP_CRAM/PAL_REGION/RUN_GRADIENT/RUN_RAMP/PAL_RESTORE, raster.emp:714-723), and raster_dsl's own model prices SetReg dispatch at RUNG*RUNGS = 16*5 = 80 cyc (raster_dsl.emp:1046), with the R1 rung tax measured on real fixtures (F1 396->412, F5 612->628, raster_dsl.emp:1125,1133). Both shipped OJZ event fires carry a SetReg (OJZ_TEST_HAND and OJZ_TC_HAND both open with `0, $8C89`). A `jmp .table(pc,d1.w)` on the already-byte-offset opcodes is ~22 cyc for every op, deletes RASTER_DEPTH_* and the 'TRAP for opcode 12's author' block (raster_dsl.emp:1030-1041). The stated blocker is tooling, not hardware: 'a computed jmp defeats the contract-closure dataflow' (raster.emp:711).
findings.fix_sketch: Book as a sigil ask: a declared-dispatch annotation (bounded jump table with named targets) the contract closure can enumerate. When it lands, flip the chain to the table, delete the depth pins, re-measure once — after which the model's dispatch term becomes a single constant and opcode additions stop re-pricing existing programs.

findings.title: Raster_BuildSchedule re-records every VBlank even when no latched line moved
findings.claim: While a patched program is live the whole schedule is re-derived and re-copied into the inactive buffer every VBlank, though its only inputs are Effects_Screen_L[ch] (4 words) and the static template — on frames where the camera and anchors are unchanged (idle, horizontal-only scroll) the rebuild reproduces the live buffer byte-for-byte.
findings.evidence: raster.emp:1101-1183: the only early-out is `move.l Raster_Patch_Tab, d0 / beq .none`. For OJZ_TwoChannel each VBlank walks 2 table entries (~15 instructions each, ~250 cyc) plus copies 18+14 = 32 body bytes = 16 words through `move.w (a2)+,(a1)+ / dbf` (~22 cyc/word, ~350 cyc) plus prologue/terminator/park writes — roughly 700-800 cyc of VBlank per frame, spent against a ~7.3k-cycle VBlank window that also carries DMA, on every frame including ones where Effects_LatchWorldLines produced the same 4 words as last frame (raster.emp:1289-1300 shows the derivation is exactly `anchor - Camera_Y` per channel, so vertical-camera-still frames are bit-identical inputs).
findings.fix_sketch: Keep a 4-word Effects_Screen_L snapshot from the last build; compare (4x cmp.w, ~60 cyc) and skip the rebuild+swap when equal — the live buffer is already the correct schedule and the cursor rewind to Raster_Active_Buf is unchanged. Invalidate the snapshot on any install path (the three sites that already clear Raster_Patch_Tab).

coverage_notes: Walked, in order: engine/effects/raster.emp in full (both halves — opcode/constant layer, comptime dense constructors, Raster_Install/Raster_VBlank/Raster_HInt, then InstallPatched/BuildShipEntry/BuildSchedule/GetChannelBand/LatchWorldLines/SetWorldY); games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp in full (the ground truth for data shape: programs of 1-2 fires, 1-2 ops, 2-record patch tables, one variant slot live act-wide); engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp in full (descriptors, constructors, compose, cost model + fixture pins, check_intervals/check_density, encoder, patch_table/ship_trailer, layout guards, band twins); engine/effects/preset.emp in full (EffectsPreset, preset(), Effects_InstallPreset); engine/effects/palette.emp in full (compose pipeline, cycle/fade/operator/variant layers); engine/effects/palette_dsl.emp in full; engine/system/hblank.emp in full; engine/system/vblank.emp and engine/level/parallax.emp by targeted grep at their effects touchpoints only (Raster_VBlank ordering, Effects_InstallPreset call, Raster_GetChannelBand consumer), not walked line-by-line. Judged and cleared at altitude: the arm-word relative-gap schedule representation (right algorithm for the reg-$0A reload semantics), the two-priming-record protocol, empty-program-uninstalls, the Vsram-as-OP_CRAM wire dedup, compose()'s line-scan merge (O(221*n) comptime only — fine at build time), pairwise check_density (sufficient: a fire that fits its gap cannot compound into the pair after), the cost model + fixture-pin architecture (exemplary), the double-buffer swap, and the per-frame handler re-install (deliberately idempotent). NOT reached: the gate/tool layer (tools/effects_gates.py, raster_source_gate.py, raster_off_gate.py, raster_cost_probe.py, effects_budget_check.py + its test, effects_scene_assert.py, effects_budget_model.toml) and games/sonic4/test/poison/*.emp — other seats own gate soundness and my altitude questions were answerable from the runtime/encoder corpus; no findings above depend on tool behaviour. All analysis static; no build, no emulator.

findings.title: Five hand-sized .s conditionals violate the unsized-branch law; one sits inside the cycle-modeled dispatch chain
findings.claim: raster.emp carries five explicitly sized conditionals (`beq.s`/`bne.s`) in a non-@as_compat, non-patched-field module, which CODING_CONVENTIONS §1.4/§10 forbid ('write the branch unsized... Explicit sizes remain only in @as_compat ports and self-modified/patched fields'), and they are the only such sites in the entire engine tree except one in objects/animate.emp.
findings.evidence: Lines 518 `beq.s .no_install`, 549 `bne.s .copy_program`, 590 `beq.s .done`, 715 `beq.s .op_cram`, 835 `bne.s .ramp_body`. Engine-wide grep for sized conditionals returns exactly these 5 plus 1 in animate.emp — every other branch in the effects corpus is unsized. Line 715 is especially inconsistent: it is rung 1 of Raster_HInt's dispatch chain while rungs 2-5 on lines 717/719/721/723 are unsized (`beq .op_region` etc.), yet raster_dsl.emp's cost model (line 964: 'The dispatch chain is four `beq.s` rungs... a matched one is 8 + 10 = 18') prices ALL rungs at .s widths and its own trap note (raster_dsl.emp:1038: 'check the new rung's beq still assembles .s... a 4-cyc mispricing the pin cannot see') documents that the unsized rungs relax SILENTLY past the byte cliff. Failure walk per the law's own text: code growth between line 518 and .no_install past ±127 bytes fails the build loudly on the pinned .s (dead ceremony), while the same growth on the unsized rungs silently relaxes to .w and mis-prices the calibrated model by 4 cyc/rung — the mixed spelling gets the worst of both.
findings.fix_sketch: Strip the five .s suffixes (sigil emits the short form by reach anyway). If a width is genuinely meant as a timing pin for the dispatch chain, that is not one of the law's two sanctioned exceptions — either extend §1.4's exception list explicitly or add an ensure/gate on the emitted encodings; do not pin one rung of five.

findings.title: Four missed mandatory tail calls (§2.8) on per-frame paths
findings.claim: CODING_CONVENTIONS §2.8 ('When the last instruction before rts is jbsr Target, replace the pair with jbra Target. Saves 10 cycles and 4 bytes.') is violated at four sites in the subject files, all on per-frame code paths.
findings.evidence: raster.emp:560-561 `jbsr HBlank_Uninstall` / `rts` (Raster_VBlank teardown arm); raster.emp:622-624 `jbsr HBlank_Install` / `.done:` / `rts` (Raster_VBlank install arm — runs EVERY frame a program is live); palette.emp:386-389 `jbsr Palette_DoVariants` / `.done:` / `rts` (Palette_Compose, per frame); palette.emp:666-668 `jbsr Palette_DeriveVariant` / `.ret:` / `rts` (Palette_DoVariants slot 1). All four callees' clobber sets are subsets of their callers' declared clobbers (HBlank_Install clobbers(d1) ⊆ Raster_VBlank's d0-d4/a0-a2; Palette_DeriveVariant d0-d7/a2-a3 ⊆ Palette_DoVariants' d0-d7/a0-a3), so conversion is contract-clean — and the codebase demonstrably knows the rule: Raster_BuildShipEntry:1055 ends `jbra Build_DMA_Entry` correctly. Cost walk: Raster_VBlank's install arm pays 10 wasted cycles (rts) every armed frame.
findings.fix_sketch: Convert each jbsr to jbra; where the following rts is a shared label target (.done/.ret), keep the labeled rts for the other predecessors.

findings.title: lsl.w #1,dN in hot palette loops where §2.5 mandates add.w dN,dN
findings.claim: Six `lsl.w #1, dN` sites in palette.emp's per-frame loops violate the §2.5 instruction-selection table row 'lsl.w #1, d0 → add.w d0, d0 (2 cycles faster)'.
findings.evidence: Lines 521, 544 (Palette_DoFade .word loop — 48 iterations per stepping frame), 603, 619 (Palette_DoOperator .fw_word loop — 48 iterations per fade step), 708, 734 (Palette_DeriveVariant .entry loop — 16 entries x up to 3 lines x up to 2 slots). lsl.w #1,dN = 8 cycles vs add.w dN,dN = 4. Concrete cost walk for the worst consumer: Palette_DeriveVariant runs 2 such shifts per entry; a full 3-line 2-slot derive is 96 entries = 192 shifts = ~768 wasted cycles on every stale-derive frame — in the exact routine the module's own comments flag as the measured 15.1%-of-frame hot spot (palette.emp:106-110). During an operator fade both DoOperator and the forced re-derive run in the same frame.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace each `lsl.w #1, dN` with `add.w dN, dN` (identical result for these unsigned 3-bit repacks). The `lsl.w #8` + `lsl.w #1` B-channel pairs become lsl.w #8 + add.w.

findings.title: Runtime-walked wire structs lack (size: N) — pal_cycle_channel's 6-byte stride is hand-walked unguarded
findings.claim: pal_variant, pal_cycle_channel, PalCycleScript1/2 (palette.emp) and RasterGradientProgram/RasterRampProgram (raster.emp:307/382) declare no `(size: N)` and no sizeof ensure, diverging from CLAUDE.md's key rule 'struct (size: N) for ALL data structures' — and for pal_cycle_channel the runtime hard-codes the layout with no guard to catch drift.
findings.evidence: palette.emp:149-156 `pub struct pal_cycle_channel { pc_line: u8, ... pc_pad: u8 }` — no size assertion. Palette_DoCycle (palette.emp:413-418) walks it as five `move.b (a0)+` reads plus `addq.l #1, a0 // skip pad`, i.e. the 6-byte stride is restated by hand in the consumer. Failure scenario: a field added to pal_cycle_channel (or pc_period widened to u16) recompiles the DSL constructor cleanly, but Palette_DoCycle's hand walk silently reads misaligned bytes — garbage line/count/period per channel from the second channel on, with no build error anywhere (contrast bganim_band, bg_anim.emp:67, which guards its hand-tracked walk with `ensure(sizeof(bganim_band) == 44, ...)`, and EffectsPreset, preset.emp:56, whose `(size: 38)` saga documents exactly this class catching a real wrong-size bug). RasterGradientProgram/RasterRampProgram are likewise runtime-copied wire images (Raster_VBlank copies RASTER_BUF_SIZE bytes from them) with no size pin.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `(size: 8)` to pal_variant, `(size: 6)` to pal_cycle_channel, and sizes to the two Raster*Program structs; optionally respell bganim_band's ensure as (size: 44) per §1.6's stated preference.

findings.title: Raster_HInt's `with ints_off { }` body not indented — §10 strict bracket nesting
findings.claim: The entire ~200-line body of Raster_HInt inside `with ints_off {` sits at the same indent level as the `with` itself, violating §10's tranche-2 rule 'EVERYTHING inside a { } indents at least one level (4 spaces)... each nested bracket indents one more'.
findings.evidence: raster.emp:656-657: `        with ints_off {` immediately followed by `        movem.l d0-d1/a1-a2, -(sp)` at the identical 8-space column, through the closing `}` at line 859. The same construct in the same corpus is compliant: vblank.emp:123-125 `with z80_stopped {` / 12-space-indented `move.b #1, SND_DMA_ACTIVE_SLOT` / `}`, and vblank.emp:131-218's `with z80_stopped if ...` block indents its whole pipeline one level. Pure formatting — zero byte effect — but it is intra-corpus drift on a rule the conventions doc attributes to an explicit owner ruling.
findings.fix_sketch: Indent the bracket body one level (or, if the 200-line handler is a deliberate exemption to preserve asm columns, record the exemption in §10).

findings.title: Struct-name case drift inside palette.emp and across the effects files; §4.1 has no struct-name row
findings.claim: palette.emp mixes snake_case and PascalCase struct type names in the same file (pal_variant/pal_cycle_channel at lines 129/149 vs PalCycleScript1/PalCycleScript2 at 161/162), and raster.emp uses PascalCase (RasterGradientProgram/RasterRampProgram) — while CODING_CONVENTIONS §4.1's naming table covers routines, RAM, constants, locals, fields, comptime fns, enums and SST overlays but has no row for struct type names at all.
findings.evidence: palette.emp:129 `pub struct pal_variant {` and :149 `pub struct pal_cycle_channel {` versus :161 `pub struct PalCycleScript1 { pcs_count: u16, ... }` — two casing schemes 12 lines apart in one module. Tree-wide the same split exists (structs.emp: Sec/DMAEntry/CharacterDef vs parallax_config; parallax.emp: band_entry), so no fix can cite the law — the law is silent. This is the one naming axis §4.1 does not legislate, and the effects suite now exhibits both spellings in one file.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a struct-name row to §4.1 (the dominant tree convention is PascalCase) and, if ratified, rename pal_variant/pal_cycle_channel at a byte-neutral moment (type names emit nothing; pure source rename).

findings.title: and.w #imm where the corpus and §2.5 use andi.w
findings.claim: bg_anim.emp:149 `and.w   #BGANIM_BANKS-1, d1` is the only immediate-AND in the subject corpus not spelled andi, against §2.5's table row 'and.w #$FF → andi.w #$FF (identical, but be consistent)'.
findings.evidence: Grep across the subject files: this is the sole `and.w #` site; raster.emp (7 andi uses) and palette.emp (23 andi uses) spell every immediate AND as andi.w/andi.b (e.g. raster.emp:1235 `andi.w #RASTER_MAX_PATCH-1, d0`). Encoding-identical (AS/sigil assemble both to ANDI), so zero byte or cycle effect — consistency only, which is precisely what the table row asks for.
findings.fix_sketch: Spell it andi.w.

findings.title: §5.2 one-line file headers and §10 never-change-history are dead letters in the effects corpus — law/practice desync
findings.claim: The written law ('Every .emp file starts with a one-line description. No multi-line headers', §5.2; 'Comments describe function, never change-history', §10) is systematically contradicted by the effects corpus, whose multi-paragraph headers and dated change-history comments are clearly deliberate, owner-endorsed practice — the doc and the practice cannot both be the law.
findings.evidence: raster.emp opens with a 9-line header including provenance history ('Pure code motion... byte-for-byte what shipped in chain 105', lines 1-9); dated change-history narration is pervasive and load-bearing: raster.emp:674-681 'CORRECTED 2026-08-14. This comment used to conclude...', raster_dsl.emp:1125 '// measured 2026-08-17 at RUNGS=5... (was 396 at RUNGS=4)', ojz_effects.emp:622 'LO WAS 40 UNTIL Parcel W SHIPPED AND SOMEBODY LOOKED AT IT'. These comments carry measurement provenance the gate culture depends on, and the project's own working notes treat comments as the record — so the divergence to fix is in the DOC, not the code. As written, §5.2/§10 would condemn essentially every subject file; a reviewer or subagent applying the letter of the law would 'clean up' evidence trails the substrate freeze relies on.
findings.fix_sketch: Amend §5.2/§10 to say what the practice actually is: headers may be multi-paragraph when they carry design rationale; comments may carry dated measurement/decision provenance; what stays banned is uninformative changelog noise. Cheap doc edit, and it should land before the P1 migration freeze turns these files into trusted substrate that later reviewers sweep against the current wording.

coverage_notes: Read CODING_CONVENTIONS.md in full first (the charter's law text), then walked the subject .emp files in this order, every line: engine/effects/raster.emp (both halves, 1-1316), engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp (1-1949), engine/effects/palette.emp (1-768), engine/effects/preset.emp (1-308), engine/effects/palette_dsl.emp (1-126), engine/level/bg_anim.emp (1-207), engine/system/hblank.emp (1-82), engine/system/vblank.emp (1-418), games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp (1-726), plus samples of the poison lane (poison_sentinel.emp, poison_band_h2_sh.emp, README.md — clean ceremonially; the remaining 10 poison files were not read line-by-line, but they are ensures-only zero-byte modules of the same template). Calibration greps ran engine-wide for sized branches, struct declarations, immediate-AND spelling, and lsl #1 sites so every 'divergence' claim is measured against the corpus norm, not just the doc. Checked specifically: branch-sizing ceremony (finding 1), jbsr/jbra/raw-jsr discipline incl. §2.8 tail calls (finding 2; vblank.emp:84's `jsr (a0)` is the sanctioned register-indirect form), comptime-vs-runtime math (clean — the 10n shift-add at raster.emp:951-953 and the no-mulu rule are honored everywhere), struct/(size:N) ceremony (finding 4), region/vars usage (clean — both RAM span guards phrase against extern() marks with documented reasons), naming case for procs/consts/locals/comptime fns (clean; struct-name drift is finding 6; PascalCase comptime-enum variants like RasterOp.SetReg were deliberately NOT flagged — §4.1's ALL_CAPS enum row plainly governs C-style value enums and PascalCase sum-type variants are the settled tree norm incl. engine.vdp), dead ceremony (clean — the corpus is unusually good at deleting dead helpers and documenting why survivors survive, e.g. ojz_effects' measured-redundant `use` lines), and formatting/bracket nesting (finding 5). NOT reached / out of my seat: the gate/tool layer (tools/effects_gates.py, raster_source_gate.py, raster_off_gate.py, raster_cost_probe.py, effects_budget_check.py + its test, effects_scene_assert.py, effects_budget_model.toml) — Python, not governed by the .emp ceremony law I was charged with; no correctness review of them was attempted. parallax.emp walker/fill internals untouched per charter; its touchpoints seen only as callers/callees in preset.emp and raster.emp comments. The two booked known-open items (Raster_Buf_B observability, EFX-4b .copy_program over-read) were recognized at their sites and not re-reported; nothing new about either surfaced on the ceremony axis. No emulator tools touched; no files modified; read-only greps and reads only.

findings.title: Offscreen-ship dropped-base gate hardcodes palette line 2 while the encoder admits lines 1-3
findings.claim: Enqueue_Dirty_Buffers' ship gate tests `btst #2, Palette_Dirty` (palette line 2's base-ship status) unconditionally, but ship_trailer/stream_pal_region admit shipped regions on any of lines 1-3, so for a line-1 or line-3 ship the gate reads the wrong line's dropped-DMA state.
findings.evidence: buffers.emp:399-403: `// btst instead of a saved carry: bit 2 CLEAR means line 2 either shipped this frame or was not dirty ... btst #2, Palette_Dirty / bne .no_ship`. The trailer's CRAM address is authored data: raster_dsl.emp op_ship_cram_addr returns the fire's own stream_pal_region address, and stream_pal_region's ensure allows `pal_line 1..3` (raster_dsl.emp:208-209). Walk: author `patchable(fx_tint_band(line: L, slot: 0, pal_line: 3, entry: 4, count: 3, sh: 0), ch: 0, lo: 3, hi: 220, offscreen_ship: 1)` — builds clean (every comptime guard passes). On a frame where the anchor is above the screen (latched L <= 0) and the DMA queue drops line 3's base ship (bit 3 stays SET) while line 2 is clean (bit 2 clear), the gate passes and queues Static_Pal_Ship over a line-3 region whose base reload never landed — exactly the state the btst exists to refuse (its own comment: "shipping over a line that did not get reloaded is not a state to add to"). Inverse error too: a dropped line-2 base blocks a line-3 ship that was actually safe. Latent: the only shipped trailer (OJZ_TwoChannel, addr $48) is on line 2, so no current data reaches it — but the P1 freeze bakes this consumer as trusted substrate.
findings.fix_sketch: Comptime-resolve it, per project law: ship_trailer already knows the address, so either (a) ensure `(op_ship_cram_addr(o) >> 5) == 2` in ship_trailer until the consumer generalises (turns the latent mismatch into a build refusal), or (b) emit the derived dirty-line bit (1 << (addr >> 5)) as a trailer word and have buffers.emp `btst` that value instead of the literal 2.

findings.title: Per-op/per-fire ceilings are constructor-only, violating the tree's own ratified 8F/8A precedent
findings.claim: raster_program's tree-wide bypass-proof scan covers only reg $0F and reg $0A words, so every other op-level bound — RASTER_CRAM_MAX, the 2-stream-op and 4-op fire ceilings, and the CRAM line-0 character-palette ban — remains a constructor-only refusal that direct enum construction bypasses, which the module's own precedent declares insufficient.
findings.evidence: raster_dsl.emp:1378-1380 states the precedent: "constructor-only refusals are not refusals — the $8F/$8A precedent", and the E-D scan at :1383-1389 checks only `op_reg_word(o) >> 8` against $8F/$8A. RasterOp is deliberately `pub` ("the match arms are the wire contract", :1370), so `raster_program([RasterFire.Fire(50, [RasterOp.Cram($02, [$0E,$0E,$0E,$0E,$0E,$0E,$0E,$0E])])])` is an admitted spelling that never passes through stream_cram or fire(): it builds a program whose handler streams 8 words in one fire (op_words emits `cols.len - 1` = 7 verbatim, :721-724), blowing the ~60-cycle HBlank window into active-display dot noise, AND writes CRAM line 0 — the character's palette — with op_mask forcing a spurious line-0 re-assert every frame (:891). check_density partially charges the cost but the per-fire HBlank-landing property and the line-0 ban are not schedule properties, so nothing program-level refuses either. The poison lane confirms the gap: poison_direct_8a.emp / poison_direct_8f.emp are the only direct-`RasterOp.` construction poisons — none exists for an oversized Cram or a line-0 address.
findings.fix_sketch: Extend the existing E-D program-level walk with the op-level facts the constructors check, via the already-total comptime accessors: per fire, sum op_stream_words <= RASTER_CRAM_MAX and count op_is_reg==0 <= 2; per CRAM-class op, `(a >> 5) != 0` (op_cram_span already exposes the address). One loop, zero bytes, and it inherits the same "cannot be dodged" property the $8F/$8A scan has. Add one poison twin.

findings.title: NEW on booked EFX-4b: static programs need no RAM copy at all — walk the ROM template directly
findings.claim: The static-program install path copies a fixed 128 bytes into Raster_Buf_A although a static program is never written at runtime, so pointing Raster_Active_Buf at the ROM program directly is a fourth fix option EFX-4b's booking does not list — it closes the over-read structurally, deletes the copy, and removes the 128-byte static-tier size ceiling that exists only because of the copy.
findings.evidence: EXPLICITLY new information on a booked item, not a re-report: docs/BUGS.md EFX-4b lists three fixes — "a length word, or a bounded copy, or padding static programs the way patched ones already are" — all of which preserve the copy; none is the no-copy option. The copy: raster.emp:573-578 `lea Raster_Buf_A, a2 / move.l a2, Raster_Active_Buf / move.w #(RASTER_BUF_SIZE / 2) - 1, d1 / .copy: move.w (a1)+, (a2)+ / dbf d1, .copy`. Nothing ever writes a static program's buffer: Raster_HInt only reads through Raster_Cursor (its sole stores are to reg $0A/VDP_DATA and RAM cells, :698-853), and Raster_BuildSchedule — the only buffer writer — early-outs on `Raster_Patch_Tab == 0` (:1102-1103), which .copy_program itself just cleared (:568). The handler already fetches its own code and, for OP_RUN_GRADIENT, streams data from ROM mid-HInt, so ROM reads in handler context are established practice with identical bus timing. Downstream simplifications fall out: the `out.len * 2 <= 128` ensure at raster_dsl.emp:1526-1527 exists for the copy ("Raster_VBlank's static-program path copies a FIXED RASTER_BUF_SIZE bytes into Buf_A") and would become patched-tier-only, lifting an authoring ceiling on static programs; Buf_A/Buf_B stay as the patched double-buffer pair unchanged (Raster_InstallPatched sets Active_Buf = Buf_B explicitly, :985-987, and the builder's not-active pick only runs under a live Patch_Tab). Byte-moving, hence cheap NOW and fix->repin->refreeze churn after the P1 freeze.
findings.fix_sketch: In .copy_program: `move.l d0, Raster_Program / clr.l Raster_Patch_Tab / clr.l Effects_Offscreen_Entry / move.l d0, Raster_Active_Buf` and delete the copy loop. Move raster_program's 128-byte ensure into patched_program (where the 64-word pad already enforces it). Update EFX-4b's booking either way — even if rejected, the option should be on the entry.

findings.title: Budget model carries two pre-R1 stale fire costs (F1 396->412, water 660->676) in its ungated half
findings.claim: sparse_fire_reg1_cycles = 396 and sparse_fire_water_cycles = 660 predate Parcel R1's fifth dispatch rung and disagree with the shipped model and its re-measured pins, and the [symbols] gate cannot see these rows — the exact ungated-row drift class EFX-5/EFX-9 already booked once for this same file.
findings.evidence: toml:55 `sparse_fire_reg1_cycles = 396 # measured — fixture F1` vs raster_dsl.emp:1124-1125, the live pin: `ensure(fire_cost_cycles(fire(3, [reg_set($8C81)])) == 412, ...)` with trailing comment "measured 2026-08-17 at RUNGS=5, 3 boots spread 0 (was 396 at RUNGS=4)"; raster.emp:185-186 records the same re-pin ("F1 396->412, F5 612->628"). toml:57 `sparse_fire_water_cycles = 660 # modelled — reg_sh_on + 3-word region` vs the current model's own arithmetic, stated at raster_dsl.emp:643-644: "the merged fire tops out at 302 + 110 + 264 = 676" (reg op = 8 fetch + 5x16 fall-through + 12 work + 10 tail = 110 under RUNGS=5; the 660 is the RUNGS=4 figure, 302+94+264). Neither row appears in the [symbols] gate table, so tools/effects_budget_check.py cannot catch this — the file's own header calls itself "the ONE machine-readable budget", and its history (EFX-5: raster_state_bytes drifted 288 vs 298 in exactly this ungated way) is the precedent.
findings.fix_sketch: Update the two rows to 412/676 with the RUNGS=5 provenance comment (keep the old values as _SUPERSEDED per the file's own convention), and consider adding gated rows for the F-series pins so a future rung change fails the checker instead of going stale silently again.

findings.title: Two stale wire-format comments describe the rejected trailer format the freeze will enshrine as docs
findings.claim: Raster_InstallPatched's header comment documents the trailer as "[n (word)][channel (word)][DMAEntry (14 bytes)]" — the built-entry format that was measured, rejected, and replaced by parameters — and raster_dsl.emp's ship_trailer comment says the trailer sits at "128 + 2 + 8*records" when table entries have been 5 words (10 bytes) since rec_off/rec_len landed.
findings.evidence: raster.emp:934-935: `// Trailer layout: [n (word)][channel (word)][DMAEntry (14 bytes)], sitting after the patch table at RASTER_BUF_SIZE + 2 + 10*records` — the DMAEntry half contradicts Raster_BuildShipEntry's own header 80 lines down (:1020-1024, "THE TRAILER CARRIES PARAMETERS RATHER THAN A BUILT ENTRY... Measured three ways... all three produced here.provisional errors") and the actual consumer layout buffers.emp:411-412 documents ("[stage off][colour count][CRAM addr][reg count][reg words...]"). raster_dsl.emp:1629-1631: "The trailer's own offset is 128 + 2 + 8*records" — with 5-word entries the offset is 128 + 2 + 10*records, which is exactly what the runtime computes (raster.emp:949-954, the 10n arithmetic whose comment even explains why 10 replaced the old lsl #3 stride); for OJZ_TwoChannel (2 records) the trailer is at +150, not +146. Both files are the runtime source-of-truth docs the migration gate freezes as trusted substrate, and this format has already drifted once per era (the arm_off deletion) — a hand-author or a later parcel reading either comment reconstructs the wrong wire format.
findings.fix_sketch: Fix both comments: raster.emp:934 to the parameter layout (name buffers.emp's spelling), raster_dsl.emp:1630 to 10*records. Comment-only, zero bytes, no repin.

findings.title: OP_SET_REG (opcode 0) pays the entire 5-rung compare chain — 80 of its 110 cycles — on both live band fires
findings.claim: The op dispatch chain is ordered by frequency of the OTHER opcodes, so OP_SET_REG, which is opcode 0 and appears in every shipped band fire, falls through five failed compare rungs (80 cycles by the project's own fitted model) before doing its 12 cycles of work; a leading `tst.w d1 / beq` would decide it in 14.
findings.evidence: raster.emp:714-725 — `cmpi.w #OP_CRAM, d1 / beq.s .op_cram / cmpi.w #OP_PAL_REGION, d1 / beq .op_region / cmpi.w #OP_RUN_GRADIENT, d1 / beq .op_run_gradient / cmpi.w #OP_RUN_RAMP, d1 / beq .op_run_ramp / cmpi.w #OP_PAL_RESTORE, d1 / beq .op_pal_restore / move.w (a1)+, (a2)`. The comment above it claims frequency ordering with "OP_SET_REG the fall-through", but SET_REG is present in BOTH live records: games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp:132 (OJZ_TestRaster, section 1 preset) and :655 (OJZ_TwoChannel channel 0, section 0 preset) each open with `0, $8C89`. Cycle walk with the project's own gate-pinned constants (raster_dsl.emp:995-997, 1030, fitted to 8 oracle fixtures with residual 0): RASTER_DISPATCH_RUNG_CYC=16 (`cmpi.w #imm,d1` 8 + `beq.s` not-taken 8), RASTER_DISPATCH_RUNGS=5, RASTER_WORK_REG_CYC=12, RASTER_OP_FETCH_CYC=8, RASTER_OP_TAIL_CYC=10. SetReg op = 8+80+12+10 = 110 cycles, of which 80 (73%) is proving the opcode is not one of five nonzero values. raster.emp:183-186 records the tax being paid and accepted: "The SetReg fall-through pays the +16 rung tax (F1 396->412, F5 612->628)" — i.e. measured fixture F1, a fire with ONE reg_set, costs 412 cycles of which 80 (19% of the whole fire) is failed dispatch. OP_PAL_RESTORE is no better: depth 4 = 16*4+18 = 82 cycles of dispatch. Consequence on live content: the OJZ water fire (reg_sh_on + 3-word pal_region) is 660-710 cycles against RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC=488, which is why check_density forces OJZ_TwoChannel's two bands 2 fire lines apart (ojz_effects.emp:618-620: "channel 0's fire is modelled at 526 cycles against a 489-cycle line, so it spills about one line past its own").
findings.fix_sketch: Insert `tst.w d1 / beq.s .op_set_reg` (4+10 = 14 on hit) ahead of the cmpi chain and move the single `move.w (a1)+,(a2)` body out of the fall-through: SetReg op 110 -> 44 (-66), the other four ops pay +12 (tst.w Dn 4 + Bcc.s not-taken 8, cheaper than a cmpi rung's 16). Net -54 on the live water fire. The bigger version is the pc-relative `jmp .tab(pc,d1.w)` -> `bra.w` table, flat ~24 cycles at every depth (-56 for SetReg, -58 for PalRestore, +6 for Cram) — rejected at raster.emp:707-713 for contract-closure dataflow reasons, i.e. a tooling constraint costing up to 82 cycles per op. Either change shifts pre-burst timing, so EFX_BLANK_DELAY (raster.emp:232) and EFX_RESTORE_DELAY (:238) must be re-run through their oracle ladders — which is precisely why this is cheap now and expensive after the P1 identity freeze. raster_dsl's RASTER_DISPATCH_* constants and the check_density ensures must be re-pinned in the same change.

findings.title: Streamed words cost 30 cycles each (abs-long store + dbf) where a comptime-known count and the live a2 make 16 achievable — this is the constant that sets RASTER_CRAM_MAX = 3
findings.claim: Every colour/scroll word in every streaming op is written with an absolute-long store inside a dbf loop (20+10 = 30 cycles/word) even though the count is a build-time constant and VDP_DATA is reachable as -4(a2) from the already-live control-port pointer (16 cycles), so the per-fire word ceiling that shapes the whole OP_PAL_REGION design is ~46% larger than the hardware requires.
findings.evidence: raster.emp:736-739 — `.cram_loop: move.w (a1)+, VDP_DATA / dbf d1, .cram_loop`; same shape at :757-759 (.region_loop), :816-818 (.restore_loop), :837-839 (.dense_body's three writes), :852 (.ramp_body). VDP_DATA = $C00000 and VDP_CTRL = $C00004 (engine/system/constants.emp:420-421), and a2 holds VDP_CTRL across .op_cram, .dense_body and .ramp_body, so -4(a2) IS the data port. 68000 counts: MOVE.W (An)+,(xxx).L = 20 vs MOVE.W (An)+,(d16,An) = 16; MOVE.W Dn,(xxx).L = 16 vs MOVE.W Dn,(d16,An) = 12. The project pins the current figure itself: raster_dsl.emp:998 `RASTER_STREAM_WORD_CYC = 30 // one streamed word: move.w to VDP_DATA + dbf`. A 3-word op therefore costs 3*20 + (10+10+14) = 94 cycles from the count load, where three straight-line displacement stores are 48 — a 46-cycle saving, against a documented usable window of 60 (tools/effects_budget_model.toml: usable_cycles_after_entry = 60). The count is never a runtime unknown: the DSL emits `count-1` as a literal, and RASTER_CRAM_MAX = 3 bounds it, so the dbf loop is runtime rediscovery of a comptime fact — the exact pattern CODING_CONVENTIONS.md forbids. This is load-bearing on the architecture, not just on cycles: raster.emp:103-108 justifies the scoped-region design ("a full-line region is authored as CONSECUTIVE OP_PAL_REGION fires ... takes ceil(N/3) lines") entirely from this budget, and effects_budget_model.toml:99-108 turns it into full_line_fire_lines = 6 plus "REFUSED — space them, or use the dense tier".
findings.fix_sketch: Two tiers. Cheap and local: in .op_cram/.dense_body/.ramp_body write through `-4(a2)` instead of absolute VDP_DATA (-4/word; -12 per 3-colour fire, -12 per dense line). Real fix: let the encoder emit per-count opcodes (OP_CRAM1/2/3, OP_PAL_REGION1/2/3) whose bodies are straight-line stores with no dbf — 3 words in 48 cycles instead of 102 including the count fetch, which is ~11% of a scanline reclaimed per streaming fire and would let RASTER_CRAM_MAX rise (shrinking full_line_fire_lines from 6). Per-count opcodes lengthen the compare chain, which argues for pairing this with finding 1's jump table. All three delay knobs are calibrated against current pre-burst counts and must be re-laddered; do it before the identity freeze, not after.

findings.title: Raster_HInt pays a redundant SR push/pop (~30 cycles) on every fire — rte already restores SR from the exception frame
findings.claim: The handler brackets its body in `with ints_off`, which pushes and pops SR around the body, but the handler ends in `rte`, which restores the pre-exception SR unconditionally — so the push/restore pair is pure overhead: ~30 cycles on every fire, including all ~101 fires per frame of the live OJZ section-2 dense run (~3,000 cycles/frame, 2.3% of an NTSC frame).
findings.evidence: raster.emp:656-657 `with ints_off { movem.l d0-d1/a1-a2, -(sp)` and :858-860 `movem.l (sp)+, d0-d1/a1-a2 / } / rte`. The bracket expands (engine/irq.emp) to acquire `move.w sr,-(sp)` + `move.w #$2700,sr`, release `move.w (sp)+,sr`. 68000: MOVE SR,-(SP) = 8+6 = 14, MOVE (An)+,SR = 12+4 = 16 — 30 cycles for the save/restore pair; the mask write itself (16) is the only part that does work. `rte` (20 cycles) pops SR+PC from the frame the CPU pushed at entry, so the restored value is discarded one instruction later. The code documents that the bracket was chosen over a bare `move.w #$2700,sr` for VERIFIER reasons, not hardware ones (raster.emp:645-649: "bare, the write needs `sr` in the contract, and adding it to preserves() defeats the movem round-trip proof (the checker cannot model `rte` restoring SR ...)") — so ~30 cycles/fire is being spent to keep a contract clause provable. Scale: 30 of the measured 412-cycle F1 reg fire (7%); 30 of ~433 cycles/dense line (dense_run_cycles_per_frame 41579 / 96 lines, effects_budget_model.toml:129) = 7% of the hottest per-line path in the engine; ~3,030 cycles/frame during the section-2 run. Secondary point, in the safety direction: with the restore present there is an instruction boundary between `move.w (sp)+,sr` (back to IPL 4) and `rte` where a pending IRQ6 can nest on top of the handler's own frame; letting rte do the restore removes that window as well as the cycles.
findings.fix_sketch: Add an interrupt-context flavour of the bracket whose release is EMPTY and whose SR claim is discharged by the terminating `rte` (e.g. `context ints_off_irq { acquire = move.w #$2700,sr; release = }` plus a sigil rule that an `rte`-terminated proc satisfies the SR balance), then use it in Raster_HInt. Zero behavioural change, -30 cycles on every fire, and it is a sigil-side change so it must be sequenced with the aeon/sigil pairing ritual.

findings.title: .dense_body re-tests the run-invariant Raster_Dense_Kind on every scanline: 24 cycles x 96 lines = ~2,300 cycles/frame for free
findings.claim: Which dense body to run is fixed for the whole run by the ENTER op, but the handler reloads and tests Raster_Dense_Kind from RAM on every single dense line, ~24 cycles of a ~433-cycle line, while the flags from the entry test of Raster_Dense_Lines could carry the same information at zero cost.
findings.evidence: raster.emp:834-835 — `tst.w Raster_Dense_Kind / bne.s .ramp_body`; the value is written once per run at :773 (`clr.w Raster_Dense_Kind`) and :786 (`move.w #1, Raster_Dense_Kind`). 68000: TST.W (xxx).L = 16, Bcc.s not-taken = 8 -> 24 cycles per line. The live OJZ section-2 gradient runs 96 dense lines (ojz_effects.emp:303-304 OJZ_GRAD_TOP 96 / OJZ_GRAD_LINES 96, bound in OJZ_Preset_Sec2 at :573), so 96*24 = 2,304 cycles/frame = 1.8% of an NTSC frame, spent re-deriving a constant. The information is already in hand: the handler enters via `tst.w Raster_Dense_Lines / bne .dense_body` (:695-696) and Bcc does not alter CCR, so the N flag from that tst is still live at .dense_body's first instruction. Full dense-line walk for context (44 exception + 12 slot jmp + 30 SR + 40 movem push + 12 lea + 16 tst + 10 bne + 12 arm + 24/28 cmd + 24 kind test + 20 cursor load + 60 three stores + 24 cursor store + ~20 subq + 10 bra + 44 movem pop + 16 SR pop + 20 rte) = ~440, which matches the model's own 41579/96 = 433 — so this is 5.5% of the line.
findings.fix_sketch: Encode the kind in the SIGN of Raster_Dense_Lines (ramp = negative count, counted with addq) and reorder to `tst.w Raster_Dense_Lines / beq .sparse_walk / bmi .ramp_body / <gradient body>`, duplicating the 2-instruction shared prologue (arm word + constant command) into each body. -24 cycles/line, +~10 bytes of ROM, and it retires the Raster_Dense_Kind RAM word (RASTER_STATE_SIZE and the ram.emp twin move, so it is a repin). Combined with findings 2 and 3 the dense line drops ~66 of ~440 cycles (15%), i.e. ~6,300 cycles/frame during the live run. Note the separate, already-FLAGGED per-line Dense_Cursor reload/store (raster.emp:689-693, ~44 cycles/line) is NOT re-reported here — it is booked as needing user sign-off on engine-wide register conventions.

findings.title: Palette_DeriveVariant re-reads six loop-invariant descriptor bytes per palette entry — 3,456 of ~19,300 cycles per derive
findings.claim: The inner entry loop reloads v_shift_r/v_bias_r/v_shift_g/v_bias_g/v_shift_b/v_bias_b from the descriptor for every one of the 48 entries it derives, 72 cycles/entry of pure re-fetch, and the whole shift/bias/clamp chain around them is re-executed per entry when only 8 distinct input values per channel exist.
findings.evidence: palette.emp:702-704, 714-716, 727-729 — e.g. `move.b pal_variant.v_shift_r(a0), d2 / lsr.w d2, d1 / move.b pal_variant.v_bias_r(a0), d2 / ext.w d2 / add.w d2, d1`. MOVE.B (d16,An),Dn = 12 cycles, six per entry = 72; 3 lines x 16 entries = 48 entries -> 3,456 cycles per derive. Hand walk of one channel block: move.w 4 + lsr.w #1 8 + andi.w 8 + move.b 12 + lsr.w d2 ~8 + move.b 12 + ext.w 4 + add.w 4 + clamp_d1_07 ~32 + lsl.w 8 + or.w 4 = ~104; x3 channels + 30 entry overhead = ~342/entry, x48 = ~16,400 plus per-line setup — which reproduces the measured 19,332 cyc/frame recorded at palette.emp:106-110, so the model is calibrated. A naive register hoist is NOT available (d0/d1/d2/d4/d5/d6/d7 all live; only d3 is free), so the fix is a table. Note also the B-channel extraction is the most expensive piece: `lsr.w #8,d1 / lsr.w #1,d1` = (6+16)+(6+2) = 30 cycles, where reading the colour's high byte directly (-2(a2), big-endian) is 12.
findings.fix_sketch: Build three 8-entry byte LUTs (24 bytes on the stack or in Palette_State scratch) once per derive — clamp((v>>shift)+bias) for v in 0..7 per channel, ~1,440 cycles — then point a0 at the table (the descriptor is no longer needed inside the loop) and make each channel `move.w d0,d1 / lsr.w #n,d1 / andi.w #7,d1 / move.b disp(a0,d1.w),d1 / lsl.w #n,d1 / or.w d1,d4` = ~46 cycles instead of ~104. Net ~-6,900 of ~19,300 (-36%) on every frame the derive actually runs (each cycling rotation, every stepped fade frame, every section crossing). The stale-bit gate at palette.emp:383-385 reduced the FREQUENCY of this cost, not its size.

findings.title: Raster_BuildSchedule reloads a loop-invariant template base from RAM per record and recomputes the buffer selection twice — ~96 of its measured 1,228 cycles, with d1 free
findings.claim: The per-record copy re-derives the template body base (`movea.l Raster_Patch_Tab,a2` + `suba.w #RASTER_BUF_SIZE,a2`) on every record even though it is computed once at :1114-1118, and the destination-buffer selection is computed a second time at the end; the proc declares d1 in clobbers and never uses it, so both are free to hoist.
findings.evidence: raster.emp:1153-1156 — `move.w (a0)+, d3 // rec_off / movea.l Raster_Patch_Tab, a2 / suba.w #RASTER_BUF_SIZE, a2 / adda.w d3, a2`, inside the `.entry` loop that `dbf d4, .entry` (:1164) drives. MOVE.L (xxx).L,An = 20 plus SUBA.W #imm,An = 8 = 28 cycles per record, replaceable by `movea.l d1,a2` (4) after one `move.l a2,d1` outside the loop. d1 never appears anywhere in the proc body (only d0, d2, d3, d4 are used) yet is licensed by `clobbers(d0-d4/a0-a2)` at :1101. Separately, :1175-1181 repeats the four-instruction selection (`move.l Raster_Active_Buf, d3 / lea Raster_Buf_A, a1 / cmpa.l d3, a1 / bne .swap / lea Raster_Buf_B, a1`) already done at :1107-1111, ~40 cycles that a second stack slot or d1 would carry. Measured baseline: effects_budget_model.toml build_schedule_cycles = 1228 for 2 records, and this proc runs on BOTH VInt_Level and VInt_Lag (raster.emp:588 via Raster_VBlank, called at vblank.emp:157 and :291), so on a lag frame it is paid twice. With 2 records the saving is 2*24 + 40 = ~88 cycles/frame (~7%); it grows linearly with record count as Aurora-authored scenes add channels.
findings.fix_sketch: Hoist the template base into d1 once after :1118 (`move.l a2, d1`) and use `movea.l d1, a2 / adda.w d3, a2` per record; stash the destination base in the existing 8-byte stack frame (widen to 12) or in d1's upper half and reuse it at the swap instead of re-testing Raster_Active_Buf.

findings.title: Raster_VBlank's static-program copy is a fixed 128-byte WORD loop: 1,408 cycles constant where the live programs are 28 bytes (~210) — new cost data for the booked EFX-4b
findings.claim: The install copy always moves RASTER_BUF_SIZE/2 = 64 words with move.w, so every static install costs ~1,408 VBlank cycles regardless of program size, and the shipped static programs are 14 words — the same fixed length that causes the booked over-read also makes the copy ~6.7x more expensive than the data warrants.
findings.evidence: raster.emp:575-578 — `move.w #(RASTER_BUF_SIZE / 2) - 1, d1 / .copy: move.w (a1)+, (a2)+ / dbf d1, .copy`. MOVE.W (An)+,(An)+ = 12 + DBF taken 10 = 22 cycles x 64 = ~1,408. The live static programs are 14 words each (ojz_effects.emp:137-142 OJZ_TestRaster via raster_words(OJZ_TEST_PROG), and OJZ_TestVsram at :420-441), i.e. 28 bytes; a length-driven copy would be 7 move.l = ~210 cycles. Even keeping the fixed size, move.l halves the loop: 32 iterations x (20+10) = 960 (-448), and halves the number of reads past the program end from 64 to 32. This is NOT a re-report of EFX-4b (docs/BUGS.md:253-267, which books the over-read and lists "a length word, or a bounded copy, or padding" as candidate fixes) — it is new information the booking does not carry: the length-word option is not merely the correctness fix, it also reclaims ~1,200 cycles of VBlank on every section crossing, and the DSL already knows the number (raster_words() is the comptime length used to size the emitted array). That turns EFX-4b from "harmless, deferred" into a change that pays for itself.
findings.fix_sketch: Have the DSL emit the program's word count as part of the program (or pad static programs to a longword multiple and copy with move.l bounded by that count), then drive the copy from it. Cheapest interim step with no format change: convert the loop to move.l with `#(RASTER_BUF_SIZE/4)-1` (RASTER_BUF_SIZE = 128 is a multiple of 4 and the 68000 needs only even alignment), -448 cycles and half the over-read.

findings.title: The dense tier's published per-line cost (342) contradicts the model's own numbers and its stated derivation is arithmetically wrong
findings.claim: per_line_body_cycles_upper = 342 is presented as an upper bound on the dense body, but the file's own dense_run_cycles_per_frame / line count gives 433, the neighbouring full_frame_fraction_ntsc = 0.76 can only be produced from 433 (224*342/128000 = 0.60, not 0.76), and a hand cycle walk of .dense_body lands at ~440 — so the published figure understates the real per-line cost by ~27%.
findings.evidence: tools/effects_budget_model.toml:128 `per_line_body_cycles_upper = 342`, :129 `dense_run_cycles_per_frame = 41579   # a 96-line run`, :140 `full_frame_fraction_ntsc = 0.76   # measured-derived: 224 lines * 342 cyc / 128000 (upper bound)`. Check the stated arithmetic: 224 * 342 = 76,608; 76,608 / 128,000 = 0.599. The published 0.76 requires 41,579 / 96 = 433.1 cyc/line: 224 * 433.1 = 97,014 / 128,000 = 0.758. Independent hand walk of raster.emp:822-842 (44 exception + 12 slot jmp + 14+16 SR + 40 movem push + 12 lea VDP_CTRL + 16 tst Dense_Lines + 10 bne + 12 arm word + 24-28 MOVE.L (xxx).L,(An) + 16 tst Dense_Kind + 8 bne + 20 movea cursor + 3x20 stores + 24 cursor store + ~20 subq to memory + 10 bra + 44 movem pop + 16 SR pop + 20 rte) = ~440, agreeing with 433 and not with 342. The 342 comes from a differential of two absolutes taken under the acknowledged interrupts.hint instrument bug (:118-127), whereas 41579 is a direct read; the differential is the weaker number yet it is the one labelled as the body cost. Impact: 342 is the figure a future dense-tier budget guard would divide by (no [symbols] row maps it today, so nothing catches the drift), and it is the basis of the neighbouring 'costs ZERO lag frames' ruling (:133-139) whose headroom conclusion is 27% optimistic.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace per_line_body_cycles_upper with 433 (= 41579/96, direct read) or publish both with explicit provenance, fix the 0.76 comment to name its real derivation, and add a [symbols]-style pin or an ensure so the dense per-line constant cannot drift silently the way EFX-5/EFX-9 documents the raster_state_bytes row doing.

findings.title: Palette_DoFade's snap loop pays a redundant addq.l #4,a0 that (a0)+ makes free
findings.claim: The final-frame snap reads the source with a non-incrementing move and then bumps the pointer by hand, 8 cycles per iteration that post-increment addressing gives away.
findings.evidence: palette.emp:493-498 — `.snap: move.l (a0), d1 / move.l d1, (a1)+ / move.l d1, (a2)+ / addq.l #4, a0 / dbf d0, .snap`, with `moveq #(96/4)-1, d0` = 24 iterations. MOVE.L (An),Dn and MOVE.L (An)+,Dn are both 12 cycles, so `move.l (a0)+, d1` makes the ADDQ.L #4,An (8 cycles) dead: 24*8 = 192 cycles off the fade's final frame, iteration cost 54 -> 46.
findings.fix_sketch: `move.l (a0)+, d1` and delete the addq.

coverage_notes: Walk order (forward, as chartered): (1) engine/effects/raster.emp end-to-end, all 1,315 lines — module header/timing model, opcode constants and the two delay knobs, the comptime dense-program constructors (raster_arm / raster_gradient_program / raster_ramp_program / fp16), Raster_Install, Raster_VBlank (install + copy + header + arm), Raster_HInt instruction by instruction (entry bracket, dense fast-path test, record walk, the 5-rung dispatch chain, .op_cram, .op_region, .op_run_gradient, .op_run_ramp, .op_pal_restore, .advance, .dense_body, .ramp_body, .park, .out), Raster_InstallPatched, Raster_BuildShipEntry, Raster_BuildSchedule, Raster_GetChannelBand, Effects_LatchWorldLines, Effects_SetWorldY. (6) Calibration cross-check: tools/effects_budget_model.toml and raster_dsl.emp's RASTER_*_CYC cost-model constants, used to validate my hand counts against the project's own fitted/measured numbers (my walks agree within ~10% on the sparse fire and to within 2% on the dense line). Deliberately NOT reached, and left for other seats/walks: raster_dsl.emp's encoder internals, guards and check_* validators beyond the cost-model constants (~1,900 lines of comptime — zero emitted bytes, so outside an instruction-level perf charter); palette_dsl.emp; the gate tools' own logic (effects_gates.py, raster_source_gate.py, raster_off_gate.py, raster_cost_probe.py, effects_budget_check.py, test_effects_budget_check.py, effects_scene_assert.py) except where the budget model's published numbers contradicted themselves; games/sonic4/test/poison/*.emp; engine/level/parallax.emp (out of scope by charter, and its Raster_GetChannelBand consumer was read only for the register contract, not for perf).
