findings.title: Effects runtime uses zero `assert.*` constructs; BuildSchedule's record-count walk is unbounded where bg_anim asserts the identical shape
findings.claim: The engine ships a zero-byte-in-release DEBUG bound-check construct (`assert.<w|b|l> dN, cc, #imm`) used at 47 sites, including a structurally identical table-count walk in bg_anim.emp — and engine/effects/*.emp uses it nowhere, leaving Raster_BuildSchedule's `dbf`-driven record walk with no bound on the count word it reads out of ROM.
findings.evidence:
raster.emp:1101-1126 reads the count and immediately drives a dbf with it, unchecked:
```
proc Raster_BuildSchedule () clobbers(d0-d4/a0-a2) {
        move.l  Raster_Patch_Tab, d0
        beq     .none                       // liveness: the TABLE, never Active_Buf
...
        move.w  (a0)+, d4                   // record count (a WORD)
        subq.w  #1, d4
    .entry:
```
The engine's own answer to exactly this shape is bg_anim.emp:117-121:
```
        move.w  (a3)+, d7                       // band count
        assert.w d7, ls, #BGANIM_MAX_BANDS      // table wider than BgAnim_LastStep = a4 walk
                                                // off the state array + garbage DMAs. DEBUG-ONLY
                                                // backstop (asserts are zero bytes in plain) — the
                                                // emitter's <= 4 assert is the release defense
```
`grep -rn '^\s*assert\.' engine/` returns 47 hits across core.emp, sprites.emp, section.emp, plane_buffer.emp, vdp_init.emp, sound_api.emp, bg_anim.emp — and zero in engine/effects/. raster.emp's sibling walk at :1237-1240 covers the same class with a hand RELEASE branch instead (`move.w (a0)+, d2 // record count` / `beq .none` commented "unreachable — but a 0 here would dbf 65536 times through ROM comparing garbage"), so the file is already inconsistent with itself about the hazard.

Concrete failure walk. `Raster_Patch_Tab` is set from `a0 + RASTER_BUF_SIZE` with no proof that a0 names a patched template (raster.emp:930-931), `EffectsPreset.ep_patched` is a bare `*u8`, and preset() cannot check it — preset.emp:103-108 records that comparing a Label to an integer is unevaluable and silently always-passes, so no comptime guard is even expressible. Author a preset with the keywords swapped — `preset(pal: OJZ_Palette, patched: OJZ_TestRaster, ...)` instead of `raster:` — which passes every existing ensure (exclusivity holds: `raster == 0`). Install: Patch_Tab = OJZ_TestRaster+128, i.e. 108 bytes past the end of a 20-word `data` object, so the count word is whatever ROM follows. If that word is 0, d4 = -1 and the loop runs 65536 times, copying rec_len bytes per iteration through `move.w (a2)+, (a1)+` into a 128-byte RAM buffer — unbounded RAM corruption inside VBlank, every frame, with no diagnostic. A `assert.w` costs zero release bytes and names it on the first frame of a debug build.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `assert.w d4, ls, #<record ceiling>` after the count read at raster.emp:1125 (and the same at :949, where Raster_InstallPatched multiplies the same unvalidated count into a trailer offset, and at :1237 where GetChannelBand pays a release branch for it). The ceiling is derivable: raster_program bounds the padded body to 64 words, so a genuine table cannot exceed ~15 records — spell it as a named const in raster_dsl (glob-injected, so nameable in raster.emp) and let the assert carry it, exactly as BGANIM_MAX_BANDS does.

findings.title: Raster_InstallPatched hand-decomposes a ×10 multiply that the tree's `mul_const.w` cost-model construct owns
findings.claim: The trailer-offset computation hand-writes a shift/add chain for ×10 and documents the decomposition as a design decision, while sigil provides `mul_const.w dst, #n, scratch` — a cost-model-driven multiply lowering used at 13 sites in this tree, including ones whose stride is derived from a struct so it cannot rot.
findings.evidence:
raster.emp:938-953:
```
        // TEN BYTES PER ENTRY, AND TEN IS NOT A SHIFT. The stride was a single `lsl.w #3`
        // while entries were four words; the fifth word (rec_off/rec_len replacing arm_off)
        // makes it 10n, and `mulu` is forbidden (CODING_CONVENTIONS.md). 8n + n + n is three
        // instructions and no multiplier.
        move.w  (a1), d0                        // record count
        move.w  d0, d1
        lsl.w   #3, d0                          // 8n
        add.w   d1, d0                          // 9n
        add.w   d1, d0                          // 10n — the table's byte length
```
The existing construct, same shape, in the immediately adjacent subsystem — parallax.emp:672:
```
        mul_const.w d3, #sizeof(band_entry), d5  // d3 = d2 × sizeof(band_entry); d5 trashed
```
and section.emp:151 (`mul_const.w d0, #66, d1`), tile_cache.emp:105-109 (wrapped in a named helper with a stride ensure), plane_buffer.emp:76/265, collision_lookup.emp:62, entity_window.emp:1624. It is a mnemonic-position language construct (sigil/crates/sigil-frontend-emp/src/mul_lower.rs: "Two 68k-only mnemonic-position constructs", candidates priced by the same M68000UM cycle table the budget walk uses, `mulu` included and rejected when a chain is cheaper), so no import or helper-glob concern applies. d1 is free here (proc declares clobbers(d0-d4/a0-a2)) and the `.w` contract's undefined upper word is unread — d0 is only consumed as `(a1, d0.w)`.

Why it is a defect and not a style note: the comment itself records that this chain was ALREADY hand-rewritten once when the entry grew from 4 words to 5, and the literal 10 is a magic number in the runtime while raster_dsl.emp:1588-1592 is the authority that emits 5 words per entry. The same stride appears twice more as bare literals (`addq.l #8, a0` at raster.emp:1185 and :1246 — 'skip the 4 words after line_src'). A sixth table word means three unrelated hand edits, with no build-time check on any of them; parallax's `#sizeof(band_entry)` spelling absorbs that edit automatically. The comment's optimality claim is also unverified — the construct's own enumeration would consider `move.w d0,d1; lsl.w #2,d0; add.w d1,d0; add.w d0,d0` (20 cyc) against this chain (22 cyc).
findings.fix_sketch: Replace lines 950-953 with `mul_const.w d0, #PATCH_ENTRY_BYTES, d1`, defining PATCH_ENTRY_BYTES = 2 * 5 in raster_dsl (where the 5-word entry is emitted) so the runtime and the encoder read one number; re-spell the two `addq.l #8` skips against the same const. NOTE this is byte-changing (the construct may pick a different, cheaper chain), so it belongs BEFORE the P1 identity freeze, not after — repin/refreeze after landing.

findings.title: Two effects gates each carry a private, weaker .emp constant reader while the same directory ships a tested resolver
findings.claim: `effects_gates.emp_int` and `raster_off_gate.emp_const` are two near-identical one-line-regex readers of `const NAME = <literal>`; tools/effects_budget_check.py already ships a comment-stripping, expression-evaluating, reference-following resolver for exactly this job with ten unit tests behind it, and the ad-hoc copies silently return a WRONG number on forms the tested one handles.
findings.evidence:
effects_gates.py:51-59:
```
def emp_int(rel: str, name: str) -> int:
    """A `const NAME = <int>` out of an .emp source, so no expectation here is hand-copied."""
    txt = (AEON / rel).read_text()
    m = re.search(rf"^\s*(?:pub\s+)?const\s+{re.escape(name)}\s*=\s*(\$[0-9A-Fa-f]+|-?\d+)", txt, re.M)
```
raster_off_gate.py:48-56 — the same function under another name, already diverged (no `-?`):
```
def emp_const(rel: str, name: str) -> int:
    m = re.search(rf"^\s*(?:pub\s+)?const\s+{re.escape(name)}\s*=\s*(\$[0-9A-Fa-f]+|\d+)", txt, re.M)
```
The existing construct, in the same directory and in the same subject set — effects_budget_check.py:51-53 + :71-135 + :138-166 (`CONST_RE` with the `(?::[^=]*)?` type-annotation arm, `emp_constants` via `strip_comments`, `eval_int_expr` with the whitelisted-AST evaluator and cycle detection, `make_resolver` with the sibling `*_dsl.emp` glob injection). Its test file enumerates precisely the forms the ad-hoc copies get wrong (test_effects_budget_check.py:26-45, 64-79): `pub const SUM = 4 + 4 + 2 + BUF + BUF`, `pub const NEWTYPED : VramTile = $03E0`, and a `/* ... */` block-commented declaration.

Concrete failure scenario. effects_gates.py:209 reads RASTER_WORK_RESTORE_CYC, today `const RASTER_WORK_RESTORE_CYC = 212`, whose own comment (raster_dsl.emp:1009-1016) derives it as `64 + (moveq 4 + 13*10 + 14 expired) = 64 + 148 = 212` and whose CLAIM D-D direction is explicitly to keep cost constants cost-keyed. Re-spell it as `= 64 + 148` — legal .emp, and the build's own F8 pin (raster_dsl.emp:1138) still passes — and `emp_int` matches the prefix `64` and returns 64 with no error. expect_f8 then comes out 888 cycles low and the gate prints `FAIL cost_model vs hardware`, blaming a correct ROM for a reader bug, while the build's own fixture pin says the model is right. The block-comment direction is worse: `   pub const ALSO_BLOCKED = 997 */` matches `^\s*pub\s+const\s+...`, so a commented-out constant becomes a live gate expectation.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete both private readers and import the tested path: `from effects_budget_check import make_resolver`, then `make_resolver(AEON)("engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp:RASTER_WORK_RESTORE_CYC")`. It already handles $/%/expressions/sibling-dsl names and raises loudly rather than truncating.

findings.title: parse_lst_locals is copy-pasted between two effects gates while its sibling parse_lst is properly shared
findings.claim: The mangled-local-label listing parser exists twice — once as a named function in raster_source_gate.py and once inlined verbatim into snapshot_poison_gate.py's main() — even though both files already import the sibling `parse_lst` from raster_cost_probe rather than duplicating it.
findings.fix_sketch: Move `parse_lst_locals` next to `parse_lst` in raster_cost_probe.py (or a small tools/lst.py) and import it in both gates; snapshot_poison_gate's inline loop becomes one call.

findings.title: The 3-channel unpack/repack idiom is hand-written nine times in palette.emp, which already ships the Code-splice construct for its neighbours
findings.claim: Palette_DoFade, Palette_DoOperator and Palette_DeriveVariant each hand-write the same extract-shift-mask / shift-back-or repack for R, G and B — nine copies of a ~7-instruction block — while the same file already factors the two SMALLER pieces of those bodies into parameterless `comptime fn -> Code` splices, and the engine's own splice idiom takes Reg parameters.
findings.evidence:
palette.emp:175-201 establishes the construct in-file:
```
comptime fn clamp_d1_07() -> Code { return asm { ... } }
comptime fn step_d3_toward_d4() -> Code { return asm { ... } }
```
with the rationale at :164-172 ("inlined rather than jbsr'd ... a Code splice sidesteps both"). The larger surrounding idiom is not factored. Palette_DoFade:513-545 —
```
        move.w  d0, d3
        lsr.w   #1, d3
        andi.w  #7, d3
        ...
        lsl.w   #1, d3
        or.w    d3, d2
```
x3 channels; Palette_DoOperator:596-621 the same x3 (d3/d2); Palette_DeriveVariant:698-735 the same x3 (d1/d4). The B channel is the trap the duplication carries: `lsl.w #9` is not encodable, so every one of the three B blocks must spell `lsr.w #8` + `lsr.w #1` and `lsl.w #8` + `lsl.w #1` by hand (palette.emp:532-545, 612-620, 727-734) — three chances to get a bit position wrong with nothing checking them against each other. The engine's parameterised-splice precedent is coords.emp:42 `pub comptime fn abs_w(v: Reg) -> Code` (and objects/aabb.emp:41, page_cache.emp:457), so a `chan_get(src: Reg, dst: Reg, shift: int)` / `chan_put(v: Reg, acc: Reg, shift: int)` pair is expressible. parallax.emp:95-98 records that this tree already tracks this exact class as a gap-ledger row ("SIBLING, still hand-written: engine.buffers' queue_static_dma spells the same shape ... One shared generator over both is its own byte-proving parcel").
findings.fix_sketch: Add `chan_get`/`chan_put` Code splices beside clamp_d1_07 in palette.emp, with the >8 shift emitted as the two-instruction form so the expansion is byte-identical, and replace the nine hand blocks. Land it before the P1 identity freeze and verify byte-identity with --freeze --ab; palette_dsl.emp:65-70's variant_word model plus its three ensures is the comptime twin that keeps the bit positions honest.

findings.title: Raster_BuildSchedule spells the inactive-buffer selection twice instead of splicing it
findings.claim: The 'which buffer is not live' four-instruction sequence is written out twice inside one proc — once to pick the destination, once to publish the swap — with no shared construct, in a proc whose neighbours in the same subsystem use the file-local Code-splice idiom for smaller repeats.
findings.evidence:
raster.emp:1106-1112:
```
        // --- destination = whichever buffer is NOT live ---
        move.l  Raster_Active_Buf, d3
        lea     Raster_Buf_A, a1
        cmpa.l  d3, a1
        bne     .dst_ready
        lea     Raster_Buf_B, a1
    .dst_ready:
```
and raster.emp:1174-1181, the same four instructions with a different label:
```
        // --- swap: the buffer just built becomes the one Raster_HInt walks ---
        move.l  Raster_Active_Buf, d3
        lea     Raster_Buf_A, a1
        cmpa.l  d3, a1
        bne     .swap
        lea     Raster_Buf_B, a1
    .swap:
        move.l  a1, Raster_Active_Buf
```
The existing construct: parallax.emp:99 `comptime fn copy_band_entry() -> Code` and palette.emp:175/190 show the in-subsystem pattern (sigil uniquifies the local labels per expansion, which is what makes a two-site splice with a `.dst_ready`-style label legal). Consequence if it drifts: the two copies must agree exactly or the proc builds into one buffer and publishes the other — the handler then walks the stale schedule with the arm words it did not build, and the arm words are RELATIVE gaps, so the whole tail of the chain desynchronises (the failure the proc's own header at :1082-1086 describes). Nothing checks the two blocks against each other today.
findings.fix_sketch: Factor a `select_inactive_buf()` Code splice emitting the identical four instructions and call it at both sites; byte-identical by construction, and the swap site keeps its own `move.l a1, Raster_Active_Buf` tail.

coverage_notes:
Walked, in this order: (1) engine/effects/raster.emp in full (both pages, 1315 ln) — comptime constructors, Install/VBlank/HInt, InstallPatched, BuildShipEntry, BuildSchedule, GetChannelBand, LatchWorldLines, SetWorldY; (2) engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp in full (1949 ln) — descriptors, op/fire constructors, compose, preset library, encoder, cost model + fixture pins, check_intervals/density/mixed_fire, raster_program, patch_table, ship_trailer, layout guards, both band twins; (3) engine/effects/palette.emp (768 ln) and palette_dsl.emp (126 ln); (4) engine/effects/preset.emp; (5) engine/level/bg_anim.emp; (6) engine/system/hblank.emp and vblank.emp; (7) games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp in full; (8) tools/effects_gates.py, raster_source_gate.py, raster_off_gate.py, raster_cost_probe.py, effects_budget_check.py, test_effects_budget_check.py, effects_scene_assert.py, plus snapshot_poison_gate.py (not in the subject list but invoked by effects_gates as an effects gate — it is the third copy in finding 4); (9) games/sonic4/test/poison/README.md and 4 of the 12 poison modules.

Reuse targets searched before claiming reinvention: every `comptime fn` in engine/ outside effects/ (75 hits enumerated); `mul_const`/`mul_bounded` call sites tree-wide plus sigil's mul_lower.rs contract; `^\s*assert\.` tree-wide (47 hits, 0 in effects/); oracle/linux-port/harness/ab_runner.py (correctly used by effects_gates --selfcheck and by effects_scene_assert's sidecar contract — no reinvention there); `def parse_lst`-class listing parsers across tools/ and the harness; every `const`-scraping regex in tools/*.py; block-copy / memcpy helpers in engine/ (none exist, so the Raster_VBlank and Palette_LoadPal copy loops are NOT reinventions and are not reported); comptime fixed-point helpers (none exist, so raster.emp's fp16 is new); TILE_SIZE-family constants (bg_anim's local TILE_BYTES_SHIFT is justified by its documented standalone-port constraint at bg_anim.emp:40-47, so not reported); double-buffer selection helpers (none exist engine-wide).

Deliberately NOT reported. (a) engine/system/buffers.emp:320-378 — the R1 palette snapshot splice is four hand-written 8x`move.l (a1)+,(a2)+` runs where core.emp:45's `clear_longs(n)` fold precedent applies directly; buffers.emp is outside the subject file list, and parallax.emp:95-98 already books this class as a gap-ledger row. (b) The arm-word formula now has four implementations — raster_dsl.arm_at:1276, raster.emp's raster_arm:272 (dense tier, pinned), raster_cost_probe.program_words' inner `arm()`:131, effects_gates.derive_arms' inner `arm()`:94 — plus the runtime twin in BuildSchedule:1143-1147. The two .emp copies are pinned to each other by comment and by the hand twins; the two Python copies model different things (static encode vs runtime clamp/suppress), so I judged a merge unsound rather than merely unshared. Flagging it here because the P1 freeze makes all five load-bearing. (c) raster.emp's pal_stage_off literals (128/32/2) and raster_dsl's inlined opcode literals are duplications with documented ensure-pins and a language reason (call-site name resolution) — working as intended. (d) The doubled `ensure(PAL_MAX_VARIANTS == 2, ...)` in preset.emp:114 and palette_dsl.emp:125 is redundant-by-design across reachability domains.

Not reached: the remaining 8 poison modules (read 4 of 12 — the 4 I read were uniform in idiom, so I sampled rather than exhausted); tools/emp_expect_fail.py and tools/emp_helper_closure.py bodies (only their imported `strip_comments` surface); the harness launcher.py / aether client; tools/scenes/*.json contents; effects_budget_model.toml row values (I checked only that effects_budget_check is the resolver its tests exercise). Per charter I reviewed parallax.emp only at its effects touchpoints (Effects_InstallPreset seam, Raster_GetChannelBand consumer, copy_band_entry as a splice precedent) and reported nothing inside its walker/fill loops. On the two KNOWN-OPEN BUGS.md items: I found nothing new about the Raster_Buf_B observability gap; on EFX-4b I note only that raster_dsl.emp:1520-1527 already scopes it correctly in comment, and neither is re-reported.

findings.title: OP_PAL_REGION's cost is measured by nothing — F4 is excluded from the only wired cost gate
findings.claim: The cost-model-vs-hardware gate runs `--only F0,F1,F3,F5,F8`, omitting F4 (the sole `stream_pal_region` fixture), so RASTER_WORK_REGION_CYC — the constant that gates the shipped OJZ water band — has no path back to hardware in any runnable gate.
findings.evidence: tools/effects_gates.py:214 `"--rom", rom, "--lst", lst, "--only", "F0,F1,F3,F5,F8",` while the fixture exists at tools/raster_cost_probe.py:192 `"F4": { "what": "stream_pal_region, 3 words — the region premium against F3"`. The three other candidate authorities are all model-internal: (1) engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp:1130 `ensure(fire_cost_cycles(fire(3, [stream_pal_region($22, 0, 1, 1, 3)])) == 566, ...)` re-derives 566 from the same constants it is pinning (302+8+(16+18)+122+3*30+10 = 566), so it cannot see the handler; (2) tools/effects_budget_check.py compares `raster.cost_model.work_region_cycles` to `engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp:RASTER_WORK_REGION_CYC` — toml vs const, both sides move together; (3) tools/effects_budget_model.toml:100 `handler_extra_cycles = "NEEDS-MEASUREMENT"  # oracle: lea+adda.w+stream vs a plain OP_CRAM` states outright that the region premium was never measured, and :88 derives 122 by hand (`the above + lea 8 + adda.w 12 + lea restore 12`). CONCRETE FAILURE: add one instruction (or lengthen the blank spin) inside `Raster_HInt`'s `.op_region` body only. Real per-fire cost rises above 566; the :1130 ensure still passes (its arithmetic is unchanged), effects_budget_check still passes (toml == const), F3/F5/F8 are unaffected because they exercise `.op_cram`, `.op_reg` and `.op_restore` bodies. The shipped consumer then silently mis-budgets: games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp:639 authors channel 0 as `fx_tint_band(...)` = an OP_PAL_REGION, and its own note (:617-620) records "channel 0's fire is modelled at 526 cycles against a 489-cycle line, so it spills about one line past its own. Two lines of separation is the margin" — a margin computed from the unverified 122. The band pair (lo 3/hi 220 and lo 222/hi 223) is 2 lines apart, so an under-charge of >=1 line of work puts the water fire's writes into channel 1's line with every gate green.
findings.fix_sketch: Add F4 to the `--only` list and compute its expectation the same way F3 is computed, with the region work constant and the region op's dispatch depth (1 failed rung + hit): `fire_region = base + fetch + (rung*1 + hit) + wregion + 3*word + tail`. F2/F6/F7 are equally cheap to fold in and would additionally pin the per-op vs per-fire split the model rests on.

findings.title: UNWIRED: nothing invokes effects_gates, and it is the only invoker of five gates
findings.claim: effects_gates.py is invoked by no build, no test runner, no hook and no CI, so raster_off_gate, raster_source_gate, snapshot_poison_gate, effects_scene_assert (with its three scenes) and every cost fixture are reachable only when a human types one command — and the P1 migration plan that will freeze these bytes does not name it.
findings.evidence: tools/effects_gates.py:11 asserts the constraint but names no home: "These CANNOT go in `build.sh`: every one boots a headless emulator and takes tens of seconds. This is the pre-merge / post-effects-change command instead". Measured invokers: `grep -rn effects_gates` over the tree outside docs/ returns ONLY its own file; build.sh's gate block (build.sh:171-234) runs exactly three things — s4lint, effects_budget_check.py:191, and emp_expect_fail.py:232 (plus the pytest step); `.github/` does not exist; `.git/hooks/` contains no non-sample hook; `grep -n "effects\|raster\|palette" test.sh` returns nothing. That last one is the sharp part: test.sh IS the tree's aggregate runner and it already has `section "8. Replay Net (headless oracle)"` (test.sh:244), i.e. the harness slot for an emulator-backed gate exists and the effects suite is absent from it. And `grep -n "effects_gates" docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-17-scanline-p1-scene-model.md` returns nothing, while that plan's verification steps name only `emp_expect_fail.py` CASES (:394,:405) and `refreeze --freeze <table> --ab` (:446). So the P1 byte-identity freeze can be declared green with zero of the five handler-observing gates ever having run against the frozen ROM. This is the tree's documented recurring failure mode restated by this very file's own docstring (:4-9).
findings.fix_sketch: Add an `effects_gates.py` section to test.sh beside section 8 (both boot headless oracle, so the dependency is already accepted there), and name it in the P1 plan's verification ritual alongside refreeze --ab.

findings.title: Scenes hardcode an absolute s4.debug.lst, so --rom/--lst cannot re-point them
findings.claim: All three committed scenes pin `"symbols": "/home/volence/sonic_hacks/aeon/s4.debug.lst"`, and effects_gates passes only `--old/--new` ROM to ab_runner, so gating any other shape or checkout resolves every poke and capture through the wrong symbol table.
findings.evidence: tools/scenes/effects_raster_mid_band.json:3 `"symbols": "/home/volence/sonic_hacks/aeon/s4.debug.lst",` (identical in effects_raster_suppressed.json:3 and effects_raster_above_screen.json:3). tools/effects_gates.py:147-149 builds `["python3", str(HARNESS / "ab_runner.py"), "--old", rom, "--new", rom, "--scene", ..., "--out", str(out), "--selfcheck"]` — the `--lst` the tool accepted at :111 is threaded to raster_off_gate (:163) and raster_source_gate (:168) but never to the scene lane. FAILURE SCENARIO: `python3 tools/effects_gates.py --rom s4.bin --lst s4.lst` (the release shape, which build.sh also ships). ab_runner boots s4.bin but resolves `Debug_Scene_Freeze`, `Camera_Y`, `Effects_World_Y`, `Raster_Buf_A/B` and `Raster_Active_Buf` from the DEBUG listing; the pokes land at debug addresses in a release ROM whose RAM layout differs, and the shape assertions are then computed over whatever bytes those addresses hold. findings.title: The probe's own integrity signals never reach the exit code or the JSON the gate reads
findings.claim: raster_cost_probe.main() returns 0 unconditionally, and its three integrity signals (no HInt routine row, buffer rewritten mid-sample, call-count variance) are printed only — the --out JSON carries none of them and effects_gates ignores `calls`, so the docstring's claim that a failed install "cannot be silently measured" does not hold on the aggregated path.
findings.evidence: tools/raster_cost_probe.py:410 `    return 0` is the only non-error return from main. :382 `flag = "  !! buffer was rewritten during the sample" if bad else ""` — the flag is a print-only string while :389 `table[name] = {"cycles": cyc, "calls": cal, "n": n}` still records the (now meaningless) cycles, and :406-408 writes exactly those three fields to the JSON. :392-393 prints "call count VARIED across repeats" and likewise changes nothing. The docstring's promise at :21-22 ("`calls` is a free correctness check ... so a fixture that failed to install cannot be silently measured") is unenforced downstream: tools/effects_gates.py:221-228 reads `d["Fn"]["cycles"][0]` for five fixtures and never reads `calls`. SECOND, SHARPER FAILURE: :379-381 `if any(x is None for x in rows): print(... NO HInt ROUTINE ROW ...); continue` drops the fixture from `table` entirely, so the JSON lacks that key — and effects_gates.py:222 `got_f0 = d["F0"]["cycles"][0]` raises an uncaught KeyError inside main(), aborting before the results loop at :237 prints anything. One missing fixture therefore discards the PASS/FAIL verdicts of every scene, teardown and source gate that already ran in the same invocation.
findings.fix_sketch: Make main() return nonzero when any selected fixture is missing a row, has a readback mismatch, or varies in `calls`; put those flags in the --out JSON; and have effects_gates read them (plus `.get()` the fixture keys so a missing one is a FAIL row, not a traceback).

findings.title: expect-absent/expect-present scan stale words past RASTER_OPS_END that the builder never clears
findings.claim: The presence/absence scan runs over the whole captured region rather than the live program, and Raster_BuildSchedule does not clear the buffer tail behind a shortened program — so the assertion is neither sound (a value past the terminator counts as PRESENT) nor complete (a value past word 23 of a 64-word buffer is unseen).
findings.evidence: tools/effects_scene_assert.py:87 `w = words(reads[live]["bytes"])` then :102-105 `for spec in a.expect_absent: ... if val in w: failures.append(...)` and :106-108 the mirror for expect_present — both over the full `w`, with no truncation at RASTER_OPS_END ($FFFF). engine/effects/raster.emp:1166-1167 writes only the terminator and stops: `move.w #RASTER_ARM_PARK, (a1)+` / `move.w #RASTER_OPS_END, (a1)+` — nothing zeroes the remainder of the 128-byte buffer, so words after the terminator are whatever the previous build of THAT buffer left (the buffers alternate, raster.emp:1107-1111/1175-1181). FAILURE SCENARIO, both directions: the suppressed scene shrinks the program from 23 words (games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp:646-663, `$8C89` at word 8) to 14, so words 14..23 of the live buffer are a stale earlier program; if a future channel-0 record places its `$8C89` op word anywhere in 14..23, `--expect-absent 0x8C89` (effects_gates.py:156) fails on correct code. Conversely the scenes capture `"len": 48` (24 of 64 words, tools/scenes/effects_raster_mid_band.json), so a `$8C89` that survives at word 24+ is reported ABSENT when it is present in the buffer. Neither direction is a verdict about the live program.
findings.fix_sketch: Truncate `w` at the first RASTER_OPS_END word before the absent/present scan (and refuse if no terminator appears inside the captured span — a program that overruns the capture is a scene bug, exit 2).

findings.title: No directory scan: a poison module with no CASES row is silently never run
findings.claim: The lane runs exactly the rows hand-listed in CASES and never compares that list against the poison directory, so a poison added without a row is parsed on every build (satisfying README property 1) and evaluated by nothing.
findings.evidence: tools/emp_expect_fail.py:63 `CASES: list[tuple[str, str, str, int]] = [` ... 11 rows; main() at :129-135 checks only the reverse direction — `missing = [(path, entry) for path, entry in named if not (AEON / path).is_file()]` — i.e. a named module that does not exist. Nothing enumerates `games/sonic4/test/poison/*.emp`. Today the set happens to be complete (12 .emp files = 11 CASES + the SENTINEL at :57), so this is latent, not live — but games/sonic4/test/poison/README.md's own author checklist ends with "Register the row in `CASES`", i.e. the wiring is a manual step with no gate, and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-17-scanline-p1-scene-model.md:63 queues four more (`poison_scene_*.emp` + "Register 4 CASES rows", :405). FAILURE SCENARIO: P1 Task 8 lands `poison_scene_boundary.emp` and one of the four CASES rows is dropped in review. The module is syntactically valid and imported by nothing, so every build stays green, `module.unreachable` ticks up by one (the same signature docs/BUGS.md:89-90 records for the sentinel), and the guard it was written to prove is never exercised. Cost of the omission is exactly the guard's coverage.
findings.fix_sketch: In main(), glob the poison dir and fail if `set(globbed) != set(named)` — one assertion, and it also catches a poison deleted while its CASES row survives (currently a file-missing error, which is already handled, so only the orphan direction is open).

findings.title: Derived bands are last-wins over the whole file, not "the first two calls" as the comment claims
findings.claim: The band table is built by a whole-file findall into a dict keyed by channel, so a second preset in ojz_effects.emp declaring ch:0/ch:1 silently re-points every derived expectation at the LAST matching pair while the comment asserts the first.
findings.evidence: tools/effects_gates.py:129-130 `pat = re.findall(r"\bch:\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*lo:\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*hi:\s*(\d+)", src, re.S)` / `bands = {f"ch{c}": (int(lo), int(hi)) for c, lo, hi in pat}` — dict comprehension, later keys overwrite. The comment three lines above (:123-124) says "the first two calls in ojz_effects.emp are channels 0 and 1 of OJZ_TwoChannel". Currently benign: `grep -n "ch:\s*[0-9]" games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp` returns exactly two hits (:639 ch:0 lo:3 hi:220, :641 ch:1 lo:222 hi:223). FAILURE SCENARIO: a second two-channel preset is authored below OJZ_TC_PROG (which the OJZ showcase work is heading toward). `derive_arms` (:87-91) then clamps channel 1 to the new preset's floor and tests channel 0's suppression against the new ceiling, so word1/word3 are computed for a program the scenes never install — the gate goes RED on correct code, with a message that reads as an engine defect. Not a false green, but a false red in the gate the P1 migration will lean on.
findings.fix_sketch: Take the first occurrence per channel (`bands.setdefault`), or better, anchor the search to the `OJZ_TC_PROG` definition so the gate names the preset it is actually modelling.

findings.title: reg $00's shadow offset is hardcoded to 0 in the gate that claims nothing is copied
findings.claim: The gate reads Mode-Set-1 as byte 0 of VDP_Shadow_Table with the register's offset implicit, while its own docstring asserts every expectation is derived — VDP_MODE1_OFF exists as a named constant and is not read.
findings.evidence: tools/raster_off_gate.py:64-65 `mode1 = int((await b.call("emulator/read_memory", {"addr": hex(sym["VDP_Shadow_Table"]), "len": 1}))["bytes"], 16)` — no offset term. The engine spells it: engine/vdp.emp:31 `pub const VDP_MODE1_OFF = $00                // reg $00 (Mode Set 1) — carries IE1`, and engine/system/hblank.emp:63/78 both write through `VDP_Shadow_Table + VDP_MODE1_OFF`. The docstring at :20-23 claims the opposite discipline: "EXPECTATIONS ARE DERIVED, NEVER COPIED ... A gate that hard-coded $4E73 and $10 would keep passing after someone changed the constant". FAILURE SCENARIO (low likelihood, high blast radius): if the shadow table were ever re-based or MODE1 moved off offset 0, this reads an unrelated register byte. `armed/ie1-set` and `off{1,2}/ie1-cleared` would then both be testing bit $10 of some other register — and since two of the three facts (Raster_Program == 0, slot == rte) would still hold, the gate can report OK for the exact regression the docstring calls "the one that buys the cycles". Note the gate DOES derive HBLANK_SLOT_RTE and HBLANK_IE1_BIT (:141-142), so this is the one un-derived address in it.
findings.fix_sketch: Read VDP_MODE1_OFF through the same `emp_const` helper (engine/vdp.emp) and add it to the address.

findings.title: The source gate is self-consistent with the probe's Python encoder, so an encoder-side stride change passes
findings.claim: Both the fixture and its prediction come from the same Python transcription of the wire format, so the gate proves the handler agrees with tools/, not with the raster_dsl encoder that authored programs actually use — and the offset arithmetic is duplicated on both sides of the comparison.
findings.evidence: tools/raster_source_gate.py:92-94 `def offset_of(f: dict) -> int: ... return f["slot"] * 128 + f["pal_line"] * 32 + f["entry"] * 2`, and the program it measures is built by the identical expression at tools/raster_cost_probe.py:112 `return [4, (c >> 16) & 0xFFFF, c & 0xFFFF, o["n"] - 1, o["slot"] * 128 + o["pl"] * 32 + o["e"] * 2]` — the encoder file itself flags the duplication at :62-69 ("It is a SECOND implementation of that format on purpose"). FAILURE SCENARIO: the per-slot stride changes in engine/effects/raster.emp's `pal_stage_off` (:130-134 only bounds slot/line/entry, it does not pin the strides). Authored .emp programs then encode the new stride and the handler streams from the address they encode — correctly — while this gate builds a 128-stride fixture, predicts a 128-stride address, and passes. The nearest other authority cannot cover it either: the hand pin at games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp:648-663 uses slot 0 ("72 is pal_stage_off(0, 2, 4) = 0*128 + 2*32 + 4*2"), so the slot term is multiplied by zero, and the budget row `"ram.variant_stage_bytes" = "engine/effects/palette.emp:PAL_MAX_VARIANTS * 128"` (tools/effects_budget_model.toml:228) supplies the 128 from the checker's own literal on both sides. The gate's stated anti-vacuity proof (the A/B differential, :204-211) does not close this: both fixtures share the same wrong stride, so the delta matches too.
findings.fix_sketch: Pin the encoder side once — a comptime `ensure` in raster_dsl that `pal_stage_off(1,0,0) == 128` (and the line/entry strides), or have the gate read a slot-1 offset out of a real .emp-authored program — so the Python transcription has an authority other than itself.

findings.title: The dense tier has no fixture and no gated row — its per-line cost is a once-measured number with a known-contaminated instrument
findings.claim: Every cost fixture (F0-F8) is sparse-tier; the dense tier's per-line body cost is neither in [symbols] nor re-measured by any gate, so a dense-body regression is invisible to the whole tool layer.
findings.evidence: tools/effects_budget_model.toml:128 `per_line_body_cycles_upper = 342` and :129 `dense_run_cycles_per_frame = 41579`, with the section's own caveat at :113-116 that the figure "INCLUDES profiler instrumentation, autovector entry and rte" from the contaminated `interrupts.hint` bucket. Neither row appears in the [symbols] table (tools/effects_budget_model.toml:220-245), so effects_budget_check cannot see them. tools/raster_cost_probe.py:171-221 defines F0-F8 and none installs OP_RUN_GRADIENT or OP_RUN_RAMP. On the .emp side the dense constructors carry structural guards only — engine/effects/raster.emp:346-360 (`top >= 3`, `lines >= 1`, `top + lines <= 224`, `stream_words == lines * RASTER_CRAM_MAX`) — with no cycle guard analogous to check_density's `cost <= gap * RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC` (:1240). The indirect bound is RASTER_CRAM_MAX = 3 words/line; nothing ties the dense body to RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC. Consequence given the runtime note at raster.emp:598-608, a dense run that fails to finish in its frame takes the next frame's priming fire down `.dense_body` and "the whole sparse schedule is dead too" — a failure with no build-time refusal and no gate.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a dense fixture to raster_cost_probe (an OP_RUN_GRADIENT program is installable by the same buffer poke) and gate its per-line marginal cost against a named constant, so the 342 becomes code-derived rather than a dated prose row.

findings.title: BGANIM_MAX_BANDS is defined TWICE with different consumers; the release-shape defense is a Python literal
findings.claim: The band-count ceiling exists as two independent `= 4` definitions — engine/system/constants.emp:205 (which is what actually sizes the RAM array) and engine/level/bg_anim.emp:48 (which is what actually bounds the runtime walk) — with nothing tying them, so raising one alone lets BgAnim_Update walk off BgAnim_LastStep in the release shape.
findings.evidence:
Two definitions of one name:
  engine/system/constants.emp:205  `pub const BGANIM_MAX_BANDS = 4              // animated BG strips per act`
  engine/level/bg_anim.emp:48      `const BGANIM_MAX_BANDS = 4`  (module-local "ON PURPOSE — do not re-home this to engine.constants (tried, item 30/F, reverted)", :40-47)
The two are consumed by DIFFERENT things:
  engine/ram.emp:413 `BgAnim_LastStep: [u16; BGANIM_MAX_BANDS],` — a region array length, so it must resolve to the engine.constants one (ram.emp names MAX_PARALLAX_BANDS from constants.emp:578 at ram.emp:266 the same way); bg_anim.emp's const is module-local and cannot reach here.
  engine/level/bg_anim.emp:118 `assert.w d7, ls, #BGANIM_MAX_BANDS      // table wider than BgAnim_LastStep = a4 walk off the state array + garbage DMAs. DEBUG-ONLY backstop (asserts are zero bytes in plain) — the emitter's <= 4 assert is the release defense` — the runtime bound, resolving to bg_anim.emp:48.
The named "release defense" is a third, hand-typed copy:
  tools/inject_editor_bg.py:48 `assert len(anims) <= 4, 'engine supports at most BGANIM_MAX_BANDS=4 bands'` — the literal 4 is not read from either .emp.
FAILURE WALK. An author adding a 5th/6th animated band reads bg_anim.emp:40-48 ("MODULE-LOCAL ON PURPOSE", i.e. presented as this file's authority), sets bg_anim.emp:48 = 6, and raises inject_editor_bg.py:48 to 6. constants.emp:205 is untouched, so BgAnim_LastStep stays [u16; 4] = 8 bytes. BgAnim_Update walks `lea BgAnim_LastStep, a4` (:116) with d7 = count-1 = 5 and `addq.w #2, a4` per band (:202), so bands 4 and 5 read `cmp.w (a4), d0` (:142) and write `move.w d5, (a4)` (:192) at offsets +8 and +10 — past the array. engine/ram.emp:413-416 puts `Static_Pal_Line0: [u8; sizeof(DMAEntry)]` immediately after it, so the overrun rewrites the first four bytes of the frame-top palette DMA entry that Enqueue_Dirty_Buffers queues every frame (engine/system/buffers.emp:304). The DEBUG assert at :118 catches it; asserts are zero bytes in the plain shape, and the documented release defense is the Python literal the same author just raised.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete one definition. If bg_anim.emp must stay standalone-linkable, keep bg_anim.emp:48 as the sole authority and give ram.emp its own literal 4 with the drift comment the raster/palette blocks already use (ram.emp:274-276, :327-332) — plus an `ensure(BGANIM_MAX_BANDS == 4)` beside it in bg_anim.emp so the two cannot part. Either way, make inject_editor_bg.py read the constant with the `emp_int()` helper effects_gates.py:51 already has rather than spelling 4.

findings.title: Claim D-F (snapshot offset == CRAM byte address) is prose in five files and enforced nowhere; the gate that observes it duplicates the assumption
findings.claim: pal_restore reuses one field as both a CRAM address and a Palette_Ship_Snap offset on the strength of a Palette_Buffer->CRAM->snapshot 1:1 mapping that is hand-authored as literals in buffers.emp and asserted by no `ensure`, so a change to the palette-line offsets silently makes every band OFF edge restore the wrong line's colours.
findings.evidence:
The claim, stated as fact and never checked:
  engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp:272-273 `// pal_restore — ... The snapshot offset IS the CRAM\n// address (BuildStaticDMA's 1:1 mapping — claim D-F), so one field carries both.`
  engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp:736-739 `PalRestore(a, cnt) => [10, vdp_comm(a, ...Cram, Write) >> 16, ... , cnt - 1, a],` — the same `a` is emitted as the command address AND as the tail offset word.
  engine/effects/raster.emp:811-815 `move.w (a1)+, d1 ... lea Palette_Ship_Snap, a2 / adda.w (a1)+, a2` with `// + offset == CRAM byte address (payload D-F ...)`.
The two halves the identity actually rests on, both literal-authored in one file, neither pinned:
  engine/system/buffers.emp:13-16 `equ SRC_PAL_LINE1 = ((extern("Palette_Buffer") + $20) >> 1) & $7FFFFF` (etc. for $00/$40/$60)
  engine/system/buffers.emp:110/117/124/131 `move.l #vdp_comm($20, VdpTarget.Cram, VdpOp.Dma), d2` (etc.) — i.e. buffer offset X -> CRAM address X
  engine/system/buffers.emp:319-320, 336-337, 353-354, 370-371 `lea Palette_Buffer+$40, a1 / lea Palette_Ship_Snap+$40, a2` — i.e. buffer offset X -> snapshot offset X
Grep for the claim id returns only comments (engine/effects/raster.emp:813, raster_dsl.emp:90/273/1845, tools/raster_cost_probe.py:114, tools/raster_source_gate.py:83/229); there is no `ensure` anywhere relating a snapshot offset to a CRAM address.
FAILURE WALK. Palette_Buffer currently holds all four CRAM lines even though "The engine writes CRAM lines 1-3 ONLY" (engine/effects/palette.emp:48) and every engine-side field is 96 bytes (Pal_Base/Pal_Target, ram.emp:391-392, copied to `Palette_Buffer + $20`). A future tidy that drops the unused line-0 slot from Palette_Buffer makes SRC_PAL_LINE1 = Palette_Buffer+$00 -> CRAM $20 and moves the splices to match; both halves stay internally consistent. pal_restore($48, 3) then still emits $48 as the snapshot offset while line 2's base bytes now live at snapshot offset $28, so the band's OFF edge streams line-3 colours over line 2 for every frame the band is on screen. Every build-time band guard (raster_dsl.emp:1406-1499) is green — none of them models the snapshot layout — and tools/raster_source_gate.py:217-229 cannot see it either, because its prediction is `want = snap_base + off` with `off = f["addr"]` (:97-99), i.e. it asserts the handler performs the addition, not that the sum names line 2's base.
findings.fix_sketch: Put the four line offsets in one comptime table (e.g. `PAL_LINE_OFF = [$00,$20,$40,$60]`) used by BuildStaticDMA's destination, SRC_PAL_LINE_n and the splice displacements, and add an `ensure` in buffers.emp that for each n the Static_Pal_LineN command's `vdp_comm_addr` equals the snapshot displacement the splice uses. Then pal_restore's one-field claim has a machine-checked authority instead of five prose copies.

findings.title: The probe carries a second, unpinned implementation of the raster wire format — and it is the instrument that calibrates the cost constants band() enforces
findings.claim: tools/raster_cost_probe.py re-implements op_words/arm_at/raster_program in Python (opcode numbers, VDP command longwords, the staging-offset formula, park/terminator words, the 128-byte cap) with no cross-check against engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp, and the encoder's only claimed check (`calls`) is insensitive to op-body drift — so a transcription slip mis-measures the very fixtures RASTER_WORK_* and band()'s minima are derived from.
findings.evidence:
The duplicate encoder and its own defence:
  tools/raster_cost_probe.py:62-69 `# A transcription of engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp's op_words / raster_program. It is a\n# SECOND implementation of that format on purpose ... The cross-check that it is transcribed\n# correctly is empirical and strong — `calls` reports the fires the hardware actually took, so\n# a mis-encoded program shows up as the wrong fire count before any cycle figure is read.`
What is duplicated, site for site:
  opcodes — raster_cost_probe.py:100-117 literals `0 / 2 / 4 / 10` vs engine/effects/raster.emp:94-187 OP_SET_REG/OP_CRAM/OP_PAL_REGION/OP_PAL_RESTORE (the .emp copies are held by raster_dsl.emp:35-36's pin; the Python ones by nothing)
  command longwords — raster_cost_probe.py:71-76 `CRAM_WRITE = 0xC0000000`, `VSRAM_WRITE = 0x40000010`, `_delta()` vs engine.vdp's vdp_comm (pinned .emp-side at games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp:93, 207, 312 — never Python-side)
  the staging offset — raster_cost_probe.py:112 `o["slot"] * 128 + o["pl"] * 32 + o["e"] * 2` and again in tools/raster_source_gate.py:94 `return f["slot"] * 128 + f["pal_line"] * 32 + f["entry"] * 2`, vs engine/effects/raster.emp:135
  the schedule — raster_cost_probe.py:131-144 `0x8AFF` / `0x8A00 | gap` / `0xFFFF` and the `L[i+2]-L[i+1]-1` rule vs raster_dsl.emp:1276-1279 arm_at, and :145-146 `len(out) * 2 > 128` vs raster_dsl.emp:1526
WHY `calls` DOES NOT COVER IT: `calls` is the HBlank entry count, which is driven by the arm words alone. Concrete slip: transcribe the restore arm as `[10, hi, lo, o["n"], o["a"]]` instead of `o["n"] - 1` (note raster_dsl.emp:739 spells `cnt - 1`). F8 then streams 4 words per fire instead of 3, `calls` stays 6 (raster_cost_probe.py:219 authors 6 fires either way), and the probe reports 704 + 30 = 734/fire with "spread 0" across boots. That number is what the constant is set from — engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp:1009-1016 `RASTER_WORK_RESTORE_CYC = 212 // MEASURED 2026-08-17 ... F8 re-measured at 704/fire after calibration` — and RASTER_WORK_RESTORE_CYC is what band() divides the author's height by (raster_dsl.emp:626-628, :652-653), so a 30-cycle inflation refuses legal band heights and a deflation admits overrunning ones. The tree already anticipates the trigger: raster.emp:180-186 and raster_dsl.emp:1034-1039 both warn that appending or reordering an opcode re-prices the chain and names the .emp literals to update; neither names raster_cost_probe.py, which carries the same opcodes.
No automated cross-check exists: `tools/test_*.py` has no test for raster_cost_probe (18 test files, none of them it), and build.sh:209-217 runs pytest over tools/ — so the encoder is exercised only by hand runs of the emulator-backed gates.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a tools-side pytest that reads the opcode/park/terminator/buffer-size constants out of the .emp with the existing `emp_int()`/`emp_constants()` helpers and asserts the Python encoder against them, plus one golden word-list per op class copied from an existing hand twin (e.g. ojz_effects.emp:250-260 OJZ_WATER_HAND, raster_dsl.emp:1853-1866 RASTER_BAND_TWIN_HAND) — those twins are already hand-derived, so reusing them makes the Python encoder answerable to the same authority as the .emp encoder. Also collapse raster_source_gate.py:94's copy of the staging formula onto the probe's.

findings.title: The budget model's ungated fire-cost rows have already drifted from the .emp fixture pins they mirror
findings.claim: effects_budget_model.toml mirrors the per-fire cost measurements that raster_dsl.emp pins, but only the [raster.cost_model] rows are gated by [symbols]; the F1 and water-fire rows still carry pre-RUNGS=5 values, so the build-fatal budget check passes while the file states two numbers the code contradicts.
findings.evidence:
Drifted pair 1 — fixture F1, the same quantity in both files:
  tools/effects_budget_model.toml:55 `sparse_fire_reg1_cycles   = 396      # measured — fixture F1; the old model scored this ZERO`
  engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp:1124-1125 `ensure(fire_cost_cycles(fire(3, [reg_set($8C81)])) == 412, ... )  // measured 2026-08-17 at RUNGS=5, 3 boots spread 0 (was 396 at RUNGS=4)`
Drifted pair 2 — the OJZ water fire (reg_sh_on + 3-word region):
  tools/effects_budget_model.toml:57 `sparse_fire_water_cycles  = 660      # modelled — reg_sh_on + 3-word region, the OJZ water fire`
  engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp:644 `merged fire tops out at 302 + 110 + 264 = 676`. Recomputing from the shipped constants: SetReg = 8 fetch + 16*5 dispatch + 12 work + 10 tail = 110; PalRegion(3) = 8 + (16*1+18) + 122 + 3*30 + 10 = 264; + RASTER_FIRE_BASE_CYC 302 = 676. Both rows are exactly 16 low — the RUNGS 4->5 tax on the fall-through op (raster_dsl.emp:1030-1041).
A third copy of the same figure, in a subject file:
  games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp:617-618 `channel 0's fire is modelled at 526 / cycles against a 489-cycle line` — 526 is the superseded interrupts.hint differential (toml:59 keeps it as `sparse_fire_cram3_cycles_SUPERSEDED`), the real model is 676, and RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC is 488 not 489 (raster_dsl.emp:983).
WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A COMMENT: this file declares itself "the ONE machine-readable budget" (toml:1) and tools/effects_budget_check.py runs build-fatal (build.sh:190-194), so a green build reads as "the model agrees with the code". Only [symbols]-listed rows are compared (effects_budget_check.py:194-199, toml:220-245), and none of the sparse_fire_* rows is listed. The file even has a convention for this case — `*_SUPERSEDED` rows at toml:41-42, 58-59 — which was not applied when F1 was re-measured. Supporting evidence that stale prose accumulates beside gated numbers here: toml:203-206's comment says raster_state_bytes went "288 -> 306" while the gated value on :203 is 318.
findings.fix_sketch: Either rename the two drifted rows to `*_SUPERSEDED` and add the current values, or (better) add [symbols] entries for the fixture rows keyed to a comptime expression over the shipped constants so effects_budget_check gates them like the cost_model block; fix ojz_effects.emp:617-618 to the model's own numbers while touching that comment.

findings.title: Poison EXPECTED FRAGMENT headers have drifted from the CASES table for exactly the pair the runner deliberately split
findings.claim: The README makes each poison's `EXPECTED FRAGMENT` header comment a hand-synced copy of its CASES row; the two $8F cases still say "autoincrement" while CASES was changed to two distinct fragments, so the surviving header text points a maintainer back at the non-discriminating fragment that makes case 8d E-D vacuous.
findings.evidence:
The contract: games/sonic4/test/poison/README.md:61-63 `- **Register the row in `CASES`** in `tools/emp_expect_fail.py` — path, entry id, expected message fragment, expected `[Error]` count — and give the module the exact `EXPECTED FRAGMENT` header comment the row quotes.`
The two sites, disagreeing:
  games/sonic4/test/poison/poison_regset_8f.emp:4 `// EXPECTED FRAGMENT: "autoincrement"`  vs  tools/emp_expect_fail.py:74 `(f"{POISON}/poison_regset_8f.emp",  "8d D-C",  "assumes stride 2", 1),`
  games/sonic4/test/poison/poison_direct_8f.emp:4 `// EXPECTED FRAGMENT: "autoincrement"`  vs  tools/emp_expect_fail.py:75 `(f"{POISON}/poison_direct_8f.emp",  "8d E-D",  "cannot be dodged", 1),`
The runner's own comment says why the split exists: emp_expect_fail.py:56-60 `The two $8F cases (8d D-C and 8d E-D) expect DISTINCT fragments so a case passing does not merely mean "the string 'autoincrement' appeared somewhere"`. All ten other headers match their rows exactly (checked: two_restores/band_buried_tint/patchable_band_fire/patchable_partner/setreg_on_restore/direct_8a/ship_plus_restore/band_h1_region/band_h2_sh/sentinel), so these two are the only drift.
FAILURE WALK. Both target messages contain the word "autoincrement": raster_dsl.emp:151-152 (the reg_set constructor) and raster_dsl.emp:1385-1386 (the program-level scan). Reword either message keeping "autoincrement" but dropping "assumes stride 2" — which the stale header presents as sufficient — and build.sh:229-232's expect-fail lane goes build-fatal with "failed WITHOUT the expected fragment". The repair a maintainer reaches for from the header is to relax CASES back to "autoincrement", at which point poison_direct_8f.emp passes on either guard's text and stops proving that the un-dodgeable program-level scan (claim E-D, the one that catches direct `RasterOp.SetReg($8F04)` construction) fires at all — the exact vacuity the split was introduced to prevent.
findings.fix_sketch: Update the two headers to quote their rows verbatim, and add a two-line check to emp_expect_fail.py's `main` startup scan (it already opens every module path at :128-134) asserting each poison's `EXPECTED FRAGMENT:` header contains its CASES fragment — turning the README's hand ritual into a mechanism.

findings.title: effects_gates hardcodes reg_sh_on's word and the restore's dispatch depth in a gate whose contract says nothing is copied
findings.claim: The gate's docstring and derive_arms go to real trouble to derive every arm word from the scene's own pokes and the bands read out of game source, then spell $8C89 and the restore's dispatch depth as literals — two facts that live as named constants the file's own emp_int() helper could read.
findings.evidence:
The stated contract: tools/effects_gates.py:20-23 `raster program shape — `effects_scene_assert` on each scene's sidecar, against arm words DERIVED here from the scene's own pokes and the bands read out of the game source. Never copied from a table: two gates in this tree were written against copied numbers and would have passed on incorrect code.`
Copy 1 — the S/H word:
  tools/effects_gates.py:156 `"--expect-present" if setreg else "--expect-absent", "0x8C89"]`
  engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp:162-163 `const RASTER_SH_BASE = $8C81` / `const RASTER_SH_BIT  = 8` — reg_sh_on() is their OR (:170-172), and reg_sh_off()'s note at :180-184 records that a future `Set_VDP_Reg($0C)` caller legitimately re-bases reg $0C, i.e. moves this word.
Copy 2 — the restore's dispatch depth:
  tools/effects_gates.py:210 `fire_rest = base + fetch + (rung * 4 + hit) + wrest + 3 * word + tail` — the 4 is a literal, while every other term on the line is read with emp_int()
  engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp:1033 `const RASTER_DEPTH_RESTORE          = 4      // rungs FAILED before this op matches`, whose pin at :1040 and TRAP note at :1034-1039 exist precisely because that number moves when the chain changes; effects_gates.py:186 already proves private consts are readable (`RASTER_WORK_REG_CYC`).
CONSEQUENCE. Both drifts fail loudly on the scene where the word must be PRESENT / against measured hardware, so the damage is bounded — but the `--expect-absent 0x8C89` half is the assertion that proves record suppression on the `suppressed` and `above_screen` scenes (effects_gates.py:98, :156), and it is satisfied by any change that removes $8C89 from the program for the wrong reason. Run with `--only scene:suppressed` (the file offers the flag at :117) and that is the only $8C89 assertion in play, with nothing left to fail loudly.
findings.fix_sketch: `sh_word = emp_int("engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp", "RASTER_SH_BASE") | emp_int(..., "RASTER_SH_BIT")` and `rung * emp_int(..., "RASTER_DEPTH_RESTORE") + hit`; both constants are already in reach of the helper at :51.

findings.title: pal_stage_off's formula has three unpinned inline copies whose only value check is a hand twin scheduled to retire
findings.claim: The variant staging offset is inlined in three places in raster_dsl.emp because imported names do not travel into a comptime body, and the module-level pin checks only its own fourth copy — the emitter copies are held to their values solely by the OJZ hand twins, whose comments say they retire in Parcel D.
findings.evidence:
The authority: engine/effects/raster.emp:131-136 `pub comptime fn pal_stage_off(...) { ... return slot * 128 + line * 32 + entry * 2 }`
The pin, and what it actually reads: engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp:57-60 `// stream_pal_region inlines the staging arithmetic rather than calling pal_stage_off (a\n// call-site name); this pins the formula against its authority.\nensure(pal_stage_off(1, 3, 5) == 1 * 128 + 3 * 32 + 5 * 2, ...)` — it compares pal_stage_off against a literal expression written inside the ensure, so it fires when the AUTHORITY changes and never reads any emitter site. (It also misnames the site: stream_pal_region at :204-220 validates addresses; the copies are elsewhere.)
The three real copies:
  raster_dsl.emp:729 `slot * 128 + pl * 32 + e * 2]` (op_words, PalRegion — the emitted program word)
  raster_dsl.emp:824 `PalRegion(a, slot, pl, e, cnt) => slot * 128 + pl * 32 + e * 2,` (op_ship_stage_off — the frame-top DMA source)
  raster_dsl.emp:580 `addr:     0 * 128 + pal_line * 32 + entry * 2,` (fx_tint_band — the CRAM destination)
What holds them today: only literal `72` in the game-side twins — games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp:258 `72,  // Pal_Variant_Stage offset` and :704 `72,  // Pal_Variant_Stage offset — the fire's own` — and both fixtures are marked for deletion: ojz_effects.emp:124 `It retires in Parcel D together with the fixture it pins (design spec 8.2)` and :246 `Retires in Parcel D with the fixture.` Every shipped fixture uses slot 0, so the `slot * 128` term is unexercised by the twins at all; the only check on it is tools/raster_source_gate.py's slot-1 fixture (:79), which is emulator-backed, manual, and carries its own copy of the formula (:94).
Related census, same fact spread wider: the 128-byte slot stride also appears at engine/effects/palette.emp:665 `lea Pal_Variant_Stage + 128, a1` (the runtime derive's slot-1 destination), palette.emp:91 `(128 * PAL_MAX_VARIANTS)`, engine/ram.emp:398 `[u8; 128 * 2]`, and tools/effects_budget_model.toml:228 `PAL_MAX_VARIANTS * 128`; only the last two are related by a guard (the PALETTE_STATE_SIZE span ensure).
findings.fix_sketch: Add module-level ensures in raster_dsl.emp that read the EMITTERS rather than restating the formula — e.g. `op_words(stream_pal_region(...))`'s last word and `op_ship_stage_off(...)` compared against `pal_stage_off(...)` for a slot-1 case — so the pins survive the Parcel D retirement of the OJZ hand twins, and name the 128 stride once for palette.emp:665 too.

findings.title: Off-screen ship's drop guard hardcodes Palette_Dirty bit 2 while the trailer carries the line
findings.claim: The frame-top ship's "did the base palette DMA actually land" guard tests a hardcoded `Palette_Dirty` bit 2, but the ship's palette line is authored data (it comes from the trailer's CRAM byte address), so for any ship on CRAM line 1 or 3 the guard tests a bit nothing sets and goes fully vacuous — the ship then re-issues variant colours over a line whose base reload was dropped.
findings.evidence:
buffers.emp:397-433 is the whole ship path:
```
        move.l  Effects_Offscreen_Entry, d0
        beq     .no_ship
        btst    #2, Palette_Dirty               // (Palette_Dirty).w
        bne     .no_ship
```
with the comment at :399-401 stating the intent: "bit 2 CLEAR means line 2 either shipped this frame or was not dirty ... Bit 2 still SET means the base ship DROPPED (queue full), and shipping over a line that did not get reloaded is not a state to add to."

The line is NOT fixed by anything upstream. `ship_trailer` (raster_dsl.emp:1633-1665) emits `op_ship_cram_addr(o)` verbatim, and `Raster_BuildShipEntry` (raster.emp:1049-1051) turns that byte address into the DMA destination:
```
        move.w  6(a1), d2
        vdp_comm_reg(d2, VdpTarget.Cram, VdpOp.Dma)
```
The only constraint on the address is `stream_pal_region`'s `pal_line >= 1 && pal_line <= 3` (raster_dsl.emp:208-209), and `patchable`'s `offscreen_ship` guard only requires "exactly ONE stream_pal_region op" (raster_dsl.emp:408-411) — it says nothing about which line. `fx_tint_band(line: 100, slot: 0, pal_line: 1, entry: 4, count: 3, sh: 1)` marked `patchable(..., offscreen_ship: 1)` is therefore fully legal today, and no `ensure` anywhere pins the ship's line to 2 (grepped: `btst #2, Palette_Dirty` is the only reference, and tools/effects_gates.py / raster_source_gate.py / snapshot_poison_gate.py never exercise a non-line-2 ship).

Concrete walk for a line-1 ship. `op_mask` (raster_dsl.emp:891) makes the program's `pal_dirty_mask` = `1 << ($28 >> 5)` = %0010, so `Raster_VBlank` (raster.emp:593-594 `or.b d1, Palette_Dirty`) sets ONLY bit 1 each frame. On a steady OJZ frame `Palette_Compose` (palette.emp:327-389) contributes no dirty bits at all — base is one-shot, cycling/fade/operators are off, and the variant arm early-outs on PAL_ACT_VARIANT_STALE — so bit 2 is CLEAR every frame. Now let the Critical DMA queue be full at the line-1 enqueue (buffers.emp:332-333 `queue_static_dma(Static_Pal_Line1)` / `bcs .skip_pal1`): bit 1 is deliberately left set and CRAM line 1 keeps last frame's contents (which, if the previous frame shipped, are the VARIANT colours). Execution then falls to :402, `btst #2` reads 0, the guard passes, and `queue_static_dma(Static_Pal_Ship)` re-ships the variant colours over line 1 on top of a base that was never restored — precisely the state the comment says must be refused. The line-2 case works only by coincidence of today's authored address ($48).

Inverse direction, same root: with a line-1 or line-3 ship, a frame where line 2 IS dirty-and-dropped (a fade or cycling frame that ORs %1110, palette.emp:365/373) suppresses a ship that had nothing to do with line 2 — one frame of the dry stripe the ship exists to remove.
findings.fix_sketch: The bit is a build-time fact of the fire's own address, exactly like `op_mask`. Cheapest correct fix: have `ship_trailer` emit `1 << (addr >> 5)` as a sixth word of the entry and replace :402 with `move.w <mask>(a2), d1 / and.b Palette_Dirty, d1 / bne .no_ship` (the entry pointer is already in d0/a2 by then). Zero-cost stopgap if the trailer format must stay frozen for P1: an `ensure` in `patchable`/`ship_trailer` refusing `offscreen_ship` unless the op's `pal_line == 2`, quoting buffers.emp:402 as the reason.

findings.title: Raster_BuildSchedule re-records the whole schedule every VBlank with no change detection
findings.claim: The patched-program schedule is rebuilt from the ROM template on every single VBlank whenever a patch table is live, at a project-measured 1228 cycles, even though its only frame-varying inputs are the RASTER_MAX_PATCH words of Effects_Screen_L — so for every frame in which no anchor's clamped fire line moved (a still camera, a paused/frozen scene, a vertical-only move that does not cross a pixel boundary) the proc reproduces a byte-identical buffer at full price.
findings.evidence:
The only liveness test is the table pointer:
```
proc Raster_BuildSchedule () clobbers(d0-d4/a0-a2) {
        move.l  Raster_Patch_Tab, d0
        beq     .none                       // liveness: the TABLE, never Active_Buf
```
(raster.emp:1101-1103) and `Raster_VBlank` calls it unconditionally on both the install and no-install paths (raster.emp:588), from BOTH `VInt_Level` and `VInt_Lag` (vblank.emp:157, 291) — so on a lag frame it runs twice against one `Effects_LatchWorldLines` update and produces the same schedule twice.

Everything it writes except the arm bytes is frame-invariant: the header word and both priming records are copied verbatim (`move.w (a2)+, (a1)+` / two `move.l (a2)+, (a1)+`, :1119-1123), each emitted record's whole body is copied out of the template unchanged (:1153-1162), and the terminator is re-emitted (:1166-1167). The only per-frame computation is `gap = L[k] - L[k-1] - 1` written as one byte per record (:1143-1147) plus the emit/suppress/clamp decision (:1128-1139), all of which are pure functions of `Effects_Screen_L[ch]` and the record's two band words.

The cost is the project's own measurement, not my estimate — tools/effects_budget_model.toml:195: `build_schedule_cycles = 1228   # 2 records, none suppressed`, with :190-193 recording `Raster_VBlank 634 -> 1490 (+856)` and `VInt_Level 7499 -> 8421 (+922, the BRACKET)`, i.e. ~1.9 scanlines of an ~18,200-cycle NTSC VBlank, spent inside the sound-ON DMA-flag / sound-OFF z80_stopped bracket. OJZ section 0 is exactly the 2-record case measured, and its steady state is a still or slowly-panning camera, so most frames pay 1228 cycles to write the same 18 words they wrote last frame.

This is the same shape the parcel already accepted elsewhere: `Palette_Compose`'s variant derive was 19,332 cycles/frame of bit-identical recomputation until PAL_ACT_VARIANT_STALE gated it (budget model :164-176, "same image, ~19.5k fewer cycles"). No equivalent gate exists here.
findings.fix_sketch: Keep one word per channel of the previous frame's CLAMPED fire line (or a 4-word shadow of Effects_Screen_L) and early-out when none moved: `RASTER_MAX_PATCH` word compares against a shadow bank is ~60 cycles versus 1228. It must compare the clamped/suppressed decision, not the raw anchor, so a move entirely inside a clamp region still short-circuits. Note the buffer swap must then also be skipped (do not swap when nothing was rebuilt), which is the one subtlety — the cursor rewind at raster.emp:609 reads Active_Buf after the call.

findings.title: Budget model's reg-op fire rows are stale by one dispatch rung and are outside the [symbols] gate
findings.claim: `sparse_fire_reg1_cycles = 396` and `sparse_fire_water_cycles = 660` in the file that calls itself "the ONE machine-readable budget" are the pre-OP_PAL_RESTORE (RUNGS=4) figures; the shipped model gives 412 and 676. Both rows are absent from the `[symbols]` table, so `tools/effects_budget_check.py` cannot see the drift, and the authored data quotes a third, differently-stale number to justify a live band separation.
findings.evidence:
The shipped cost model charges OP_SET_REG the whole fall-through: `SetReg(w) => RASTER_DISPATCH_RUNG_CYC * RASTER_DISPATCH_RUNGS` (raster_dsl.emp:1046) with `RASTER_DISPATCH_RUNGS = 5` (raster_dsl.emp:1030) since OP_PAL_RESTORE was appended (raster.emp:180-186: "The SetReg fall-through pays the +16 rung tax (F1 396->412, F5 612->628, re-pinned in raster_dsl.emp by the encoder task)").

So, by the model's own arithmetic (`op_cost = fetch 8 + dispatch + work + 30*words + tail 10`, raster_dsl.emp:1067, over `RASTER_FIRE_BASE_CYC = 302`):
- F1, one reg_set: 302 + (8 + 16*5 + 12 + 0 + 10) = 412. raster_dsl.emp:1124-1125 pins exactly this and annotates "measured 2026-08-17 at RUNGS=5, 3 boots spread 0 (was 396 at RUNGS=4)". effects_budget_model.toml:55 still reads `396      # measured — fixture F1`.
- The OJZ water fire (`reg_sh_on` + 3-word `stream_pal_region`): 302 + 110 + (8 + (16*1 + 18) + 122 + 90 + 10) = 302 + 110 + 264 = 676. effects_budget_model.toml:57 still reads `660      # modelled — reg_sh_on + 3-word region, the OJZ water fire`, which is the RUNGS=4 value (302 + 94 + 264).

Neither row appears in `[symbols]`, whose own preamble lists the deliberate exclusions (save_set_registers, program_overhead_fires, full_line_fire_lines, compose_static_frame) and does not mention these — so the gate that caught `418 + 36x` drifting "out from under this file" is structurally blind to exactly the two rows that moved. Confirmed: `grep -rn 'sparse_fire_reg1\|sparse_fire_water' tools/*.py` returns nothing.

The authored data then reasons from a fourth number. games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp:619: "channel 0's fire is modelled at 526 cycles against a 489-cycle line, so it spills about one line past its own. Two lines of separation is the margin". 526 is the SUPERSEDED `interrupts.hint` differential for a 3-word stream_cram fire (budget model :60 `sparse_fire_cram3_cycles_SUPERSEDED = 526`), not a reg+region fire, and 489 is not `RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC` (488, raster_dsl.emp:983). The true figure for that fire is 676 = 1.39 lines. The conclusion survives — `check_density`'s worst-case gap for OJZ_TwoChannel is band_lo_fl(ch1) 221 - band_hi_fl(ch0) 219 = 2 lines = 976 cycles >= 676 — but the stated margin is 300 cycles wider than the reader is told, on the one number the file says "is the number to watch" for the next op added to channel 0.
findings.fix_sketch: Set :55 to 412 and :57 to 676, and add both to `[symbols]` as derived rows (they are pure functions of the gated cost-model constants: reg1 = fire_base + fetch + rung*rungs + work_reg + tail; water = reg1 + fetch + rung + hit + work_region + 3*stream_word). Then rewrite ojz_effects.emp:619's sentence against the derived 676/488. A derived-row check is what makes the +16-per-rung tax visible next time the chain grows, which is the trap raster_dsl.emp:1034-1039 already warns about for opcode 12's author.

findings.title: Dense-body kind discriminator is a build-time constant, evaluated per scanline, for an op class with no live client
findings.claim: `Raster_Dense_Kind` is written once per ENTER and is a property of the program's opcode (OP_RUN_GRADIENT vs OP_RUN_RAMP), yet it is re-read and branched on inside `.dense_body` on every line of a run — and OP_RUN_RAMP has no reachable client in the shipped ROM, so the live gradient run pays the discriminator for a feature nothing can select.
findings.evidence:
The per-line body opens with the test:
```
    .dense_body:
        move.w  #RASTER_ARM_EVERY_LINE, (a2)       // reg $0A=0: fire every line
        move.l  Raster_Dense_Cmd, (a2)             // constant command (sets the address)
        tst.w   Raster_Dense_Kind
        bne.s   .ramp_body
```
(raster.emp:822-835). `Raster_Dense_Kind` is written only by the two ENTER arms — `clr.w Raster_Dense_Kind` at .op_run_gradient (:773) and `move.w #1, Raster_Dense_Kind` at .op_run_ramp (:786) — i.e. once per frame per program, from a value the opcode already determined at build time.

Cost walk, gradient path (Kind == 0), 68000 with sigil's absolute-short RAM addressing: `tst.w (xxx).W` = 4 + 8 = 12 cycles, `bne.s` not taken = 8 cycles, so 20 cycles per dense line. OJZ_TestGradient is `lines: 96` (ojz_effects.emp:304, 335-340), so ~1,920 cycles per frame in OJZ section 2 — against a measured per-line body upper bound of 342 cycles (tools/effects_budget_model.toml:128), i.e. ~6% of the dense body, in the one loop DEFERRED_WORK item 6 already flags as the dense tier's optimisation target ("for a 224-line gradient that difference is ~thousands of cycles/frame"). At 224 lines it is ~4,480 cycles/frame. It is also positioned between the constant-command write and the first `move.w (a1)+, VDP_DATA`, and `.dense_body` carries NO EFX_BLANK_DELAY of its own, so those 20 cycles shift the whole per-line burst later in the line — the dense landing is prologue-timing-dependent by construction.

The ramp half is unreachable in the shipped ROM. `OJZ_TestRamp` (ojz_effects.emp:478-483) is the tree's only `RasterRampProgram`, and it is bound only to `sec_raster_table` (act_descriptor.emp:187, annotated "legacy pal:/raster: pair above (which stays, inert, for Task 13)"). `sec_raster_table` has no reader: the legacy installers were deleted (preset.emp:152-153 names `Raster_InstallSection` as replaced; commit e6b016e5 "remove the dead legacy per-field installer path"), and section 0's live preset is `OJZ_Preset_Sec0`, which binds `patched: OJZ_TwoChannel` and surrenders the ramp by preset()'s own exclusivity ensure (ojz_effects.emp:553-559, 569-571). So `.op_run_ramp`, `.ramp_body`, `Raster_Ramp_Acc`/`Raster_Ramp_Step`/`Raster_Dense_Kind` (10 of the 318 bytes of Raster_State, ram.emp:307-309) and OP_RUN_RAMP's dispatch rung are all runtime-dead, alongside ~96 bytes of emitted-but-never-installed fixtures (OJZ_TestRamp 34 B, OJZ_WaterRaster 34 B, OJZ_TestVsram 28 B — none of the three has an installer; the water fixture's only remaining mention is ojz_scroll_test.emp:269, "The hand install of OJZ_WaterRaster that used to sit here is GONE").
findings.fix_sketch: Two build-time-honest spellings, both zero-risk to the live gradient: (a) hoist the discriminator to the handler top so it shares the `tst.w Raster_Dense_Lines` already there — store the ramp's line count NEGATED at ENTER, then `tst.w Raster_Dense_Lines / beq .sparse / bmi .ramp_body` costs one extra taken branch and no second RAM read (saves ~12 cyc/line and removes a word of RAM); or (b) if the ramp stays clientless through the freeze, delete it and re-add it with its first real content, which is what raster.emp's own precedent says (the row-119 note at :212-214 deleted `raster_fire_screen` for being "dead code that had never affected a shipped program"). Either way, decide BEFORE the P1 identity freeze — after it, removing the discriminator is a fix/repin/refreeze cycle.

findings.title: The two priming records exist because reg $0A = 0 is hardcoded, not because the hardware needs two
findings.claim: Every armed raster program pays two priming HInt fires — a project-measured 572 cycles per frame — solely because `Raster_VBlank` always hands `HBlank_Install` a reg $0A of 0. The parameter for a program-carried preload already exists, and every program's first fire line is a comptime constant, so the encoder could eliminate one of the two priming records for any program whose first event lands on an even screen line.
findings.evidence:
The hardcode is one instruction:
```
        moveq   #0, d0
        lea     Raster_HInt(pc), a0
        jbsr    HBlank_Install
```
(raster.emp:613-622), against a callee that already takes the counter as data: `pub proc HBlank_Install (a0: HBlankHandler, d0: u8)` ... `move.b d0, VDP_Shadow_Table + VDP_HINT_OFF` (hblank.emp:57-61). Raster_HInt writes reg $0A directly and never touches the shadow, so the shadow value is purely a frame-top preload.

Apply the module's own timing model (raster.emp:23-31, Ruling 1b: "the VDP reloads its internal line counter from reg $0A at the instant of underflow, before the 68000 executes a single handler instruction ... it is consumed by the reload at fire i+1"). With reg $0A preloaded to P: F0 = P, F1 = P + P + 1, and the arm written at F0 governs F2. Today P = 0 gives F0 = 0, F1 = 1, F2 = 1 + arm0 + 1, and `arm0 = $8A00 | (M - 3)` lands F2 at M-1 — exactly the derivation at raster.emp:890-901. Choose instead P = (E1 - 1)/2 where E1 = M - 1 is the first event's fire line, and F1 IS the first event: for OJZ_TestRaster (M = 120, E1 = 119) P = 59; for OJZ_TwoChannel's first fire (screen 100, E1 = 99) P = 49; for OJZ_TestGradient's T-1 setup line (top 96, E1 = 95) P = 47. Every arm after that is still expressible, because record i's arm governs record i+2 and there are still two records ahead of every event. One priming record disappears; the encoder can test `(M - 2) & 1 == 0` at build time and fall back to the pair when it is odd.

What that buys is the project's own F0 measurement: "Its two priming records read 572 cycles, i.e. 286 per no-op record" (raster_dsl.emp:1140-1144, five boots, spread 0). 286 cycles/frame and one exception entry, forever, on every armed program — the same class of "cost forever to accomplish nothing" the EFX-7 fix already removed for empty programs (raster.emp:536-543: "armed, Raster_Program_None cost 512 cycles per frame across TWO HInt entries, forever, to accomplish nothing").

The rigidity is what makes this a freeze-window item rather than a free optimisation: the count 2 is baked into `fire_lines`'s `out = [0, 1]` (raster_dsl.emp:1252-1253), `check_intervals`'s `prev_hi = 1` (:1193), `arm_word_index`'s `if k == 0 return 1 / if k == 1 return 3 / idx = 5` (:1543-1545), `patch_table`'s `k = 2` (:1584), and `Raster_BuildSchedule`'s fixed 5-word verbatim prologue (raster.emp:1113-1123, documented at :1502-1505 as "a constant rather than a computed skip"). All of those move, and so do every program's emitted bytes.
findings.fix_sketch: Not a change to smuggle into a zero-byte parcel — but the decision belongs before the P1 identity freeze, because afterwards it is a byte-moving fix/repin/refreeze across every program plus both hand-word twin sets. Minimum shape: one header word carrying the preload (or a `prime_records: 1|2` field the encoder computes), `Raster_VBlank` loading it into d0 instead of `moveq #0`, and the five baked-in `2`s above parameterised on it.

findings.title: check_density never covers the priming-to-first-event gap
findings.claim: `check_density` walks only the authored fire list, so the gap between priming record 1 and the first authored record — the one gap whose left-hand fire the runtime, not the author, controls — is never charged. It is harmless only because a priming record's cost happens to fit one scanline.
findings.fix_sketch: Charge the schedule, not the authored list: build `L = fire_lines(fires)` first (raster_program already does, :1336) and walk pairs of L with a cost function that returns RASTER_FIRE_BASE_CYC for the two priming indices. That is ~5 lines, zero ROM bytes, and it makes the guard's coverage match its own docstring.
