findings.title: OP_RUN_GRADIENT wire format has no repeat: 528 of 576 stream bytes are literal repetition
findings.claim: The dense-gradient wire body pays an unconditional 6 bytes per scanline (RASTER_CRAM_MAX words), but CRAM is 3 bits per channel, so a monotonic gradient can never hold more than 8 distinct rows — the shipped stream is 96 rows of which 88 are byte-identical duplicates of their predecessor, 528 dead ROM bytes (43% of all authored OJZ effects data, 15% of the whole effects substrate ROM).
findings.evidence: Authoring site: `pub data OJZ_GradientStream: [u16; 288] = comptime for i in 0..288 { grad_word(i) }` (ojz_effects.emp:326), fed to `raster_gradient_program(top: OJZ_GRAD_TOP, lines: OJZ_GRAD_LINES, ... stream_words: 288)` (:335-340). The comment at :315-317 already states the fact: "the ramp steps every 12 lines and a 'monotonic ramp' claim means non-decreasing with exactly 8 distinct levels, not 96." Measured from the shipped image (s4.bin, OJZ_GradientStream @ $124FA, 96 rows x 6 bytes, derived by differencing s4.lst labels OJZ_GradientStream $124FA .. OJZ_TestGradient $1273A = 576 bytes): 8 distinct rows, each repeated exactly 12x — $0000/$0000/$0000, $0200/$0220/$0202, $0400/$0440/$0404, $0600/$0660/$0606, $0800/$0880/$0808, $0A00/$0AA0/$0A0A, $0C00/$0CC0/$0C0C, $0E00/$0EE0/$0E0E. Unique payload = 8 x 6 = 48 B; emitted = 576 B; waste = 528 B. The format itself is the cause: engine/effects/raster.emp:~168-176 defines the body as `dc.w <line count L>` + `dc.l <ROM gradient stream pointer>   L*3 colour words, 3 per line`, with no hold/repeat term, and Raster_HInt's `.dense_body` (s4.lst $6A0C, 46 bytes) advances Raster_Dense_Cursor by 6 unconditionally every line. Cost comparison, derived from the same op sizes: the identical 8-step visual expressed in the SPARSE tier is 8 OP_CRAM fires = 8 x (4 framing + 4 cmd + 2 count + 6 colours) = 128 B, + 2 header + 8 priming + 4 terminator = 142 B, replacing 30 (OJZ_TestGradient) + 576 (stream) = 606 B — a 464-byte ROM saving, and 8 HInt entries per frame instead of 96.
findings.fix_sketch: Either (a) add a hold/repeat word to the OP_RUN_GRADIENT body (`dc.w lines_per_row`) so the handler advances the cursor only every Nth line — costs a decrement+branch in the hottest handler path, so it needs a cycle measurement before adoption; or (b) cheapest and zero handler cost: re-author step-wise CRAM gradients in the sparse tier (one fire per step) and reserve OP_RUN_GRADIENT for streams that genuinely differ per line, i.e. VSRAM targets. Do this BEFORE the P1 identity freeze — afterwards it is a fix+repin+refreeze chain.

findings.title: Patched-template 128-byte pad: its stated justification was deleted with the copy it protected; 82 of OJZ_TwoChannel's 164 bytes are zero pad
findings.claim: `patched_program` pads every patched template to a full 64 words because "the runtime's copy routine copies a FIXED 128 bytes from every template" — but the patched path's copy was deleted (the builder re-records from the ROM template), so nothing ever reads the pad; its only surviving function is putting the patch table at a constant +128, which a single length word would do for 2 bytes instead of up to 82.
findings.evidence: raster_dsl.emp:1776 `comptime var pad = 64 - out.len` / `for i in 0..pad { out = out ++ [0] }` (:1779), justified at :1767-1771: "WHY THE PADDING IS NOT WASTE. The runtime's copy routine copies a FIXED 128 bytes from every template, so a patched template is already read to +128 — padding makes that read defined". That premise is now false for patched programs: engine/effects/raster.emp:981 records "The install half of what Raster_CopyPatchedTemplate used to do. The COPY is gone — the builder re-records the whole schedule from the ROM template at the next VBlank". Raster_VBlank's fixed 128-byte copy (`move.w #(RASTER_BUF_SIZE / 2) - 1, d1` / `.copy`, raster.emp:575-577) is reachable only from `.copy_program`, i.e. only for programs staged through Raster_Pending (Raster_Install), and Raster_InstallPatched instead does `clr.l Raster_Pending` (raster.emp:~988) — so no patched template ever takes it. Raster_BuildSchedule reads only the header (`move.w (a2)+, (a1)+`), the two priming records, and per-record spans via rec_off/rec_len (raster.emp:1116-1160); Raster_BuildShipEntry reads the trailer table-relative. The pad is touched by nothing. Measured from the shipped image (s4.bin @ $1287C, span derived from s4.lst OJZ_TwoChannel $1287C .. ObjDef_Static $12920 = 164 bytes): real body = 23 words (words 0..22, ending $8AFF/$FFFF at byte 42-45), then words 23..63 are all $0000 = 82 bytes of pad, i.e. 50% of the program. The only three sites assuming +128 are `lea RASTER_BUF_SIZE(a0), a1` (raster.emp:930) and two `suba.w #RASTER_BUF_SIZE, a2` (raster.emp:1118, 1155). NEW INFORMATION ON THE BOOKED EFX-4b: the padding is what BUGS.md's booking implicitly credits for making the 128-byte copy defined, but since patched templates never take that path, the pad mitigates EFX-4b for nothing — every program that actually reaches `.copy_program` is a SHORT static one (OJZ_TestRaster 32 B, OJZ_TestVsram 28 B, OJZ_TestGradient 30 B, OJZ_TestRamp 34 B, all derived from s4.lst label deltas), so the over-read is 94-100 bytes past the end in every live case, not an edge case.
findings.fix_sketch: Put a body-length word in the patch table header (it already carries a record count) or emit the table first, and replace the three `RASTER_BUF_SIZE` displacements with that length; drop the pad loop. Keeps `ensure(out.len * 2 <= 128)` (raster_dsl.emp:1526) as the RAM-buffer bound. Saves 82 B on the one shipped patched program and removes a 128-byte ROM floor from every future one. If the pad is instead kept deliberately, rewrite :1767-1771 — the reason it states no longer exists.

findings.title: Pal_Variant_Stage reserves a line-0 image per slot that is never written or read: 64 dead RAM bytes
findings.claim: The variant staging is 2 slots x 128 bytes (a full 4-line image) but the derive only ever fills lines 1-3 and every consumer's offset arithmetic forbids line 0, so bytes 0-31 and 128-159 (64 of 256) are permanently dead — 6.8% of the 940-byte effects RAM footprint.
findings.evidence: `Pal_Variant_Stage: [u8; 128 * 2],  // PAL_MAX_VARIANTS(2) x 128` (engine/ram.emp:398), confirmed 256 bytes in the shipped image (s4.lst RAM symbols: Pal_Variant_Stage $FFFF8B92 .. Pal_Variant_Ptr $FFFF8C92). The producer starts at line 1 and stops at 4: `moveq #1, d6  // current line index (start at 1)` then `addq.w #1, d6 / cmpi.w #4, d6 / bcs .line` (engine/effects/palette.emp:683, :737-739) — line 0 is never a destination. Every consumer forbids it too: `ensure(line >= 1 && line <= 3, "pal_stage_off: line {line} outside 1..3 (line 0 is the character's)")` (engine/effects/raster.emp:133) and the same slot*128 + line*32 + entry*2 form at raster_dsl.emp:580, :729, :824. The two slot bases are already separate `lea`s — `lea Pal_Variant_Stage, a1` and `lea Pal_Variant_Stage + 128, a1` (palette.emp:659, :665) — so no multiply or power-of-two stride depends on 128.
findings.fix_sketch: Make the slot image 96 bytes (lines 1-3 only): change the two `lea` bases, index dest as (line-1)*32 with `lea Palette_Buffer+32, a2` for the source (pre-shift the line mask once with `lsr.b #1, d5` so btst still lines up — +2 bytes ROM), and change the 128/32 literals at raster.emp:133-137 and raster_dsl.emp:580/729/824. Net -64 B RAM for +2 B ROM. Worth doing before P1 freezes the layout, since it moves Pal_Variant_Ptr onward and forces a repin either way.

findings.title: Three Sec pointer fields have had zero runtime readers since the legacy path was deleted: 108 dead ROM bytes across the shipped section table
findings.claim: sec_pal, sec_raster_table and sec_pal_cycle are read by nothing — Effects_InstallPreset total-binds every channel from sec_effects, and the legacy per-field installers were deleted — yet all three still occupy 4 bytes each in every one of the 9 shipped Sec entries: 108 bytes of ROM the P1 freeze will baseline as identity.
findings.evidence: `sec_pal: *u8, // $10 — 128-byte palette` (:115), `sec_raster_table: *u8 = 0, // $18 — raster command table` (:117), `sec_pal_cycle: *u8 = 0, // $24 — palette cycling script` (:120) in the 66-byte Sec struct. A repo-wide grep for `Sec.sec_pal`, `Sec.sec_raster` and `Sec.sec_pal_cycle` across engine/ and games/ returns NO instruction operand — the only Sec field read at the crossing is `tst.l Sec.sec_effects(a0)` (engine/level/parallax.emp:219), and the same site records "The legacy per-field ... installers (Palette_LoadSection, Palette_InstallCycleSection, Raster_InstallSection) are deleted — effects-P3-C2 Task 13" (:214-217). The data side says so as well: "Parcel C2 Task 12: total-binding preset. Same content as the legacy pal:/raster: pair above (which stays, inert, for Task 13)" (games/sonic4/data/levels/ojz/act1/act_descriptor.emp:188-189). Table size: `ensure(GRID_W * GRID_H == 9, ...)` (act_descriptor.emp:263) x 3 fields x 4 bytes = 108 B. Second-order cost: sec_raster_table is the ONLY reference keeping OJZ_TestRamp (34 B, s4.lst $12774..$12796) linked.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the three fields and the `pal:`/`raster:`/`cycle:` parameters of ojz_sec(), shrinking Sec from 66 to 54 bytes; this moves sec_type_table onward and repins, so it is a P1-migration-window change rather than a later one.

findings.title: The budget model's RAM axis omits 150 of the 940 effects RAM bytes and there is no ROM axis at all
findings.claim: [ram] gates only palette_state_bytes and raster_state_bytes (790 B), so Palette_Ship_Snap (128 B), BgAnim_LastStep (8 B) and Static_Pal_Ship (14 B) — all effects-owned, all added by R1/bg_anim — are invisible to the budget: the model understates the footprint by 16%. There is no ROM row of any kind, so nothing gates encoder output size, which is exactly what the P1 freeze will baseline.
findings.evidence: tools/effects_budget_model.toml:200-207 is the whole axis: `palette_state_bytes  = 472`, `raster_state_bytes   = 318`, `variant_stage_bytes  = 256  # ... (part of palette_state)`, `free_before_stack_kb = 31.8`. Both gated rows are correct — derived independently from the shipped image, Raster_State $FFFF8994 .. Raster_State_End $FFFF8AD2 = 318 and Palette_State $FFFF8AD2 .. Palette_State_End $FFFF8CAA = 472 (s4.lst RAM symbols) — but the real effects RAM total is 318 + 472 + BgAnim_LastStep 8 ($FFFF8CAA, BGANIM_MAX_BANDS=4 x u16) + Static_Pal_Ship 14 ($FFFF8CDC, sizeof(DMAEntry)) + Palette_Ship_Snap 128 ($FFFFB7B6) = 940 B, none of the last three named in the model or in [symbols]. Palette_Ship_Snap alone is the third-largest single effects array in RAM. No `[rom]` table exists anywhere in the file, while the derived substrate ROM is 3576 B plain / 3762 B debug (fill-excluded: RASTER 850, PALETTE 1116, PRESET 174, BG_ANIM 158/344, ojz_effects data 1230, hblank 48 — each derived by differencing s4.lst / s4.debug.lst section head labels and subtracting measured trailing $00 placer fill, e.g. s4.bin $710C..$7110 = 00000000 accounts for the whole plain-vs-debug PRESET delta of 178 vs 174). Supporting evidence that the axis is not being maintained: the row's own derivation comment (:204-206) reads "288 -> 306 in effects-P3 P-b: -4 ... +8 ... +4 for Raster_Patch_Tab, +10 for the ramp cells" and lands at 306 while the gated value is 318 — it omits Effects_Screen_L (8 B) and Effects_Offscreen_Entry (4 B), exactly the 12-byte gap.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `pub const PALETTE_SHIP_SNAP_SIZE = 128` (palette.emp) with an extern-mark span guard, plus rows + [symbols] entries for the snapshot, BgAnim_LastStep and Static_Pal_Ship; add a `[rom]` table with the five section spans and wire it to the same label-difference derivation used above so the P1 freeze has a size baseline it can regress against. Correct the stale :204-206 derivation.

findings.title: Two effects programs with no installer anywhere still ship in both canonical shapes (60 bytes)
findings.claim: OJZ_WaterRaster (32 B) was superseded by OJZ_TwoChannel and its only installer was deliberately deleted, and OJZ_TestVsram (28 B) is installed only by a Python gate poking Raster_Pending over MCP — both are emitted into the RELEASE ROM with no in-ROM path that can ever reach them, and neither orphaning is declared the way OJZ_TestRamp's is.
findings.evidence: `pub data OJZ_WaterRaster: [u16; raster_words(OJZ_WATER_PROG)] = raster_program(OJZ_WATER_PROG)` (ojz_effects.emp:266) — 32 bytes in both shapes (s4.lst $124DA..$124FA; s4.debug.lst identical). A repo-wide grep for OJZ_WaterRaster finds exactly one non-defining reference, and it is a tombstone: "The hand install of OJZ_WaterRaster that used to sit here is GONE (P-b Task 6) ... Task 7 gives a section preset a `patched:` binding, so the preset path is now that installer and a hand install here would be a second, competing one" (games/sonic4/test/ojz_scroll_test.emp:269-278). No EffectsPreset binds it: the five presets bind OJZ_TwoChannel, OJZ_TestRaster, OJZ_TestGradient and Raster_Program_None (ojz_effects.emp:569-575). OJZ_TestVsram (:441, 28 B, s4.lst $12758..$12774) has no .emp reference at all outside its own guards — its only consumer is `real_addr = sym["OJZ_TestVsram"]` in tools/raster_off_gate.py:93, installed by `write_memory` into Raster_Pending (:82-85). Contrast OJZ_TestRamp (34 B), whose parked state IS declared ("OJZ_TestRamp keeps its build-time pins; what it loses is a live render", :557-559) — that one is a knowing retention, the other two are not.
findings.fix_sketch: Either delete OJZ_WaterRaster (its DSL/hand-twin pins are duplicated by OJZ_TwoChannel's) or state the retention the way :553-559 states OJZ_TestRamp's; and move OJZ_TestVsram behind `if DEBUG == 1` so the gate keeps its fixture without the release ROM paying for it.

findings.title: Raster_Line is 2 bytes of RAM with no reader and no writer, pinned by RASTER_STATE_SIZE
findings.claim: Raster_Line survives in the RAM block and in the gated RASTER_STATE_SIZE term after the design removed the runtime line comparison it existed for; nothing in engine/ or games/ reads or writes it, and the P1 freeze will baseline it.
findings.evidence: `Raster_Line:        u16,        // line the cursor's next entry group starts at` (engine/ram.emp:281), 2 bytes at $FFFF89A0 (s4.lst), counted in `RASTER_STATE_SIZE = 4 + 4 + 4 + 2 + ...` (engine/effects/raster.emp:258) and pinned by sigil's raster_port (pins.rs:1460 `/// Raster_Line. tests: raster_port`). A repo-wide grep for Raster_Line outside engine/ram.emp returns only docs: docs/research/2026-08-12-raster-hint-survey.md:134 "Consequences: line comparisons and `Raster_Line` disappear from the runtime", and the superseded plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-11-effects-p1-raster-core.md:272/294/318 which still contain `move.w d1, Raster_Line` / `cmp.w Raster_Line, d0` — the code those lines became no longer does. The runtime confirms it: raster.emp's header states "The runtime never computes a delta and never compares a line number — the schedule IS the program order" (:31-32).
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the field and the `+ 2` term from RASTER_STATE_SIZE. It sits at offset 12, so removing it shifts Raster_Buf_A onward and needs a repin — cheap now, gratuitous churn after the freeze.

findings.title: ship_trailer's documented offset formula uses an 8-byte table stride; the real stride is 10
findings.claim: The comment states the trailer sits at 128 + 2 + 8*records, but patch_table emits FIVE words per record, so the stride is 10 bytes and the documented formula lands inside the last table entry — a reader who trusts it (and the P1 migration will re-derive these offsets) computes the wrong trailer address.
findings.evidence: raster_dsl.emp:1628-1631: "P-b resolves the table at a CONSTANT +128 ... The trailer's own offset is 128 + 2 + 8*records". The emitter directly above it is five words wide: `out = out ++ [src, fire_band_lo(f) - 1, fire_band_hi(f) - 1, 2 * arm_word_index(fires, k), 2 * record_words(f)]` (:1587-1591), and the size annotation agrees — `return 64 + 1 + 5 * fires.len + ship_trailer_words(fires)` (patched_words, :1757). The runtime is correct and says so: "the patch table at RASTER_BUF_SIZE + 2 + 10*records ... TEN BYTES PER ENTRY, AND TEN IS NOT A SHIFT" with `lsl.w #3, d0 / add.w d1, d0 / add.w d1, d0` (engine/effects/raster.emp:935-951). Confirmed against the shipped image: OJZ_TwoChannel (2 records) is 164 bytes = 128 pad-to-buffer + 22 table (2 + 10*2) + 14 trailer, and the trailer's count word $0001 is at byte 150 (s4.bin $1287C + 150), where the documented 128 + 2 + 8*2 = 146 points at the last entry's rec_off word ($001C).
findings.fix_sketch: Change 8 to 10 in the comment at :1629, or state it as `128 + 2 + 10*records` alongside the runtime's note so the two files agree.

coverage_notes:
METHOD. The tree matched HEAD (eeba0ae5) with no code diff against review SHA 48ca8b5d (`git diff --stat 48ca8b5d HEAD -- engine/ games/sonic4/ tools/` = empty), and the gitignored build artifacts s4.bin/s4.lst/s4.debug.bin/s4.debug.lst are timestamped 2026-08-17 15:44-15:45, i.e. the artifacts of commit 48ca8b5d itself (committed 15:45:49, "zero-byte verified crc ab1055d4 unchanged"). Every ROM number below is derived by differencing consecutive symbol addresses in those listings and by reading the actual .bin bytes; every RAM number by differencing the listings' $FFFFxxxx symbols. Where I quote a size I also checked for trailing $00 placer fill inside the span, because section-head differencing measures the placer, not the code (this bit: the plain-vs-debug PRESET delta of 178 vs 174 is entirely 4 bytes of fill at s4.bin $710C). I did NOT build, edit, or touch any emulator tool. I did read (read-only) /home/volence/sonic_hacks/sigil/crates/sigil-harness/src/pins.rs to see which effects labels are pinned; its region bases reproduce the listing exactly, but I derived all sizes from the listings rather than copying pin lengths.

WALKED, IN ORDER. (1) engine/ram.emp — full effects RAM census; derived Raster_State = 318 B ($FFFF8994..$FFFF8AD2) and Palette_State = 472 B ($FFFF8AD2..$FFFF8CAA) field-by-field and confirmed both against the gated RASTER_STATE_SIZE / PALETTE_STATE_SIZE expressions; added BgAnim_LastStep 8, Static_Pal_Ship 14, Palette_Ship_Snap 128, HBlank_Vector_Slot 6. Effects-owned RAM = 940 B (946 with the trampoline slot). No alignment waste found: every longword field is word-aligned, which is all the 68000 needs, and there are no odd-length runs or pads inside either block. (2) engine/effects/raster.emp — op/const surface, the RASTER_STATE_SIZE span guard, Raster_VBlank's copy path, Raster_InstallPatched's trailer arithmetic, Raster_BuildSchedule's per-record recording, Raster_GetChannelBand, Effects_LatchWorldLines/SetWorldY; label-level ROM breakdown of the 850-byte RASTER region (largest bodies: Raster_HInt .dense_body 46, Raster_BuildShipEntry 60, Raster_HInt entry 46; no data tables beyond Raster_Program_None 6 B; no trailing fill). (3) engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp — patch_table (5 words/record), ship_trailer (5 words + one word per SetReg), patched_words, the pad loop, the layout guards; verified the emitted OJZ_TwoChannel image word-by-word (23-word body, 41 words pad, 11-word table, 7-word trailer = 164 B). (4) engine/effects/palette.emp + palette_dsl.emp — 1116-byte PALETTE region label breakdown, PAL_MAX_VARIANTS/PAL_CYCLE_MAX_CHANNELS bounds, Palette_DeriveVariant's line range. (5) engine/effects/preset.emp — EffectsPreset (size: 38): fields are contiguous with no holes, verified against the emitted 38-byte presets; 174 B of code in both shapes. (6) engine/level/bg_anim.emp — 158 B plain / 344 B debug (the +186 is assert.w + raise_error); BgAnim_LastStep = BGANIM_MAX_BANDS(4) x u16 = 8 B, no waste. (7) engine/system/hblank.emp + the vblank seam — 48 B ROM, 6 B RAM slot, nothing to pack. (8) games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp — full per-symbol encoder-output census summing exactly to the 1230-byte region: OJZ_GradientStream 576, presets 5x38=190, OJZ_TwoChannel 164, OJZ_TestPal 96, variants 5x8=40, OJZ_TestRamp 34, OJZ_TestRaster 32, OJZ_WaterRaster 32, OJZ_TestGradient 30, OJZ_TestVsram 28, OJZ_ShimmerCycle 8. Verified data is shape-identical (the 1230-vs-1242 region delta is 12 bytes of debug-shape fill after OJZ_TwoChannel). (9) tools/effects_budget_model.toml + effects_budget_check.py + test_effects_budget_check.py — the [ram] axis and [symbols] resolution. (10) games/sonic4/test/poison/*.emp + README + emp_expect_fail.py + map.toml.

CHARTER ITEMS ANSWERED. Substrate ROM, fill-excluded: 3576 B plain, 3762 B debug (RASTER 850 / PALETTE 1116 / PRESET 174 / BG_ANIM 158-344 / ojz_effects data 1230 / hblank 48). Substrate RAM: 940 B. POISON ROM COST IS ZERO, VERIFIED, not assumed: no `games.sonic4.test.poison.*` module symbol appears in either canonical listing (the only "poison" hits are Variant_Poison, a real variant, and CompressionSelfTest's local .poison labels), no poison file contains a `pub data` or any byte-emitting form, and none is named in map.toml's order. THE "BANK PER-CHANNEL 18B" PIN IS NOT IN THE CODE, and correctly so: that figure is the r3.1 effects-tail design (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-17-effects-tail-design-v3.md:237/267, "two banks x 4 channel words + selector = 18 bytes"), whose Part A is BANKED (DEFERRED_WORK.md:4719, owner ruling 2026-08-17). Today's per-channel state is a single bank: Effects_World_Y [u16;4] = 8 B + Effects_Screen_L [u16;4] = 8 B = 4 bytes per channel over 4 channels, no selector; adopting r3.1 would add 10 B, not 18. Per-band/per-record ROM overhead measured: patch table 10 B per record (5 words), ship trailer 10 B + 2 B per SetReg op, plus a fixed 14 B of framing per sparse program (2 B header + two 4-B priming records + 4 B terminator) — 44% of the 32-byte OJZ_TestRaster is framing, which is a packing opportunity of roughly 4-6 B/program (terminator arm word is always RASTER_ARM_PARK, priming op_counts are always 0) that I judged too small to raise as a finding against the cost of touching the frozen wire format. Per-band parallax RAM (BAND_ENTRY_LEN=10 x MAX_PARALLAX_BANDS=8) was read only for context, per the scope exclusion.

NOT REACHED. (a) No cycle claims verified on hardware — I raised no timing finding, and the one cycle comparison I state (8 vs 96 HInt entries for the gradient) is an entry-count argument from the emitted schedule, not a profiler measurement; a controller should confirm on oracle before acting on it. (b) tools/raster_source_gate.py, raster_off_gate.py, raster_cost_probe.py, effects_scene_assert.py and snapshot_poison_gate.py were read only far enough to establish what fixtures they keep alive and whether they model size — I did not audit their assertions (that is a gate seat's charter). (c) games/demo's effects footprint (sound-off, no effects data) was not measured. (d) I did not attempt to price the ROM/RAM cost of the OP_RUN_RAMP vocabulary as a whole (48 B of handler + 10 B of RAM + 34 B of data currently without a live render); its parked state is declared at ojz_effects.emp:553-559 and deleting a designed op class is an owner call, not a footprint defect.

findings.title: Per-fire cost model omits the 44-cycle IRQ4 autovector entry, so check_density admits fires that overrun their scanline
findings.claim: RASTER_FIRE_BASE_CYC (302) is a POST-ENTRY figure — it excludes the IRQ4 autovector exception entry — so fire_cost_cycles() under-charges every fire by 44 cycles and check_density admits schedules whose real per-fire occupancy exceeds the gap it just proved was sufficient.
findings.evidence:
The constant's own comment enumerates what it covers and the exception entry is not in the list: "The per-fire constant: everything a fire costs that is not an op. The prologue (`ints_off`, the movem, the VDP_CTRL lea, the dense-run test), the arm write, the op_count read, the loop entry and exit, the epilogue and the `rte`." It is anchored on F0 (`RASTER_FIRE_BASE_CYC == 572 / 2 + 16`, :1143), i.e. 286 cycles per priming record.

I hand-counted that exact path off the EMITTED stream (s4.debug.bin, Raster_HInt = $7A36 per s4.debug.lst:1085; the bytes match this source instruction-for-instruction, incl. `720D` = moveq #EFX_RESTORE_DELAY(13) and the five-rung chain ending at OP_PAL_RESTORE, so the artifact is this code):
  $7A36 40E7 MOVE SR,-(SP) 14 · $7A38 46FC2700 MOVE #$2700,SR 16 · $7A3C 48E7C060 MOVEM.L D0-D1/A1-A2,-(SP) 40 · $7A40 45F900C00004 LEA 12 · $7A46 4A788AA6 TST.W (abs.w) 12 · $7A4A 6600 BNE.W nt 12 · $7A4E 22788998 MOVEA.L (abs.w) 16 · 3499 12 · 3019 8 · 0C40FFFF 8 · 6700 BEQ.W nt 12 · 5340 4 · 6B00 BMI.W taken 10 · $7AF4 21C98998 MOVE.L A1,(abs.w) 16 · 6072 BRA.B 10 · $7B6C 4CDF0603 MOVEM.L (SP)+ 44 · 46DF MOVE.W (SP)+,SR 16 · 4E73 RTE 20  =  282 cycles.
282 against the 286 anchor is 4 cycles of slack; the same count WITH the 44-cycle entry is 326, which is 40 cycles above the anchor and cannot be reconciled by any instruction timing in that list (all of them are now byte-verified). So the measurement — oracle's per-routine row, which keys on the handler's entry PC and therefore starts counting at $7A36 — is post-entry, and the model inherited that. The tree even records the missing term as a separate row nothing consumes: tools/effects_budget_model.toml:23 `autovector_entry_cycles = 44  # fixed — IRQ4 autovector exception entry` (grep: no tool or .emp reads it).

Concrete admission failure. Author two adjacent single-word fires:
    fire(M,   [stream_cram($22, [c0])]),
    fire(M+1, [stream_cram($26, [c1])])
check_intervals passes (`ensure(lo_fl > prev_hi)`, :1197 — fire lines M-1 and M are strictly ascending). check_density (:1240 `ensure(cost <= gap * RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC)`) computes gap = 1 and cost = 302+8+18+90+30+10 = 458 <= 488 → ADMITTED, and 458 is the same number pinned as measured for F2/F7 (:1126, :1136). Real occupancy is 44+458 = 502 against a 488-cycle line, so handler k+1 begins 14 cycles after its HInt asserted, and because each HInt asserts on the hardware's own schedule the deficit ACCUMULATES: fire n's burst lands 14n cycles (~12n pixels) later in the row than fire 1's. That is precisely the progressive mid-row shift DENSITY-EVIDENCE already measured for the cram3 shape ("transitions at x = 232/248/294 of 320", quoted at :1207) — the guard refuses it at 3 words and admits it at 1. The same omission is what makes tools/effects_budget_model.toml's `adjacent_fire_verdict = "vsram1 OK adjacent"` false: F7 = 458 modelled/measured, 502 real. Nothing currently shipped triggers it (every OJZ fire is >= 20 lines from its neighbour; games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp:115, :412, :638-640), so this is latent — which is exactly what the P1 freeze would make load-bearing.

Second-order note, same direction: all of these are nominal cycles. During active display the 68000 also loses bus cycles to VDP fetches, so nothing offsets the 44.
findings.fix_sketch: Add the entry as an explicit term: `pub const RASTER_EXCEPTION_ENTRY_CYC = 44` and start fire_cost_cycles at RASTER_FIRE_BASE_CYC + RASTER_EXCEPTION_ENTRY_CYC (:1103), leaving the eight F-series pins comparing against measured+44 so each pin still names its measurement. Then re-check the two which-side-of-the-line ensures (:1156-1169) and the `adjacent_fire_verdict` row — 502 > 488 flips the vsram/1-word-cram adjacency verdict to "space them", which is the behaviour change the guard is for.

findings.title: Opcode dispatch is a 5-rung compare chain: OP_SET_REG and OP_PAL_RESTORE pay 80/82 cycles of pure dispatch, and the comment justifying the chain is stale
findings.claim: The compare chain costs 16 cycles per failed rung and has grown to five rungs, so the two ops whose landing position matters most (OP_SET_REG, the fall-through, and OP_PAL_RESTORE at depth 4) spend 80 and 82 cycles reaching their bodies — more than 3x a pc-indexed table's 24 — while the in-code justification still asserts the opposite.
findings.evidence:
The chain, verified byte-for-byte at $7A64-$7A84 (five `0C41 000x` CMPI.W #imm,D1 = 8 cyc each, each followed by a `67xx` BEQ.B = 8 cyc not taken):
  $7A66 0C410002/6720 · $7A6C 0C410004/6734 · $7A72 0C410006/6754 · $7A78 0C410008/6760 · $7A7E 0C41000A/6776 · $7A84 3499 (the SET_REG write itself)
So SET_REG = 5*16 = 80 cycles of dispatch, OP_PAL_RESTORE = 4*16+18 = 82, OP_RUN_RAMP = 66, OP_RUN_GRADIENT = 50, OP_PAL_REGION = 34, OP_CRAM = 18. raster_dsl.emp:1046 and the model rows charge exactly this.

The comment at :707-713 says "Three-op compare chain rather than a pc-indexed jump table: at this few opcodes it is fewer cycles than the table setup". There are six opcodes now, not three, and the cycle claim is false for everything past depth 1: the opcodes are already 2-byte spaced (0,2,4,6,8,10 — raster.emp:94-187), which is exactly a BRA.B table index, so `jmp .tab(pc,d1.w)` (JMP d8(An,Xn) = 14) + `bra.s` (10) = 24 cycles FLAT. Net per op: SET_REG -56, PAL_RESTORE -58, RUN_RAMP -42, RUN_GRADIENT -26, PAL_REGION -10, OP_CRAM +6.

Measured consequence on shipped content: the OJZ water fire is `reg_sh_on() + stream_pal_region` (ojz_effects.emp:638, modelled 660 cyc in effects_budget_model.toml) and spends 80+34 = 114 of those cycles deciding which body to run; a table makes it 48, a 66-cycle (10%) cut on the single most expensive shipped fire. The R1 restore fire (F8 = 704 modelled/measured, 1.44 scanlines) drops to 646.

The REAL blocker is named two lines later — "a computed `jmp` defeats the contract-closure dataflow" — and that is a toolchain constraint, not a cycle one. Also note the depth pins carry an explicit trap for this shape (raster_dsl.emp:1034-1038: appending opcode 12 silently under-charges every SetReg by 16 cyc/rung); a flat table would make that whole hazard class unrepresentable.
findings.fix_sketch: Either (a) reorder the chain by measured frequency so SET_REG is not the fall-through — reg_sh_on appears in the shipped water band and in fx_sh_below, and raster_dsl.emp:1039 already warns a reorder invalidates the depth derivation, so the four depth literals must be re-spelled by hand and F1/F5 re-measured; or (b) take the pc-indexed table and record the contract-closure cost as the reason the chain existed. In either case correct the "three-op" comment at raster.emp:707 — as written it will be re-read as a cycle ruling by the next author.

findings.title: Dense per-line body carries ~44 cycles of redundant/loop-invariant work at 82% scanline occupancy, and the dense tier has no build-time cost guard at all
findings.claim: The every-line dense body re-writes an already-correct reg $0A, re-tests a run-invariant mode flag, and streams to VDP_DATA through abs.l while a2 already points 4 bytes past it — ~44 recoverable cycles of a 402-cycle line — and unlike the sparse tier nothing in the build models or bounds this cost.
findings.evidence:
Byte-verified dense gradient body at $7B20 (`.dense_body`):
  34BC8A00 MOVE.W #$8A00,(A2) 12 · 24B88AAC MOVE.L (abs.w),(A2) 24 · 4A788AB0 TST.W (abs.w) 12 · 6620 BNE.B nt 8 · 22788AA8 MOVEA.L 16 · 33D900C00000 x3 = 60 · 21C98AA8 MOVE.L A1,(abs.w) 16 · 53788AA6 SUBQ.W 16 · 601E BRA.B 10  = 174, plus prologue 104 ($7A36..$7A4A with the BNE taken) and epilogue 80 = 358 post-entry, 402 including the 44-cycle autovector entry — 82% of a 488-cycle NTSC line, the thinnest per-line margin in the suite.
Three items in that 174:
1. `move.w #RASTER_ARM_EVERY_LINE, (a2)` (:828) is provably redundant, 12 cyc/line. reg $0A is ALREADY 0 on every path that reaches here: raster_gradient_program/raster_ramp_program author both rgp_arm1 and rgp_arm2 as RASTER_ARM_EVERY_LINE (:366-368, :459-461), the setup fire writes it through the ordinary record walk, and the VDP reloads 0 at every underflow, so nothing can perturb it during the run. The DSL cannot author a dense op inside a patched program (RasterOp has no dense variant — raster_dsl.emp:1044-1052), which is the only shape whose builder-computed arm byte would make the write load-bearing.
2. `tst.w Raster_Dense_Kind` + `bne.s` (:834-835) is 20-22 cyc/line to re-answer a question fixed at ENTER — Dense_Kind is written only by .op_run_gradient/.op_run_ramp (:773, :786).
3. The stream writes (:837-839, and :852 in .ramp_body) use `VDP_DATA` as abs.l = 20/16 cycles, but a2 still holds VDP_CTRL ($C00004) and is never repurposed in these bodies (byte-verified: 33D9 00C00000 with a2 untouched). `-4(a2)` is d16(An) = 16/12 → 12 cyc/line on the gradient body, 4 on the ramp body. The same 4 cyc/word applies to `.cram_loop` (:737, $7A96 33D900C00000, a2 still VDP_CTRL) = 12 cycles off every 3-colour sparse fire, i.e. RASTER_STREAM_WORD_CYC 30 -> 26.
Total recoverable on a gradient line: 12 + 20 + 12 = 44 of 402 (11%). The dense tier measures 41579 cyc/frame at 32.5% for a 96-line run (effects_budget_model.toml [raster.dense]), so this is the largest single recoverable number in the suite (~4500 cyc/frame).
And nothing guards the total: raster_gradient_program/raster_ramp_program run no cycle ensure (raster.emp:342-377, :429-471), the DSL's op_cost_cycles match has no RunGradient/RunRamp arm, and effects_budget_check.py gates only the [symbols] rows — none of which is a [raster.dense] row. So the tier sitting at 82% of a scanline is the one with no pin, no fixture, and no ensure, immediately before a byte-identity freeze whose whole premise is that the shared prologue may be restructured.
findings.fix_sketch: Drop the redundant arm write and hoist the Dense_Kind test out of the per-line path (e.g. store the body's address at ENTER, or split Dense_Lines into two counters — the comment at :831-833 traded these 32 cycles for code size without a measurement); switch the three unrolled writes and .cram_loop to -4(a2). Separately, add the missing gate: a dense_line_cost model term plus an `ensure(dense_line_cycles <= RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC)` and a [raster.dense] [symbols] row, so a prologue change during the P1 migration fails the build instead of silently skewing every line of the run.

findings.title: Raster_BuildSchedule re-records the whole schedule every VBlank with no change detection, plus loop-invariant reloads per record
findings.claim: The builder pays its full 1228-cycle measured cost inside the VBlank z80/DMA-flag bracket on every physical frame including lag frames, even when its inputs are unchanged and the output is bit-identical, and it recomputes the template base once per record.
findings.evidence:
`proc Raster_BuildSchedule ()` early-outs only on `move.l Raster_Patch_Tab, d0 / beq .none` (:1102-1103) — liveness, never staleness. Its entire input is the patch table (static ROM) and Effects_Screen_L[RASTER_MAX_PATCH] latched once per frame by Effects_LatchWorldLines (:1289-1299), so a frame on which no channel's screen line moved reproduces the same bytes and the same swap. Measured cost from tools/effects_budget_model.toml [raster.schedule_build]: "Raster_PatchAll 372 cyc -> Raster_BuildSchedule 1228 cyc (+856)" for 2 records, with "VInt_Level 7499 -> 8421", and it runs on BOTH VInt_Level and VInt_Lag (vblank.emp:157, :291) inside the sound-ON DMA-flag / sound-OFF `z80_stopped` bracket — the scarcest window in the engine. A 4-word compare of the latched bank against a previous-frame copy is ~40 cycles against 1228, and skipping is the same answer (Active_Buf stays put and Raster_VBlank rewinds the cursor into it either way).
Within the loop, two reloads are invariant: `movea.l Raster_Patch_Tab, a2` + `suba.w #RASTER_BUF_SIZE, a2` (:1154-1155 = 16+12 = 28 cyc/record) recomputes the template base every iteration, and `lea Effects_Screen_L, a2` (:1132 = 8 cyc) is re-taken per patchable record. The 8-byte stack frame the proc already allocates (:1104) has room for the template base, which is the same reasoning its own STACK SCRATCH note (:1091-1095) uses for the two arm-slot pointers.
findings.fix_sketch: Gate the rebuild on a cheap dirty test (memcmp of the RASTER_MAX_PATCH-word Effects_Screen_L bank against a shadow written at the end of the build; force-dirty on install, i.e. wherever Raster_Patch_Tab is set). Hoist the template base into the existing stack frame. Both are VBlank-window cycles, so they trade directly against DMA_Budget_Remaining.

findings.title: Every stream op in a fire pays its own blanking spin, though only the first burst can be in the window the spin exists to reach
findings.claim: EFX_BLANK_DELAY/EFX_RESTORE_DELAY are spun per OP, so a fire with two stream ops burns 58 (or 148) cycles positioning a burst that is already past the offscreen window by construction — pushing it further into active display rather than out of it.
findings.evidence: `.op_cram` (:730-735) and `.op_region` (:750-753) each open with `moveq #EFX_BLANK_DELAY, d1` / self-`dbf` = 4 + (4*10+14) = 58 cycles, and `.op_pal_restore` (:808-810) with EFX_RESTORE_DELAY = 13 = 4 + 144 = 148. Byte-verified: $7A8E 7204/51C9FFFE, $7AA8 7204/51C9FFFE, $7AFC 720D/51C9FFFE. The spin's stated purpose is singular — "burn a cycle-counted delay so the colour writes below land in HBlank (offscreen)" — and the R1 calibration note (:797-806) fixes it against a measured landing position for the FIRST burst of a fire. A second stream op in the same fire starts ~150-260 cycles later, i.e. already inside the following row's active display, so its 58/148-cycle spin cannot park anything and moves its burst further right. Cost is certain and measured in the model's own pin: F6, two 1-word stream_cram ops in one fire, 614 cycles (raster_dsl.emp:1134) of which 116 is spin. Nothing forbids the shape — check_mixed_fire only constrains SetReg ordering (raster_dsl.emp:1292-1311) — but no shipped program has two stream ops in one fire today (ojz_effects.emp:115, :412, :638-640 and every poison fixture carry at most one), so this is latent.
findings.fix_sketch: Spin once per FIRE rather than per op (hoist the delay to the top of .op_loop's first stream dispatch, or set a per-fire flag in d0's high half) — or, if the second burst's position is genuinely wanted where it lands, say so at the spin and have check_density charge it as a positioning cost. The artifact direction should be confirmed with one oracle landing capture before choosing; the 58/148-cycle cost needs no capture.

coverage_notes: Reverse (handler-first) walk, in order: (1) engine/system/hblank.emp trampoline + HBlankHandler contract; (2) engine/irq.emp to price `ints_off` (acquire 30 / release 16, cross-checked against vblank.emp:394's own \"46 cy — 14+16+16\"); (3) engine/effects/raster.emp Raster_HInt in full — prologue, sparse record walk, 6-op dispatch chain, .op_cram / .op_region / .op_pal_restore bodies, both dense bodies, .advance/.park/epilogue. I then VERIFIED the whole handler against the EMITTED stream: s4.debug.lst:1085-1102 gives Raster_HInt = $7A36 and every local label, and I decoded s4.debug.bin $7A36-$7B73 instruction by instruction. That settled three things I would otherwise have had to assume: RAM operands are abs.w throughout (so an \"abs.w would be cheaper\" finding I was drafting is dead and is not reported), the intra-handler branch sizes (BNE.W/BEQ.W/BMI.W at the top, BEQ.B for all five dispatch rungs), and EFX_RESTORE_DELAY=13 is live — which also confirms the artifact matches the reviewed tree (HEAD's two commits after 48ca8b5d are docs-only). Every cycle number in my findings is from that byte-verified stream plus the M68000 timing tables, and my hand count of the priming-record path (282 cyc) reproduces the model's own F0 anchor (286) to 4 cycles, which is what makes the 44-cycle exception-entry finding a measurement about the model rather than a guess.\n(4) Outward to arm/schedule: Raster_VBlank (install path, the 64-word copy, dense-counter rewind, per-frame HBlank_Install), Raster_BuildSchedule per-record cost, Raster_GetChannelBand, Effects_LatchWorldLines, Effects_SetWorldY. (5) VBlank-side install/publish: Raster_InstallPatched, Raster_BuildShipEntry, and the preset.emp seam (confirmed Effects_InstallPreset is per-crossing, not per-frame, which is why the install-path copy cost is not reported). (6) Palette: Palette_Compose's early-out and layer order, DoCycle/RotateSpan skim, DoFade's 48-word body (per-frame only while a fade is armed; not per-scanline, so not pursued). (7) engine/level/bg_anim.emp end to end — I walked the (a3) cursor arithmetic on all four exit paths (full, .skip_band, .queue_full, DMA2-bcs) against sizeof(bganim_band)=44 and it balances on every path; no perf or correctness finding. (8) The model/gate layer: raster_dsl.emp:920-1350 (cost model, fixture pins, which-side-of-the-line ensures, check_intervals, check_density, check_mixed_fire, band() minima), tools/effects_budget_model.toml in full, tools/effects_budget_check.py's gating mechanism. (9) Authored ground truth: ojz_effects.emp fires and games/sonic4/test/poison/*.emp fires, to decide live vs latent for each finding.\nNOT REACHED: raster_dsl.emp lines 1-920 (constructor/encoder bodies, op_size/op_mask/patch_table emission) beyond what the cost model and band() needed; palette_dsl.emp; palette.emp's DoOperator and DeriveVariant at instruction level (the derive is the suite's historic 15.1% cost, now gated by PAL_ACT_VARIANT_STALE — I read the gate but did not price the loop); tools/raster_source_gate.py, raster_off_gate.py, raster_cost_probe.py, effects_scene_assert.py, test_effects_budget_check.py internals (gate-integrity is another seat's lane and I only used the model file as a cost authority); parallax touchpoints beyond Raster_GetChannelBand's contract, per the out-of-scope rule. No emulator tool was used and nothing was built, edited, or committed; the .lst/.bin were read only.

findings.title: Off-screen ship engages only at L<=0 while BuildSchedule clamps for L<=band_lo-1 — uncovered window whose width is the author's `lo`
findings.claim: The frame-top off-screen ship's trigger (`latched screen line <= 0`) and Raster_BuildSchedule's fire-line clamp floor (`band_lo_fl`) are two independently-authored thresholds with no `ensure` relating them, so for 0 < L < band_lo the boundary is silently pinned at band_lo with no ship covering the rows above it — a stripe up to `band_lo - 1` rows tall.
findings.evidence:
buffers.emp:407-409 gates the ship on the sign of the latched line only:
```
        lea     Effects_Screen_L, a1
        tst.w   (a1, d0.w)                      // the LATCHED line
        bgt     .no_ship                        // still on screen: the fire owns the boundary
```
`bgt` is signed, so the ship runs iff L <= 0. But raster.emp:1135-1139 clamps for every L below the floor:
```
        cmp.w   2(a0), d2                   // band_hi_fl
        bgt     .suppress
        cmp.w   (a0), d2                    // band_lo_fl
        bge     .have_line
        move.w  (a0), d2                    // clamp UP
```
d2 = L-1, so the clamp engages for all L <= band_lo (i.e. d2 < band_lo_fl = lo-1). Walk with OJZ_TwoChannel (ojz_effects.emp:638-639, `ch:0, lo:3, hi:220, offscreen_ship:1`) and Camera_Y such that L = 1: the author's boundary is row 1; the record clamps to fire line 2 so CRAM changes from row 3; the ship is skipped because 1 > 0 -> rows 1-2 render base. Two rows. The two authorities also state different intents for the same mechanism: raster_dsl.emp:100 says "when this channel's anchor leaves the TOP of the screen", while buffers.emp:420-421 says "the ship exists because the fire's line clamps into its band, so the rows above that line never see the fire" — those diverge exactly on 0 < L < band_lo. The amplifier is that `patchable` permits any floor: raster_dsl.emp:388 `ensure(lo >= 3 && hi <= 223)`. raster.emp:1203-1204 records that channel 0 "was 40..120 until the lo clamp was seen pinning the boundary 40 lines down" — i.e. the symptom was fixed by lowering `lo` to 3, not by fixing the threshold, and nothing stops the next author from writing `lo: 40` again and reinstating a 39-row uncovered stripe. GATE BLINDNESS: the three committed fixtures sample L = -44 / 100 / 230 only (tools/scenes/effects_raster_above_screen.json Camera_Y 144 / Effects_World_Y 100; mid_band 244; suppressed 374), so the window is never entered; and even if it were, tools/effects_gates.py:72-95 `derive_arms` asserts only the ARM WORDS and models the clamp itself (`max(l0, lo0) - 1`), so it would predict the same (correct) arm and pass. No gate in the suite reads CRAM or pixels — raster_off_gate reads the trampoline/IE1, raster_source_gate reads a2 at `.region_loop` — and oracle CRAM is frame-latched so the mid-frame boundary is unobservable in principle.
findings.fix_sketch: Ship whenever the record was clamped, not only when L <= 0: compare the latched line against the channel's band floor (available via Raster_GetChannelBand, or carry band_lo_fl in the ship trailer beside the channel word) — `cmp.w band_lo_screen, L; bge .no_ship`. If the L<=0 semantic is deliberate, add a comptime `ensure` in `patchable` tying `offscreen_ship == 1` to a small `lo` (e.g. lo <= RASTER_MIN_FIRE_LINE) so the uncovered window is bounded by the build, and delete the contradictory purpose statement at buffers.emp:420-421.

findings.title: Off-screen ship's drop guard hardcodes CRAM line 2; the ship's line is per-program authorable (1..3)
findings.claim: The ship's "did the base reload drop?" guard tests `Palette_Dirty` bit 2 unconditionally, but the shipping fire's CRAM line comes from its own `stream_pal_region` op and may legally be line 1 or 3 — so the guard interrogates a line unrelated to the ship and both directions of the mismatch are reachable.
findings.fix_sketch: Derive the bit from the ship entry itself — the trailer already carries the CRAM byte address at `6(a2)`; use `addr >> 5` as the bit number for a `btst dN, Palette_Dirty` (or equivalently test the installed program's pal_dirty_mask, which is word 0 of the live buffer). Alternatively add an `ensure` in `patchable` pinning `offscreen_ship == 1` fires to CRAM line 2 and say so at buffers.emp:402.

findings.title: Pal_Variant_Stage is rewritten from the main loop while Raster_HInt streams it during active display — torn variant read
findings.claim: Palette_DeriveVariant writes Pal_Variant_Stage entry-by-entry from main-loop context, and Raster_HInt's OP_PAL_REGION reads 1-3 words out of the same bytes during active display with no interlock, so a fire landing inside the derive streams a mix of the previous and current frame's variant image.
findings.evidence:
Writer, main loop (GameLoop -> Palette_Compose -> Palette_DoVariants -> Palette_DeriveVariant), palette.emp:736 inside the 16-entry-per-line loop:
```
        move.w  d4, (a3)+
        dbf     d7, .entry
```
Reader, raw IRQ4 context during active display, raster.emp:755-759:
```
        lea     Pal_Variant_Stage, a2   // staging base (was VDP_CTRL)
        adda.w  (a1)+, a2               // + comptime offset -> the derived colours
    .region_loop:
        move.w  (a2)+, VDP_DATA
```
GameLoop (engine/system/game_loop.emp:49) calls Palette_Compose during active display, after the state dispatch and before VSync_Wait, so the two overlap by construction. The derive is only entered when PAL_ACT_VARIANT_STALE is set (palette.emp:383-386), i.e. exactly on the frames when the staging bytes actually change — so every tear is a real value change, not a no-op. Concrete walk: cross from OJZ section 0 into section 2. Parallax_CheckBoundary -> Effects_InstallPreset (parallax.emp:194ff) runs inside the state dispatch and calls Palette_LoadPal(OJZ_TestPal) (preset.emp:257), setting Pal_Base_Dirty. Palette_Compose then runs later in the SAME tick, base-copies OJZ_TestPal into Palette_Buffer and re-derives Variant_Water_Deep — while the OUTGOING program OJZ_TwoChannel (ojz_effects.emp:569, still the live raster program until the next VBlank) is firing its stream_pal_region on slot 0. The fire streams 3 words that may straddle the derive's write cursor, so the water band shows a mix of OJZ_Palette-derived and OJZ_TestPal-derived colours for that frame. The same race exists every rotation tick in section 3 (OJZ_ShimmerCycle sets the stale bit via palette.emp:356). GATE BLINDNESS: the only observable is CRAM content at a specific scanline. raster_source_gate observes the source ADDRESS a2 (its own docstring: "asserts the address Raster_HInt ACTUALLY streams from"), not the bytes there; effects_scene_assert asserts program words; the replay net emits no framebuffer; oracle CRAM reads are frame-latched so a mid-frame mixed palette is invisible even with a pinned camera.
findings.fix_sketch: Either derive into the inactive half of a double-buffered staging image and publish the base with a single move.l that OP_PAL_REGION's `lea` reads (costs 256 B of RAM and a comptime offset that is now slot-relative), or move Palette_DoVariants into the VBlank tail where the HInt is masked at IPL 6 (costs the derive's ~19k cycles inside the blanking window, so probably only viable with the double buffer). At minimum, document the tear as a known one-frame residual beside the PAL_ACT_VARIANT_STALE note, since the migration freeze makes this substrate.

findings.title: Cycle script channel_count is unbounded at runtime — >PAL_CYCLE_MAX_CHANNELS overruns Pal_Cycle_Timers into the palette engine's scalar state
findings.claim: Neither Palette_LoadCycle nor Palette_DoCycle bounds a script's channel_count against PAL_CYCLE_MAX_CHANNELS (4), and Pal_Cycle_Timers is exactly 4 bytes followed immediately by the palette engine's control scalars, so a count of 5+ writes cycle timers over Pal_Fade_Frames / Pal_Op / Pal_Op_Step / Pal_Op_Timer / Pal_Active.
findings.evidence:
palette.emp:306-314 zeroes `count` bytes with no ceiling:
```
        move.w  (a1)+, d0                       // channel_count
        subq.w  #1, d0
        bmi   .done
        ori.b   #PAL_ACT_CYCLE, Pal_Active
        lea     Pal_Cycle_Timers, a1
        moveq   #0, d1
    .zero:
        move.b  d1, (a1)+
        dbf     d0, .zero
```
and palette.emp:419-426 indexes the same array by an unbounded channel index (`tst.b (a3, d5.w)`, `move.b d3, (a3, d5.w)`, `subq.b #1, (a3, d5.w)`). engine/ram.emp:401-411 puts the scalars directly after the array:
```
    Pal_Cycle_Timers:   [u8; 4],    // PAL_CYCLE_MAX_CHANNELS per-channel frame countdown
    Pal_Fade_Frames:    u8,
    Pal_Op:             u8,
    Pal_Op_Step:        u8,
    Pal_Op_Timer:       u8,
    Pal_Active:         u8,
```
Walk with a hand-authored 6-channel script: the `.zero` loop clears Pal_Fade_Frames and Pal_Op; then on the first compose Palette_DoCycle writes channel 5's `pc_period` into Pal_Op — a period of 1..4 lands exactly on PAL_OP_FADE_BLACK..PAL_OP_NEG_FLASH, arming a global operator with Pal_Op_Step = channel 6's period, i.e. the palette engine starts fading or flashing from a cycling script. The DSL wrappers only reach 2 (palette_dsl.emp:107-118) so this is hand-authored-data-only today, but PAL_CYCLE_MAX_CHANNELS = 4 advertises 4 as legal and the wire format is a bare `dc.w channel_count` walked verbatim. The sibling table walk in engine/level/bg_anim.emp:118 does carry a backstop (`assert.w d7, ls, #BGANIM_MAX_BANDS`) for precisely this class; this one has none, in DEBUG or release. GATE BLINDNESS: no fixture authors a >2-channel script (none can be built through the DSL), and the corruption target is RAM scalars, not pixels or arm words — nothing in effects_gates, raster_off_gate or effects_scene_assert reads Palette_State.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `assert.w d0, ls, #PAL_CYCLE_MAX_CHANNELS` (DEBUG backstop, mirroring bg_anim.emp:118) in Palette_LoadCycle right after the count read, plus a release-side `cmpi/bhi .done` clamp given the count is read from data; and give palette_dsl a `cycle_script4` (or an explicit ensure) so the declared cap and the authorable cap agree.

findings.title: Flash operators restore from Pal_Base, which is not the live palette when cycling has rotated spans in place
findings.claim: PAL_OP_WHITE_FLASH / PAL_OP_NEG_FLASH end by forcing a base recompose from Pal_Base, but Palette_RotateSpan mutates Palette_Buffer in place and never writes back to Pal_Base, so the restore silently discards the accumulated cycle phase (and, during a cross-fade, the interpolated state).
findings.evidence:
palette.emp:638-645:
```
    .op_done_restore:
        // flash over: idle the op and force a base recompose to restore the palette.
        move.b  #PAL_OP_NONE, Pal_Op
        andi.b  #~PAL_ACT_OP, Pal_Active
        move.b  #1, Pal_Base_Dirty
        move.b  #%1110, Pal_Compose_Lines
        ori.b   #PAL_ACT_BASE, Pal_Active
```
Palette_RotateSpan operates on Palette_Buffer only (palette.emp:447 `lea Palette_Buffer, a1`, then the in-place `.fwd` / `.rup` shifts); nothing copies the rotated result back into Pal_Base. Walk in OJZ section 3 (OJZ_Preset_Sec3 installs OJZ_ShimmerCycle, ojz_effects.emp:574): after N rotations Palette_Buffer's shimmer span is N steps out of phase with Pal_Base. Fire a white flash; on its last frame `.op_done_restore` sets Pal_Base_Dirty, and the next Palette_Compose's `.base` arm (palette.emp:343-348) copies the UNROTATED Pal_Base over lines 1-3 — the shimmer jumps back to phase 0 while Pal_Cycle_Timers keeps counting from wherever it was. The same restore is wrong mid-cross-fade: Pal_Base is the fade's start endpoint, so the palette snaps back toward the outgoing section's colours and then jumps to Target at the fade's final `.snap` (palette.emp:488-499). Fully latent: `Palette_SetOp` has no caller in the tree (grep over engine/ + games/ finds only its definition and preset.emp's comment), which is also why nothing can catch it. GATE BLINDNESS: no gate arms an operator at all, and the observable is palette content across frames — the replay net is pixel-blind and oracle CRAM is frame-latched, so even a hand-driven flash would need a per-frame CRAM diff nobody has.
findings.fix_sketch: Have the flash operators snapshot Palette_Buffer lines 1-3 before the first fill and restore from that snapshot (or suppress the flash arm while PAL_ACT_CYCLE / PAL_ACT_FADE is set) instead of routing through Pal_Base. If restoring from Pal_Base is intended, make Palette_RotateSpan rotate Pal_Base too so base and buffer stay phase-consistent.

findings.title: Two stale comments describe the ship trailer's stride and element shape wrongly, at the sites a future edit would consult
findings.claim: The trailer's own emitter documents its offset with the pre-P-b 8-word stride, and the runtime reader documents its element as a built 14-byte DMAEntry; both are wrong and both sit exactly where someone changing the trailer would read.
findings.evidence:
raster_dsl.emp:1628-1631 (ship_trailer's own doc): "IT GOES AFTER THE PATCH TABLE ... The trailer's own offset is 128 + 2 + 8*records" — but a patch-table entry is FIVE words since local removal (raster_dsl.emp:1566-1576, `[line_src][band_lo_fl][band_hi_fl][rec_off][rec_len]`), and the runtime computes 10n:
```
        move.w  (a1), d0                        // record count
        move.w  d0, d1
        lsl.w   #3, d0                          // 8n
        add.w   d1, d0                          // 9n
        add.w   d1, d0                          // 10n — the table's byte length
```
(raster.emp:949-953, whose own note says "TEN BYTES PER ENTRY, AND TEN IS NOT A SHIFT"). Separately raster.emp:934 states the trailer element as "[n (word)][channel (word)][DMAEntry (14 bytes)]", which contradicts both ship_trailer's actual emission (raster_dsl.emp:1651-1655: channel, stage off, colour count, CRAM addr, reg count, reg words) and Raster_BuildShipEntry's own header (raster.emp:1018-1024: "THE TRAILER CARRIES PARAMETERS RATHER THAN A BUILT ENTRY"). Failure mode: the 8n figure is the number a reader would reproduce when adding a second shipping channel (raster_dsl.emp:1663-1664 explicitly invites that edit), and an 8n reader lands 2n bytes short of the count word — inside the patch table — so `tst.w` reads a rec_len as the trailer count and the install publishes a garbage Effects_Offscreen_Entry that Enqueue_Dirty_Buffers turns into a frame-top CRAM DMA. Nothing detects the drift: the emitted-image pin (ojz_effects.emp:724-726) compares the trailer against a hand twin, not against any prose, and no gate parses comments.
findings.fix_sketch: Correct raster_dsl.emp:1630 to `128 + 2 + 10*records`, and replace raster.emp:934's "[DMAEntry (14 bytes)]" with the real element list ([channel][stage off][colour count][CRAM addr][reg count][reg words...]). Better: name the 10 once as a comptime const shared by patch_table's stride, ship_trailer's offset doc and the runtime's 8n+n+n derive.

findings.title: RASTER_BUF_SIZE/2 is a bare `64` in the encoder while the runtime derives it
findings.claim: The 128-byte working-buffer size is spelled as a derived expression on the runtime side (`RASTER_BUF_SIZE / 2`, `suba.w #RASTER_BUF_SIZE`) but as an unpinned literal `64` in four encoder/author sites across two files, so a change to RASTER_BUF_SIZE can leave the patched-template padding at the old width and mis-base the patch table the runtime reads.
findings.evidence:
Runtime side derives: engine/effects/raster.emp:242 `pub const RASTER_BUF_SIZE = 128`; :575 `move.w  #(RASTER_BUF_SIZE / 2) - 1, d1`; :930 `lea RASTER_BUF_SIZE(a0), a1`; :1118 and :1155 `suba.w  #RASTER_BUF_SIZE, a2        // the template body sits before its table`.

Encoder side hardcodes: raster_dsl.emp:1761 `return 64 + 1 + 5 * fires.len + ship_trailer_words(fires)`; :1776 `comptime var pad = 64 - out.len`; :1778 `"patched_program: the program body is {out.len} words, which does not fit the 64-word buffer the runtime copies"`. Author side hardcodes it again: games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp:714 `ensure(patched_words(OJZ_TC_PROG) == 64 + OJZ_TC_TABLE_HAND.len + OJZ_TC_TRAILER_HAND.len, ...)` and :721 `const OJZ_TC_PAD = comptime for i in 0..(64 - 23) { 0 }`.

The module's own pin, raster_dsl.emp:40 `ensure(RASTER_BUF_SIZE == 128, "raster_dsl's inlined buffer bound drifted from RASTER_BUF_SIZE")`, is worded against the `128`s (:1527's guard message spells "exceeds RASTER_BUF_SIZE (128)") and names nothing that leads to the `64`s. Grepping either `128` or `RASTER_BUF_SIZE` finds every site EXCEPT those four.

FAILURE WALK. Raise RASTER_BUF_SIZE to 160 (the cost probe already records the 128-byte cap as what bounds its fixtures: raster_cost_probe.py:146 `f"program is {len(out) * 2} bytes, over RASTER_BUF_SIZE (128)"`). The :40 ensure fires; the maintainer updates :40 and :1527's `128`s. `patched_program` still pads to 64 words = 128 bytes, so `patch_table` lands at body+128. `Raster_InstallPatched` (raster.emp:930) now computes the table pointer as body+160 — 32 bytes INTO the table — and `Raster_BuildSchedule` (:1118) recovers the body as table-160, i.e. 32 bytes BEFORE the real body. It then reads `move.w (a2)+, (a1)+` as pal_dirty_mask and `move.l (a2)+, (a1)+` twice as the two priming records from whatever `data` precedes the template, and copies record bodies from `Raster_Patch_Tab - 160 + rec_off`. Raster_HInt walks those bytes as arm words and opcodes inside a raw IRQ4 handler, every frame. Nothing at build time refuses it: patched_words agrees with patched_program's length because both use the stale 64, and the OJZ hand pins are written against 64 too, so the ensures at ojz_effects.emp:714/722/724 all pass.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `pub const RASTER_BUF_WORDS = RASTER_BUF_SIZE / 2` beside raster.emp:242, add it to raster_dsl.emp's existing `use engine.effects.raster.{...}` list (:30-31 already pulls RASTER_BUF_SIZE), and replace the `64`s at raster_dsl.emp:1761/1776 with it. Derive OJZ_TC_PAD from `RASTER_BUF_WORDS - OJZ_TC_HAND.len`; the existing `ensure(OJZ_TC_HAND.len == 23)` then becomes redundant.
