findings.title: BGANIM_MAX_BANDS exists in four hand-synced places with no gate and no span guard
findings.claim: The band-count ceiling is written four times — a pub const, a module-local const, an unrolled two-longword init, and a Python assert in the generator — and unlike the analogous RASTER_MAX_PATCH there is no span guard on BgAnim_LastStep, so a raise in the generator alone lets BgAnim_Update walk past the array into the static DMA entries in the RELEASE shape.
findings.evidence:
Copy 1 — engine/system/constants.emp:205 `pub const BGANIM_MAX_BANDS = 4`, whose own note admits the sync is manual: :203-204 `// Collapsing the two needs a comptime ram->code import path that does not exist. KEEP THE TWO IN SYNC BY HAND (both are 4).`
Copy 2 — engine/level/bg_anim.emp:48 `const BGANIM_MAX_BANDS = 4`.
Copy 3 — engine/level/bg_anim.emp:87-89, undocumented and not mentioned by the sync note:
```
        moveq   #-1, d0
        move.l  d0, BgAnim_LastStep             // (BgAnim_LastStep).w
        move.l  d0, BgAnim_LastStep + 4         // (BgAnim_LastStep+4).w
```
two longwords = exactly 4 words = exactly BGANIM_MAX_BANDS, by coincidence of the current value only.
Copy 4 — tools/inject_editor_bg.py:48 `assert len(anims) <= 4, 'engine supports at most BGANIM_MAX_BANDS=4 bands'` — the value in the comparison AND in the message string; bg_anim.emp:121 designates this the release defence: `// emitter's <= 4 assert is the release defense`.

No gate ties any pair. Contrast RASTER_MAX_PATCH, where ram.emp's literal `[u16; 4]` IS held, by a measured span guard: raster.emp:258-260 `pub const RASTER_STATE_SIZE = ... (2 * RASTER_MAX_PATCH) ...` / `ensure((extern("Raster_State_End") - extern("Raster_State")) == RASTER_STATE_SIZE, ...)`, with :251-256 stating that this is exactly what holds ram.emp's literal. BgAnim_LastStep has no such bracket: engine/ram.emp:410 is `mark Palette_State_End,`, :413 `BgAnim_LastStep: [u16; BGANIM_MAX_BANDS],` sits OUTSIDE both the Palette_State and Raster_State spans, and :416 `Static_Pal_Line0: [u8; sizeof(DMAEntry)],` follows immediately.

FAILURE WALK. Someone authoring a 6-band act raises the generator's assert to 6 — the fastest-looking edit, since it is the thing that refused them and its message names a constant whose two definitions are not visible from there. The generated table's count word is 6. In the RELEASE shape bg_anim.emp:118 `assert.w d7, ls, #BGANIM_MAX_BANDS` emits zero bytes, so nothing refuses it. BgAnim_Update loops 6 times with a4 walking `addq.w #2, a4` from BgAnim_LastStep: iterations 5 and 6 read and `move.w d5, (a4)` WRITE into BgAnim_LastStep+8/+10 — the first bytes of Static_Pal_Line0 and Static_Pal_Line1, the pre-built 14-byte DMA entries Enqueue_Dirty_Buffers queues. Independently, even with all three engine copies correctly raised to 6, BgAnim_Init (copy 3) still seeds only bands 0-3 with the -1 sentinel; bands 4-5 start at 0, compare equal to a step of 0 at bg_anim.emp:142 `cmp.w (a4), d0 / beq .skip_band`, and never take their first bank DMA — the strip shows stale VRAM until the driver moves.
findings.fix_sketch: (1) Give bg_anim the RASTER_MAX_PATCH treatment: `mark BgAnim_LastStep_End,` after ram.emp:413 plus `ensure((extern("BgAnim_LastStep_End") - extern("BgAnim_LastStep")) == 2 * BGANIM_MAX_BANDS, ...)` in bg_anim.emp — that measures the real emitted span and makes the two engine copies un-driftable, exactly as raster.emp:259 does. (2) Replace bg_anim.emp:87-89 with a dbf loop over BGANIM_MAX_BANDS, or at minimum an `ensure(BGANIM_MAX_BANDS == 4)` beside it naming the unroll. (3) tools/ already has an .emp const scraper (effects_budget_check.emp_constants) — have inject_editor_bg.py read BGANIM_MAX_BANDS from engine/system/constants.emp instead of restating 4. (Secondary, same file: bg_anim.emp:154 `lsr.w #3, d0  // step / BGANIM_BANKS` is log2(BGANIM_BANKS) restated as a literal while :149 uses `#BGANIM_BANKS-1`.)

findings.title: RASTER_SH_BASE duplicates boot's reg $0C byte with no pin, while its comment claims pin parity
findings.claim: RASTER_SH_BASE is a hand copy of boot_data.emp's VDP register-table byte for reg $0C, held only by a comment that asserts it is held "the way the opcode literals ... are held by their pins" — but the opcode literals have `ensure`s and this has none, so a change to boot's $0C makes reg_sh_on/off write the wrong resolution bits mid-frame.
findings.fix_sketch: Hoist the cell: `pub const BOOT_VDP_REG_0C = $81` in boot_data.emp, change :152 to `dc.b BOOT_VDP_REG_0C`, and add `ensure(RASTER_SH_BASE == ($8C00 | BOOT_VDP_REG_0C), "reg_sh_on/off's base drifted from boot's VDP reg $0C")` in raster_dsl.emp. Zero emitted bytes on both sides. If that cross-module import is genuinely blocked, at minimum correct the comment so it stops claiming a pin it does not have.

findings.title: Three divergent .emp-const scrapers in tools/; two lack the comment stripping the third documents as required
findings.claim: The same "read a const out of an .emp" job is implemented three times in tools/, and the two shorter copies take the first regex match without stripping comments — the exact defect effects_budget_check.py's docstring records as having been caught in review.
findings.evidence:
Copy A (hardened) — tools/effects_budget_check.py:49-52 `from emp_helper_closure import strip_comments` + `CONST_RE`, with :26-30 spelling out why: "Comments are stripped with emp_helper_closure.strip_comments, which handles `//`, the non-nesting `/* */` block form (lexer.rs:117-128) and string bodies. Stripping only `//`, as an earlier draft did, would have let a block-commented declaration become a live constant." It also resolves names/expressions and detects cycles.

Copy B — tools/effects_gates.py:51-59:
```
def emp_int(rel: str, name: str) -> int:
    txt = (AEON / rel).read_text()
    m = re.search(rf"^\s*(?:pub\s+)?const\s+{re.escape(name)}\s*=\s*(\$[0-9A-Fa-f]+|-?\d+)", txt, re.M)
```
Copy C — tools/raster_off_gate.py:48-54, the same idea under a different name (`emp_const`) with a narrower value alternation `(\$[0-9A-Fa-f]+|\d+)`.

Neither B nor C strips comments, and both take `re.search`'s FIRST match. B feeds ten constants into the cost-model expectations effects_gates asserts against hardware (:178-211: base, fetch, hit, tail, word, cram, rung, rungs, wreg, wrest). C feeds HBLANK_SLOT_RTE and HBLANK_IE1_BIT into the EFX-7 teardown assertion (:141-142) — the gate whose own docstring says at :22 "A gate that hard-coded $4E73 and $10 would keep passing after someone changed the constant".

FAILURE WALK. Recalibrating the cost model is routine (the .toml carries three SUPERSEDED measurement generations: effects_budget_model.toml:41-42, :58-59), and this tree's convention is to keep the old line for provenance: `// const RASTER_FIRE_BASE_CYC = 302   // superseded 2026-xx` above a new `pub const RASTER_FIRE_BASE_CYC = 318`. Copy B's `re.search` returns the COMMENTED line, so effects_gates computes `f0 = 2 * (302 - 16)` and `fire3 = 302 + ...` against a ROM built with 318. The gate reports FAIL on correct code, with a message ("measured F0=... F3=...") that reads like a hardware regression — while Copy A, reading the same constant from the same file via [symbols] (effects_budget_model.toml:231), correctly reports 318. Two gates in one directory disagreeing about what the source says.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete copies B and C. Both files can `sys.path.insert` on their own directory and `from effects_budget_check import make_resolver` (already parameterised on the aeon root), or at minimum `from emp_helper_closure import strip_comments` before applying the regex. One scraper, one behaviour.

findings.title: The poison lane checks named-but-missing and not present-but-unnamed, so an unregistered poison runs nothing
findings.claim: CASES and the contents of games/sonic4/test/poison/ are two hand-synced registries of the same set, and only one direction is verified: a poison module added to the directory but not added to CASES is never built, never asserted, and cannot show up as a shortfall.
findings.evidence:
tools/emp_expect_fail.py:127-133 checks one direction only:
```
    named = [(sentinel_path, "sentinel")] + [(path, entry) for path, entry, _, _ in CASES]
    missing = [(path, entry) for path, entry in named if not (AEON / path).is_file()]
    if missing:
        print("emp_expect_fail: FAIL — named poison modules that do not exist:")
```
There is no glob of POISON (:37 `POISON = "games/sonic4/test/poison"`) and no set-difference the other way, and the tally at :152 counts only `len(CASES)`.

The two registries agree today (12 `.emp` files in the directory; 11 CASES rows at :69-79 plus the SENTINEL at :44) — which is why the gap is invisible. The README asserts the invariant the check does not enforce: games/sonic4/test/poison/README.md "Each module here is deliberately broken — it exists to trip one specific guard (an `ensure`, a lowering error, a contract check) and prove the guard still fires."

FAILURE WALK. The scanline-services P1 migration adds a guard and a poison for it, say poison_scene_band_overlap.emp. The author drops the file in — it is picked up by the manifest scan, stays syntactically valid, and builds clean because nothing imports it (README property 2) — and forgets the CASES row. emp_expect_fail prints "OK — 11/11 cases" and the new guard has no negative test. This is precisely the failure mode effects_gates.py:5-9 was written against ("`effects_budget_check` sat unwired long enough for a row to drift 10 bytes; `s4lint` lints one no-op file; 147 pytest functions are invoked by no runner"), reproduced one directory over.
findings.fix_sketch: After the `missing` check, add the converse: glob `(AEON / POISON).glob('poison_*.emp')`, subtract the named basenames, and fail with "poison module present but not registered in CASES — it is being built by nothing". Four lines, and it makes README properties 1 and 3 machine-checked.

findings.title: derive_arms derives channel 0's clamp but hardcodes channel 1's outcome
findings.claim: The gate reads both bands out of the game source but applies the suppress/clamp logic to channel 0 only; channel 1's fire line is asserted to be its band floor unconditionally, hardcoding an outcome that actually depends on a preset anchor the gate never reads.
findings.evidence:
tools/effects_gates.py:81-98:
```
    l0 = pokes["Effects_World_Y"] - cam
    fires = []
    if l0 <= hi0:                                  # past the ceiling -> record suppressed
        fires.append(max(l0, lo0) - 1)             # below the floor -> clamps UP
    fires.append(lo1 - 1)                          # channel 1, clamped to its floor
    L = [0, 1] + fires
```
Channel 0 gets the full three-state resolution and correctly mirrors Raster_BuildSchedule (raster.emp:1130-1140: `cmp.w 2(a0), d2 / bgt .suppress`, then `cmp.w (a0), d2 / bge .have_line` / `move.w (a0), d2`). Channel 1 gets a constant. The docstring at :81-82 states the assumption — "channel 1 is never poked (see the scenes README), so it sits at its preset anchor and clamps up to its band floor" — and all three scenes do pin `{"poke": {"symbol": "Camera_Y", "value": 144, "width": 2}}`, so it is true today.

What makes it true is a number in a file the gate does not read: games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp:571 `patch_world_ys: [224, 314, PATCH_ANCHOR_NONE, PATCH_ANCHOR_NONE]`. 314 - 144 = 170, below channel 1's floor of 222 (:641 `ch: 1, lo: 222, hi: 223`). The gate DOES read the bands out of that same file (:129 `pat = re.findall(r"\bch:\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*lo:\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*hi:\s*(\d+)", src, re.S)`), so the omission is asymmetric rather than principled.

FAILURE WALK. Channel 1 is explicitly the negotiable fixture (ojz_effects.emp:599-603 "only its position is negotiable") and its anchor has moved before. Move it to world 370: l1 = 370 - 144 = 226 > hi1 = 223, so Raster_BuildSchedule takes `.suppress` and emits no record for channel 1. The real mid_band schedule becomes L = [0, 1, 99], word 1 = $8A00|(99-1-1) = $8A61 and word 3 = $8AFF. derive_arms still appends `lo1 - 1 = 221`, builds L = [0,1,99,221], and expects word 3 = $8A79. All three scenes FAIL on a correct build, and the message ("word 3: expected 0x8a79, got 0x8aff") points at the runtime rather than the gate.

Secondary, same function: :130 `bands = {f"ch{c}": (int(lo), int(hi)) for c, lo, hi in pat}` is last-match-wins over the whole file, so a second `patchable(...)` program added anywhere below OJZ_TC_PROG silently redefines the bands every expectation is derived from.
findings.fix_sketch: Read `patch_world_ys` out of ojz_effects.emp with the same regex approach already used for the bands, then run ONE loop over the channels applying the suppress/clamp rule to each — the logic is already written once at :85-88 and only needs parameterising. Also anchor the bands regex to the OJZ_TC_PROG block, or assert exactly two matches, so a later program cannot take over silently.

findings.title: Both $8F poison headers document a fragment the lane no longer uses
findings.claim: Each poison header's EXPECTED FRAGMENT line is a hand copy of the fragment in emp_expect_fail.py's CASES row; for the two reg-$0F poisons the tool was deliberately tightened and the headers were not, so the two files now disagree about what each case proves.
findings.evidence:
games/sonic4/test/poison/poison_direct_8f.emp:4 `// EXPECTED FRAGMENT: "autoincrement"` and games/sonic4/test/poison/poison_regset_8f.emp:4 `// EXPECTED FRAGMENT: "autoincrement"` — identical strings in the two poisons that target DIFFERENT layers.

tools/emp_expect_fail.py:74-75 uses different strings:
```
    (f"{POISON}/poison_regset_8f.emp",            "8d D-C",     "assumes stride 2", 1),
    (f"{POISON}/poison_direct_8f.emp",            "8d E-D",     "cannot be dodged", 1),
```
and :56-60 records why the headers' wording was abandoned: "The two $8F cases (8d D-C and 8d E-D) expect DISTINCT fragments so a case passing does not merely mean 'the string \"autoincrement\" appeared somewhere': D-C is the reg_set constructor's own ensure (fragment \"assumes stride 2\") ... (fragment \"cannot be dodged\")". The concern is real — `autoincrement` appears in BOTH guard messages: raster_dsl.emp:152 ("reg_set: writes reg $0F (autoincrement) — ... assumes stride 2 ...") and :1386 ("raster_program: an op writes reg $0F (autoincrement) — ... this scan is the layer that cannot be dodged ..."). The other ten headers match their rows exactly, which is what makes these two read as authoritative.

FAILURE WALK. A parcel rewords raster_dsl.emp:152. The author opens poison_regset_8f.emp to see what the lane requires, reads `EXPECTED FRAGMENT: "autoincrement"`, keeps that word, drops "assumes stride 2". The lane fails with "failed WITHOUT the expected fragment 'assumes stride 2' — wording drift" (:110) while the header just consulted says the fragment IS present — so the likely repair is to relax the CASES row back to "autoincrement", re-opening the ambiguity :56-60 exists to prevent and letting poison_regset_8f pass on the program-level scan firing instead of the constructor's ensure.
findings.fix_sketch: Either sync the two headers to the tool's strings, or — better, since this is the third registry of the same fact — have emp_expect_fail.py READ the fragment from each poison's own `// EXPECTED FRAGMENT: "..."` line and drop the string column from CASES. The header then cannot drift because it IS the input.

findings.title: The ship-trailer entry layout is decoded at hand offsets in two files and documented as 4 words where it is 6+
findings.claim: The trailer entry format has four readers and no struct; raster.emp's decoder comment still describes the pre-SetReg 4-word shape, so the one place a reader would look for the layout is wrong about half of it.
findings.evidence:
Emitter (correct) — engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp:1600 `//     [n (word)][n x (channel, stage offset, colour count, CRAM addr, reg count, reg words...)]`, built at :1653-1657.
Decoder 1 (stale doc) — engine/effects/raster.emp:1017-1018:
```
// Raster_BuildShipEntry — lay the off-screen ship's DMAEntry from the trailer's parameters.
//   a1 = trailer entry: [channel][stage offset][colour count][CRAM byte address]
```
The body reads `2(a1)`, `4(a1)`, `6(a1)` — consistent with those four words — and never mentions that words 4..N exist. :1027-1028 then claims totality: "It also means no second site knows the DMAEntry byte layout" — true of the DMAEntry, but a second site knows the TRAILER layout:
Decoder 2 — engine/system/buffers.emp:411-412 and :424-427, with its own hand offsets and its own copy of the format comment:
```
        // Entry layout after the channel word:
        // [stage off][colour count][CRAM addr][reg count][reg words...].
        ...
        move.w  8(a2), d0                       // reg count
        lea     10(a2), a1                      // -> the reg words
```
plus a third reader of the count word in Raster_InstallPatched (raster.emp:969 `tst.w (a1, d0.w)                      // the trailer's own count: 0 = no ship`). Four sites, three prose descriptions, two complete and one not; the only machine check is the OJZ hand pin (ojz_effects.emp:701-715).

This is documentation drift rather than a live bug — every offset is correct today, and a variable-length reg tail works because reg count precedes it. It matters because raster_dsl.emp:1663-1665 explicitly invites the next editor in: "relax this ensure and turn Enqueue_Dirty_Buffers' single test into a loop if a second shipping channel is real content". An editor doing that from raster.emp:1018's 4-word description computes entry 2's address with a fixed stride and lands inside entry 1's reg words.
findings.fix_sketch: Declare `struct raster_ship_entry (size: 10) { rse_channel: u16, rse_stage_off: u16, rse_count: u16, rse_cram_addr: u16, rse_reg_count: u16 }` in raster.emp and use its field names in both decoders (`move.w raster_ship_entry.rse_reg_count(a2), d0`, `lea sizeof(raster_ship_entry)(a2), a1`). bg_anim.emp:52-56 states this exact rationale for its own record — "this struct exists so every hand-tracked cursor offset below is DERIVED from the layout instead of a magic number" — so it is the tree's own idiom, and it makes the variable-length tail's start derived rather than typed.

findings.title: The probe's second wire encoder hardcodes opcode numbers the .emp side pins with an ensure
findings.claim: raster_cost_probe.py re-implements op_words with literal opcodes 0/2/4/10 plus the pal_stage_off formula and the arm/park words; all are pinned by `ensure` on the .emp side and by nothing on the Python side, and the probe's stated empirical cross-check (the `calls` count) cannot see an opcode renumber.
findings.evidence:
tools/raster_cost_probe.py:99-118 encodes opcodes as bare integers — `if k == "reg": return [0, o["w"]]`, `if k == "cram": ... return [2, ...]`, `if k == "region": return [4, ..., o["slot"] * 128 + o["pl"] * 32 + o["e"] * 2]`, `if k == "restore": return [10, ...]` — plus 0x8AFF / 0x8A00 in `arm()` (:132-137) and the 128-byte cap at :146.

Each has an authority with a pin on the .emp side: raster_dsl.emp:35 `ensure(OP_SET_REG == 0 && OP_CRAM == 2 && OP_PAL_REGION == 4 && OP_RUN_GRADIENT == 6 && OP_RUN_RAMP == 8 && OP_PAL_RESTORE == 10, ...)`, :38 `ensure(RASTER_ARM_PARK == $8AFF, ...)`, :40 `ensure(RASTER_BUF_SIZE == 128, ...)`, :59 `ensure(pal_stage_off(1, 3, 5) == 1 * 128 + 3 * 32 + 5 * 2, "raster_dsl's inlined Pal_Variant_Stage arithmetic drifted from pal_stage_off")`. The Python has no equivalent, though the sibling gate in the same directory already has the machinery (tools/effects_gates.py:51 `emp_int` reads ten constants out of raster_dsl.emp for exactly this reason).

The probe offers a different guarantee at :67-69: "The cross-check that it is transcribed correctly is empirical and strong — `calls` reports the fires the hardware actually took, so a mis-encoded program shows up as the wrong fire count before any cycle figure is read." That is real for a malformed program and blind to a renumber. Concretely: a parcel inserts an opcode and OP_PAL_RESTORE becomes 12. raster_dsl.emp:35 fires and gets fixed; the probe still emits `10`, which now decodes as whatever op holds slot 10. Its wire body is [op, cmd_hi, cmd_lo, count-1, addr] — structurally identical to OP_PAL_REGION's 5 words — so Raster_HInt parses it cleanly, advances the cursor identically, fires the same 6 times, and reports the same `calls`. F8 then measures a region fire while effects_gates.py:209-211 scores it against RASTER_WORK_RESTORE_CYC, and the disagreement reads as a cost-model regression.

Note rather than minor because the probe is a measurement instrument, not a build gate: a wrong reading misleads a calibration parcel rather than shipping bytes.
findings.fix_sketch: Give raster_cost_probe.py the same const read for the six OP_* codes, RASTER_ARM_PARK, RASTER_ARM_EVERY_LINE and RASTER_BUF_SIZE (ideally via the shared scraper from finding 5), so the transcription covers the FORMAT only and every magic number comes from the source. Leave the deliberately-illegal fixtures (F0, which has no fires and which raster_program refuses) as they are — that is the part that legitimately cannot come from the .emp.

findings.title: No interlock between a pending/in-flight IRQ4 and Raster_VBlank's frame rewind — a fire that races VINT eats priming record 0
findings.claim: Raster_HInt can execute its record walk AFTER Raster_VBlank has already rewound the schedule for the new frame, consuming priming record 0 and overwriting the primed reg $0A=0 with that record's arm word, which shifts the whole next frame's schedule by one record.
findings.evidence:
Raster_VBlank rewinds unconditionally: `clr.w Raster_Dense_Lines` / `move.l a1, Raster_Cursor       // first (priming) fire record` (raster.emp:608-609), then arms reg $0A=0 via HBlank_Install + the flush. Nothing marks the frame as re-armed, and Raster_HInt has no line/frame test at all — by design: `move.w (a1)+, (a2) // arm word -> reg $0A` then `move.w (a1)+, d0 // op_count` ... `.advance: move.l a1, Raster_Cursor` (raster.emp:697-703, 788-789).

ROUTE A (authorable today, deterministic). The project's own survey states the HInt counter "decrements once per line for lines `0..=224` inclusive" (docs/research/2026-08-12-raster-hint-survey.md:15-16). A dense run holds reg $0A=0 for every line (`move.w #RASTER_ARM_EVERY_LINE, (a2)`, raster.emp:828), and both dense constructors permit a run whose LAST line is 223: `ensure(top + lines <= 224, "…runs past screen line 223")` (raster.emp:348-349 and 433-434). With last line = 223 the counter underflows on line 224, i.e. HINT is raised at the same H position on the same line as VINT. The 68000 takes the higher level first, the VDP holds HINT pending across the IRQ6 handler (IPL 6 masks level 4), so the sequence is: VBlank_Handler -> VInt_Level -> Raster_VBlank (Dense_Lines cleared, Cursor rewound, $0A=0 armed) -> Flush_VDP_Shadow writes $0A=0 to hardware -> rte -> the still-pending IRQ4 enters Raster_HInt at ~line 240, finds Dense_Lines==0, walks the REWOUND cursor, writes priming record 0's arm word over the flushed 0, and advances Raster_Cursor to priming record 1.
Walk with the shipped gradient numbers (top=96): arm0 = raster_arm(1, top-1) = $8A00|(96-3) = 93. Next frame therefore starts with $0A=93 and cursor at priming record 1: first fire at line 94 (runs the no-op priming record, arms 0), next fire at 94+93+1 = 188, which is where the OP_RUN_GRADIENT setup record now ENTERs — the 96-line run renders at 189..223 instead of 96..191, and because Dense_Lines is still non-zero at line 224 the collision repeats every frame (a stuck broken state, not a one-frame blip).

ROUTE B (same mechanism, no dense tier). Any main-loop span masked at IPL>=6 that is entered while reg $0A holds a real gap rather than the $8AFF park leaves HINT permanently pending (the counter keeps reloading the frozen gap and re-asserting) while VINT also goes pending; at mask release IRQ6 runs first and the deferred IRQ4 then eats priming record 0 exactly as above. Section_RedrawPlanes is such a span — `move.w sr, -(sp)` / `move.w #$2700, sr` (engine/level/section.emp:214-215) held across what its own comment calls "a ~3-frame VDP poke storm" (section.emp:217-218). Today that proc is only reached via Section_Plane_Dirty (set at init before any preset is installed, and by replay restore), so route B is not live, but the comment at section.emp:167 names "cache recovery" as a designed trigger.

Not emulator-confirmed (no emulator available to this seat): the line-224 HINT/VINT coincidence and the pending-across-IRQ6 behaviour are read off the project's own survey plus 68000 interrupt priority, not measured here.
findings.fix_sketch: Cheapest closure at the freeze boundary: make the constructors refuse the collision (`top + lines <= 223`, i.e. last dense line <= 222) and add the same ceiling wherever a scene model can author a run. Structural closure: give Raster_VBlank a frame epoch — e.g. store a token beside Raster_Cursor at rewind and have Raster_HInt's first act be `tst` on a one-byte 'rewound this frame' flag that the handler clears, so a deferred pre-rewind fire retires as a park instead of consuming a record. Either is zero-cost on the hot path (one byte test) compared to fix-repin-refreeze after the migration.

findings.title: EFX_BLANK_DELAY=4 is calibrated only for SetReg-prefixed fires; a single-stream-op fire's CRAM burst lands mid-active-display
findings.claim: The CRAM/region blanking spin is sized against a fixture whose stream op was the SECOND op (94 cycles of SetReg ahead of it); a fire whose stream op is FIRST — which the DSL freely admits — writes CRAM around x~170 of the visible row, so the artifact the row-119 fix claims to remove is still there for every sh:0 band.
findings.evidence:
The constant's rationale claims the write is parked offscreen: "Row-119 fix: burn a cycle-counted delay so the colour writes below land in HBlank (offscreen)" (raster.emp:730-732) and "4 covers the ~40 cyc from mid-handler to the active-display edge on an H40 line, and 4 is what the measurement above validates" (raster.emp:228-232). The counter-evidence is in the same file, from the R1 calibration: "at ZERO delay the burst completed at x~180 of the row ABOVE the authored edge (leading-early by ~150 cyc — and the bare single-op cram ON fire spilled identically at x~170 … the clean mixed-shape evidence never covered single-op fires; … the clean mixed shape carries ~152 cyc of pre-burst delay: SetReg 94 + spin 58)" (raster.emp:797-804). So the measured-clean shape had 152 cycles of pre-burst delay while a single-op cram fire has 58 (moveq 4 + 54-cycle spin), and the measurement says the 58-cycle shape lands at x~170 of 320 — visible.
The DSL admits and even generates that shape: `region_boundary(..., sh: 0)` returns `fire(line, [stream_pal_region(...)])` (raster_dsl.emp:365), `fx_tint_band` forwards sh straight through (raster_dsl.emp:578-586), and `band(..., sh: 0)` returns `[f_on, fire(bot, [pal_restore(sa, sb / 2)])]` (raster_dsl.emp:628) — a single-op ON fire. The asymmetry is stark inside one band: the OFF edge gets EFX_RESTORE_DELAY=13 (raster.emp:238), calibrated for exactly the single-op case, so an sh:0 band renders a clean OFF edge and a dirty ON edge, and an author has no way to see it. Worse, the guard text tells the author the opposite: "that spin is what parks the write offscreen — only the FIRST op's writes are measured to land in HBlank (row 119, 1px -> 0px …)" (raster_dsl.emp:340) — the row-119 fixture is `fire(120, [reg_sh_on(), stream_cram($4A, [$000E])])` (games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp:115-116), where the stream op is second, not first.
Quantified deficit: reaching the next HBlank from x~170 needs ~150 px ≈ 170 68k cycles, i.e. roughly EFX_BLANK_DELAY 4 -> ~21, which is close to the 13 the restore path needed once its extra 64 cycles of dispatch depth (RASTER_DEPTH_RESTORE=4 rungs, raster_dsl.emp:1033) are subtracted. All shipped OJZ CRAM/region fires happen to be the two-op sh:1 shape, so nothing renders wrong today — this is exactly the latent substrate defect a freeze would make load-bearing.
findings.fix_sketch: Make the spin op-position-aware rather than one global constant: either (a) refuse single-stream-op CRAM/region fires in `fire()` unless the author passes an explicit measured opt-out, or (b) split the constant (EFX_BLANK_DELAY_FIRST vs _AFTER_REG) and select it from the op's position, re-pinning the F-series fixtures. Also correct raster_dsl.emp:340's sentence — it currently asserts the opposite of the measurement recorded at raster.emp:797-804.

findings.title: The '~60 usable cycles after entry' budget premise is arithmetically impossible against the handler's own measured prologue
findings.claim: The header (and the machine-readable budget model) justify RASTER_CRAM_MAX and the small movem save set with a ~60-cycle post-entry window, but the handler cannot reach ANY VDP write inside 60 cycles — the prologue alone is ~150-190 cycles — so the stated rationale is void and the real mechanism (spin until the FOLLOWING HBlank) is undocumented.
findings.evidence:
Claim: "~105 68k cycles from HINT-pending to the next line's active display, less ~44 for autovector exception entry — about 60 usable. A CRAM write outside that window paints a visible dot …, which is why RASTER_CRAM_MAX is 3 and why the save set below is deliberately small: a 4-register movem round trip alone would be 40 of those cycles" (raster.emp:79-82), mirrored as gospel in tools/effects_budget_model.toml:22-25 (`usable_cycles_after_entry = 60`, status "fixed").
Cycle walk to the FIRST VDP write (68000, values from the same tree's own model): autovector entry 44 + `jmp` from HBlank_Vector_Slot 12 (hblank.emp:31) + `move.w sr,-(sp)` 14 + `move.w #$2700,sr` 12 (engine/irq.emp:49-53) + `movem.l d0-d1/a1-a2,-(sp)` 40 + `lea VDP_CTRL,a2` 12 + `tst.w Raster_Dense_Lines` 12 + `bne` not taken 8-12 + `movea.l Raster_Cursor,a1` 16 + `move.w (a1)+,(a2)` 12 = ~182-186 cycles before the ARM word, and an OP_CRAM command longword lands ~265 cycles in, its colours ~330-420 cycles in. The code's own measured constant agrees: RASTER_FIRE_BASE_CYC = 302 for everything-but-ops, derived from F0's two priming fires at 286 each (raster_dsl.emp:985-991). 302 >> 60, so no shipped fire has ever written inside the stated window, and the measured landing positions (x~170/x~180 of the row, raster.emp:797-804) confirm writes land in the NEXT line's active display, not in the post-HINT HBlank.
findings.fix_sketch: Rewrite raster.emp:79-89 and the [hblank_window] rows to state the real invariant — writes land inside the fire+1 line's active display and are pushed to the FOLLOWING HBlank by a calibrated spin — and re-derive the RASTER_CRAM_MAX/save-set rationale from the ~105-cycle HBlank the burst actually lands in (3 words x 30 cyc = 90 fits; the movem argument does not belong to it).

findings.title: The dense LEAVE-schedule comment is wrong: the post-run extra fire EXECUTES the next record's ops, it does not merely arm it
findings.claim: The documented LEAVE rule says the extra every-line fire after a dense run only writes the next record's arm word, so an author is told to schedule the first post-run sparse event >= 2 lines below the run; in fact that fire consumes the record entirely — its ops run at run_last_line+1 and the cursor advances past it — so a mixed dense+sparse program fires its first sparse event at the wrong line no matter how it is spaced.
findings.evidence:
Comment: "LEAVE: the LAST dense fire (Raster_Dense_Lines 1->0) still writes reg $0A=0, so one extra every-line fire happens after the run; that fire finds Dense_Lines==0, falls through to the record walk at Raster_Cursor (already past the gradient op), and writes the NEXT record's arm word. Because of the lag that arm governs the fire after next, so the first post-gradient sparse event must be scheduled >= 2 lines below the run's last line." (raster.emp:682-688).
The code does more than that. At the extra fire the walk is entered at Raster_Cursor, which `.op_run_gradient`/.advance left pointing at the NEXT record's arm word (raster.emp:770-789), and the walk unconditionally runs that record: `move.w (a1)+, (a2)` (arm) / `move.w (a1)+, d0` (op_count) / `subq.w #1,d0` / `bmi .advance` / `.op_loop:` … then `.advance: move.l a1, Raster_Cursor` (raster.emp:697-703, 788-789). Only op_count == RASTER_OPS_END takes `.park` without advancing. So for a program [priming, priming, dense-setup@T-1, sparse@X]: the run's last line is T+L-1, the extra fire at T+L executes the sparse record's CRAM/SetReg ops there instead of at X-1, and advances the cursor to the terminator so the record never fires at its authored line. Not reachable through today's authoring surface (raster_dsl covers the sparse tier only; dense programs are the fixed 3-record structs at raster.emp:307-317/382-393), which is precisely why the wrong rule will be believed by whoever first builds a mixed program — and EFFECTS_AUTHORING.md names this module as the runtime source of truth.
findings.fix_sketch: Either state the truth (a dense run's trailing record must be the terminator; a mixed program needs an explicit op_count==0 spacer record after the run) or make it structural: have `.dense_body` write RASTER_ARM_PARK on the transition to Dense_Lines==0 so no extra fire occurs, and re-pin the F-series/dense fixtures.

findings.title: Raster_VBlank / Raster_BuildSchedule are documented VBlank-only but do not declare requires(vblank), though the engine has the mechanism
findings.claim: The two procs whose comments say they may run nowhere but VBlank carry no context contract, so a main-loop caller — the P1 scene-model migration is about to add callers — would build clean while re-recording and swapping the buffer under a Raster_HInt walk in active display.
findings.evidence: `pub proc Raster_VBlank () clobbers(d0-d4/a0-a2)` (raster.emp:516) and `proc Raster_BuildSchedule () clobbers(d0-d4/a0-a2)` (raster.emp:1101) — no `requires(vblank)`, while the builder's own header states "This is the only place it may run: the arm words are RELATIVE gaps, so a half-built schedule desynchronises the whole tail of the chain — from the main loop it would race Raster_HInt walking a buffer during active display, every frame the camera moves" (raster.emp:581-587) and "VBLANK ONLY, and that is inherited rather than new" (raster.emp:1088). The mechanism exists and is already satisfied by the call chain: `pub context vblank { granted }` (engine/irq.emp:58), `VBlank_Handler … grants(vblank)` (engine/system/vblank.emp:43), `VInt_Level () … requires(vblank)` (vblank.emp:110), `VInt_Lag () … requires(vblank)` (vblank.emp:273) — so adding the clause is zero-byte and cannot fail today's callers, and it turns a future main-loop call from a torn-buffer runtime bug into `[context.unsatisfied]`.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `requires(vblank)` to Raster_VBlank and Raster_BuildSchedule (and to Palette_Compose if it is likewise VBlank-only) before the P1 identity freeze — it emits no bytes, so it does not disturb the byte-identical migration gate.

findings.title: check_density has no interrupt-latency headroom, so an admitted adjacent-fire pair can still land its writes ~90 px late
findings.claim: The density guard compares a modelled fire cost against gap*488 with zero allowance for the 68000 finishing the instruction it interrupted, and the admitted adjacent case has only 30 cycles of slack — less than the worst-case main-loop instruction.
findings.evidence: `ensure(cost <= gap * RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC, …)` (raster_dsl.emp:1240) with RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC = 488 (raster_dsl.emp:983); the fixture pins put a 1-word stream fire at 458 cycles (F2/F7, raster_dsl.emp:1126-1137) so gap=1 is admitted with 30 cycles to spare, and the model's own provenance says the constants came from the per-routine profiler row plus a hand count of the emitted stream (raster_dsl.emp:963-970) — i.e. entry-to-rte, not the pre-entry latency. Concrete latency source in the main loop: `movem.l d0-d7/a0-a6, -(sp)` (engine/level/page_cache.emp:651) = 8 + 15*8 = 128 cycles that must complete before IRQ4 is recognised; section.emp:495's 9-register movem is 80. 458 + 128 = 586 > 488, so the second fire of an admitted adjacent pair can begin ~100 cycles late and place its colour words ~90 px further right than the model implies. Schedule integrity survives (the arm word is written ~185 cycles in, leaving ~300 cycles of margin before the next underflow), so the consequence is artifact position, not desync — but it is the failure mode the guard's own message promises to prevent ("pushes its writes into active display, which is measured as a visible mid-row colour change", raster_dsl.emp:1205-1207).
findings.fix_sketch: Add an explicit latency term to the model (a named RASTER_ENTRY_LATENCY_CYC of ~130, documented as the longest main-loop instruction) and charge it in check_density, or state in the guard comment that the budget excludes pre-entry latency so the 30-cycle adjacent margin is not read as real headroom.

coverage_notes:
HANDLER-FIRST WALK, in order: (1) engine/system/hblank.emp end to end — the RAM jmp-slot trampoline, HBLANK_SLOT_JMP/RTE, install/uninstall through the shadow, the HBlankHandler contract's CPU-state-only caveat. (2) engine/irq.emp `ints_off` (the exact acquire/release instruction pair) and engine/system/vblank.emp end to end — VBlank_Handler entry at IPL 6, VInt_Level/VInt_Lag ordering around Raster_VBlank/Flush_VDP_Shadow, VSync_Wait's masked flag pair. (3) Raster_HInt line by line from the fire boundary outward: exception entry -> jmp -> ints_off -> movem -> lea VDP_CTRL -> dense test -> arm write -> op_count -> dispatch chain -> each op body (.op_cram, .op_region, .op_run_gradient, .op_run_ramp, .op_pal_restore, .dense_body, .ramp_body) -> .advance/.park -> epilogue/rte, with a hand cycle count per instruction. (4) The three charter questions: entry-to-first-VDP-write (~182-186 cyc, cross-checked against RASTER_FIRE_BASE_CYC=302 and the measured x~170/x~180 landings) -> finding 3; IPL/nesting semantics (IRQ4 enters at IPL 4, one instruction of unmasked window before $2700, VINT priority inversion, HINT held pending across IRQ6) -> finding 1; adjacent fires (check_density's cost<=gap*488, F-series pins, the 30-cycle margin) -> finding 6. (5) Schedule-advance paths: Raster_VBlank install/teardown/rewind, Raster_BuildSchedule's two-back arm-slot walk and park-by-construction, Raster_InstallPatched's ordering, Raster_GetChannelBand, Effects_LatchWorldLines/SetWorldY. (6) raster_dsl.emp's timing surface: fire() ceilings, region_boundary/fx_tint_band/band, check_intervals, check_density, arm_at, check_mixed_fire, the whole cost model + depth constants + F0-F8 fixture pins + the both-sides-of-the-line ensures. (7) tools/effects_budget_model.toml in full; tools/raster_source_gate.py header and probe discipline. (8) games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp — every shipped program's fires, hand pins, patch table, and the dense/ramp tops and lengths (grad 96..191, ramp 112..207, both well clear of line 224). (9) engine/level/bg_anim.emp in full (main-loop, deferrable-DMA only; no HInt interaction beyond bandwidth) and the parallax touchpoints only (the reg $0B ints_off+z80_stopped bracket at parallax.emp:510-521, Vscroll_Write's VBlank position) — no walker/fill internals, per scope. (10) engine/level/section.emp's $2700 poke-storm bracket and its Section_Plane_Dirty reachability, plus a grep audit of every main-loop VDP_CTRL writer to test the header's "every main-loop command pair must be bracketed" invariant.

CLEAN RESULTS worth recording: main-loop VDP command pairs are all either single-word register writes, move.l command longwords (atomic against interrupts, so the handler can never land inside a split pair), or inside a $2700 mask — I found no unbracketed address+data burst reachable while a program is armed, so the split-latch hazard the header names is currently held. The handler-read cells (Raster_Cursor, Raster_Dense_*, Raster_Ramp_*) have no writer outside raster.emp (grepped preset.emp, palette.emp, the test game), so Effects_InstallPreset / Raster_InstallPatched cannot tear the handler's view mid-install. The dispatch-cost model's `beq.s` assumption (16 cyc/failed rung) is held honest by the F1==412 pin, so a relaxation to word displacements would fail the build rather than silently under-predict.

KNOWN-OPEN ITEMS: nothing new found on the Raster_Buf_B patched-path observability gap or on EFX-4b (.copy_program's fixed 64-word copy over short static programs) — I confirmed the over-read is bounded and harmless to the walk (the terminator stops it) and costs ~640 cycles only on install frames, so I have no wider blast radius or cheaper closure to add; neither is re-reported.

NOT REACHED: engine/effects/palette.emp and palette_dsl.emp were read only where the raster path touches them (Pal_Variant_Stage geometry, Palette_Ship_Snap, pal_dirty_mask re-assert) — the derive/fade/cycle timing inside Palette_Compose is unswept by this seat. engine/effects/preset.emp was read only at its raster install seam. tools/effects_gates.py, raster_off_gate.py, raster_cost_probe.py bodies, effects_budget_check.py + its unit test, effects_scene_assert.py, and games/sonic4/test/poison/*.emp were NOT read (only the budget model and raster_source_gate's header). No emulator work of any kind (charter rule): the line-224 HINT/VINT coincidence in finding 1 and the exact landing arithmetic in finding 2 rest on the project's own survey and on the R1 measurement quoted in the code, and both would benefit from one oracle confirmation before a fix is priced.

findings.title: Trailer offset documented as 8n; the runtime computes 10n
findings.claim: ship_trailer's doc gives the trailer's byte offset as "128 + 2 + 8*records", but a patch-table entry is FIVE words (10 bytes) and the runtime steps over the table by 10n — the doc is from the retired four-word-entry era.
findings.evidence: raster_dsl.emp:1630 — "The trailer's own\n// offset is 128 + 2 + 8*records, which the runtime computes from the count word it already\n// reads."  The table this offset skips is emitted 5 words/record (patch_table:1588-1592 emits `[src, lo, hi, 2*arm_word_index, 2*record_words]`; check_rec_layout:1728 indexes `1 + 5 * (k - 2)`; patched_words:1761 = `64 + 1 + 5 * fires.len + ship_trailer_words`). The runtime agrees with the CODE, not this comment — raster.emp:938-953: "TEN BYTES PER ENTRY, AND TEN IS NOT A SHIFT. The stride was a single `lsl.w #3` while entries were four words; the fifth word (rec_off/rec_len replacing arm_off) makes it 10n", implemented as `lsl.w #3,d0` / `add.w d1,d0` / `add.w d1,d0` / `addq.w #2,d0`. Failure scenario: an Aurora-side or tool-side emitter (or any hand check) that computes the trailer position from this sentence lands 2n bytes short for an n-record template — for OJZ_TwoChannel (n=2) at 128+2+16=146 instead of 128+2+20=150, i.e. it reads patch-table words as the ship count/channel and would build a frame-top CRAM DMA from `rec_off`/`rec_len` values.
findings.fix_sketch: Say `128 + 2 + 10*records` (five words per entry), and cross-reference raster.emp's 10n note so the two stay paired.

findings.title: Runtime says the trailer holds a built 14-byte DMAEntry; it holds parameters
findings.claim: Raster_InstallPatched's trailer-layout comment describes the trailer as `[n][channel][DMAEntry (14 bytes)]`, which the same file contradicts 86 lines later and which the encoder never emits.
findings.evidence: raster.emp:934-935 — "// Trailer layout: [n (word)][channel (word)][DMAEntry (14 bytes)], sitting after the\n// patch table at RASTER_BUF_SIZE + 2 + 10*records."  The actual wire shape is parameters: raster_dsl.emp:1600 `[n (word)][n x (channel, stage offset, colour count, CRAM addr, reg count, reg words...)]`, emitted at raster_dsl.emp:1651-1655; consumed as parameters by Raster_BuildShipEntry (raster.emp:1041 `move.w 2(a1),d1` stage off, :1047 `move.w 4(a1),d3` count, :1050 `move.w 6(a1),d2` CRAM addr) and by buffers.emp:412 ("Entry layout after the channel word: [stage off][colour count][CRAM addr][reg count][reg words...]", reading `8(a2)` and `10(a2)`). raster.emp:1020 states the opposite of :934 outright: "THE TRAILER CARRIES PARAMETERS RATHER THAN A BUILT ENTRY, and the reason is a language constraint". Failure scenario: a reader sizing or hand-writing a trailer from :934 allots 2+14 bytes for a 2+12-byte entry (and expects DMAEntry's interleaved reg-marker bytes where the count/addr/reg words actually are); the ship then queues a Static_Pal_Ship built from the wrong words.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the DMAEntry wording with the parameter list Raster_BuildShipEntry actually reads (channel, stage off, count, CRAM addr, reg count, reg words), and note the entry is variable-length in reg count. Also extend :1018's `a1 = trailer entry:` list, which stops at the CRAM address and omits the reg count/reg words that follow.

findings.title: Palette_Compose header describes a d7 dirty accumulator that does not exist
findings.claim: The proc header says each layer ORs its lines into d7 and the accumulated mask is written to Palette_Dirty at the end; the body has no d7 and no final OR, and its own inline comment says an accumulator is impossible there.
findings.fix_sketch: Rewrite the header to match :332-334 (each layer ORs Palette_Dirty directly; no accumulator survives a sub-proc call), or move the d7 sentence into Palette_DoCycle's header where a d7 accumulator really is used (:405, :431).

findings.title: OJZ_TwoChannel's density margin is justified with retired-model numbers (526/489)
findings.claim: The re-band note prices channel 0's fire at 526 cycles against a 489-cycle line; the shipped cost model gives 676 against 488, so the stated margin is 150 cycles too generous and the scanline constant is rounded the wrong way.
findings.fix_sketch: Restate as "676 cyc against a 488-cycle line (two lines = 976 available)", and key the sentence to fire_cost_cycles rather than a typed-in figure.

findings.title: EFX_RESTORE_DELAY's calibration arithmetic uses the pre-R1 SetReg cost (94, now 110)
findings.claim: The .op_pal_restore comment derives the 13-iteration spin from "~152 cyc of pre-burst delay: SetReg 94 + spin 58", but SetReg costs 94 only at RUNGS=4; R1 appended OP_PAL_RESTORE and the same file records the +16 rung tax, so the reference shape's pre-burst delay is 168.
findings.evidence: raster.emp:801-804 — "The value below was JUMPED to from the measured deficit (the clean\n// mixed shape carries ~152 cyc of pre-burst delay: SetReg 94 + spin 58)". SetReg at RUNGS=4 = FETCH 8 + 4*16 + WORK_REG 12 + TAIL 10 = 94; at the shipped RUNGS=5 it is 8 + 80 + 12 + 10 = 110 (raster_dsl.emp:1030 `RASTER_DISPATCH_RUNGS = 5`; pin :1124 "measured 2026-08-17 at RUNGS=5 ... (was 396 at RUNGS=4)"). raster.emp:182-186 states the tax explicitly: "The SetReg fall-through pays the +16 rung tax (F1 396->412, F5 612->628...)". So the same file says both "SetReg 94" and "+16 per rung on SetReg". Failure scenario: EFX_RESTORE_DELAY = 13 was pixel-verified, but the next recalibration (the comment's own "Ladder if it ever drifts") re-derives the target from 152 and lands ~16 cycles (1.6 dbf iterations) short — i.e. reproduces leading dots on the row above the authored edge, the exact artifact the value was jumped to remove.
findings.fix_sketch: Update to "SetReg 110 + spin 58 = ~168" (or express it as fire_cost terms), and note the derivation moves whenever RASTER_DISPATCH_RUNGS changes.

findings.title: Preset note says unused patch anchors are 0; the code uses PATCH_ANCHOR_NONE, and 0 is the value the design forbids
findings.claim: "Channels 2 and 3 are unused; their anchors are 0" is false — OJZ_Preset_Sec0 passes PATCH_ANCHOR_NONE ($7FFF) — and 0 is precisely the anchor value raster_dsl documents as the most invasive possible default.
findings.evidence: ojz_effects.emp:568 — "Channels 2 and 3 are unused; their anchors are 0."  The code two lines below: `patch_world_ys: [224, 314, PATCH_ANCHOR_NONE, PATCH_ANCHOR_NONE]` (:571). raster_dsl.emp:1088-1096 — "PATCH_ANCHOR_NONE — the world Y a preset gives a patch channel it does not use. LARGE AND POSITIVE, not 0 ... a 0 anchor reads as -Camera_Y, i.e. ABOVE the screen top, i.e. 'fully submerged' — the most invasive possible state as the default for a channel nobody asked for." Failure scenario: an author writing a new preset (or 'simplifying' this one) from this sentence spells `patch_world_ys: [.., .., 0, 0]`; Effects_LatchWorldLines then latches Effects_Screen_L[2..3] = -Camera_Y, and Parcel W's overlay reads that as a boundary above the screen top — the fully-submerged default the constant exists to prevent.
findings.fix_sketch: Change to "their anchors are PATCH_ANCHOR_NONE ($7FFF) — never 0; see raster_dsl.emp's PATCH_ANCHOR_NONE note".

findings.title: OJZ_TwoChannel's channel summary and gate-anchor note carry three stale band pairs
findings.claim: The fixture's own prose declares bands 3..214 / 216..223 and, in the anchor note, 40..120 / 130..200 with both boundaries "mid-band"; the shipped code authors 3..220 and 222..223, under which channel 1's authored anchor is outside its band.
findings.evidence: ojz_effects.emp:586-587 — "Channel 0 — the water shape: S/H on plus a 3-colour region swap, band 3..214.\n// Channel 1 — a plane B vertical scroll split, band 216..223."  ojz_effects.emp:563-565 — "channel 0: 224 - 144 =  80  (band 40..120  — mid-band ...)\n//   channel 1: 314 - 144 = 170  (band 130..200 — mid-band)". The code: `ch: 0, lo: 3,   hi: 220` and `ch: 1, lo: 222, hi: 223` (:639-641), confirmed by the table pin "$8000, 2, 219" / "$8001, 221, 222" (:675-678, fire lines) and by the file's own corrections at :613 ("spending eight lines ... to sit at 216 rather than 222") and :622 ("LO WAS 40 UNTIL Parcel W SHIPPED"). Failure scenario: the gate-expectation note claims channel 1 sits mid-band at screen line 170 with both clamp directions exercisable; under the shipped 222..223 band, screen line 170 is below `lo`, so Raster_BuildSchedule clamps UP to fire line 221 on essentially every frame. A verification pass deriving predicted rows from :563-567 asserts row 170 for channel 1 and reads the (correct) 222 as a failure — or, worse, 'fixes' the band to match the prose and gives back the 3 rows of water travel :613 records buying.
findings.fix_sketch: Restate :586-587 as bands 3..220 / 222..223, and rewrite the anchor note to say channel 0 is mid-band while channel 1's anchor clamps to its 2-line floor by design (poison_ship_plus_restore.emp already quotes the correct "[3,220]").

findings.title: Trailer pin comment says neither channel ships, two lines above the pin that shows one does
findings.claim: "Neither channel declares offscreen_ship, so this is the bare count word" contradicts the fixture (channel 0 declares offscreen_ship: 1), the pin data below it, and the very next paragraph.
findings.evidence: ojz_effects.emp:680-683 — "The off-screen ship trailer, after the patch table. Neither channel declares\n// offscreen_ship, so this is the bare count word — and pinning the EMPTY case is worth a line\n// on its own: it is what proves the count word is emitted unconditionally..."  Immediately below, :684 — "Channel 0 declares offscreen_ship, so the trailer carries the PARAMETERS of its frame-top entry" — and the data is `OJZ_TC_TRAILER_HAND = [1, 0, 72, 3, $48, 1, $8C89]` (:701-709), against `patchable(..., ch: 0, lo: 3, hi: 220, offscreen_ship: 1)` (:639). Failure scenario: a reader auditing gate coverage takes this paragraph at face value and concludes the empty-trailer (n=0) case is pinned here — it is not pinned anywhere — while also concluding the ship path is unexercised. Either conclusion mis-scopes the next parcel's test work; this tree's recorded failure mode is exactly "a case believed covered".
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the stale paragraph (it describes the pre-offscreen_ship revision) and keep :684 onward; if the n=0 case is still wanted as a pin, say plainly that no fixture covers it today.

findings.title: "4-register movem round trip ... 40 cycles" is the one-way cost; the round trip is 84
findings.claim: The handler's budget note prices the movem save/restore pair at 40 cycles of the ~60-cycle window; on a 68000 a 4-register MOVEM.L push is 40 and the pop is 44, so the round trip is 84.
findings.evidence: raster.emp:78-82 — "CYCLE BUDGET (Ruling 2a): ~105 68k cycles from HINT-pending to the next line's active display, less ~44 for autovector exception entry — about 60 usable ... a 4-register movem round trip alone would be 40 of those cycles."  The handler's pair is `movem.l d0-d1/a1-a2,-(sp)` (:657) and `movem.l (sp)+,d0-d1/a1-a2` (:858). 68000 timings: MOVEM.L register-to-memory -(An) = 8+8n = 40 for n=4; MOVEM.L memory-to-register (An)+ = 12+8n = 44. The same wrong figure is baked into the machine-readable budget: tools/effects_budget_model.toml:31 `movem_roundtrip_cycles = 40  # fixed — 4-register movem push+pop`. Failure scenario: this is the stated justification for keeping the save set small and RASTER_CRAM_MAX at 3; a perf change reasoning from it believes ~20 cycles of the window are still unspent and adds a register to the save set (+16 cyc) or a fourth CRAM word, when the accounting as written already overruns the quoted budget. Two seats reading 40 will reach opposite conclusions from two seats reading 84.
findings.fix_sketch: State "40 to push + 44 to pop = 84" here and in effects_budget_model.toml:31 (rename the row or split push/pop), and reconcile the "~60 usable" framing with the fact that the shipped prologue/epilogue alone exceed it.

findings.title: The budget model's ungated per-fire rows are pre-R1 (F1 396, water 660) and its header cites a retracted figure
findings.claim: effects_budget_model.toml carries F1 = 396 and the OJZ water fire = 660 — both RUNGS=4 values superseded by the R1 re-measure (412 / 676) — and its opening rationale quotes ~2090 cyc/fire, derived from the figure the same file marks SUPERSEDED.
findings.evidence: toml:55 `sparse_fire_reg1_cycles   = 396      # measured — fixture F1`, contradicted by the shipped pin raster_dsl.emp:1124-1125 "== 412 ... measured 2026-08-17 at RUNGS=5, 3 boots spread 0 (was 396 at RUNGS=4)". toml:57 `sparse_fire_water_cycles  = 660      # modelled — reg_sh_on + 3-word region, the OJZ water fire`, against the shipped model's 302+110+264 = 676 for that shape (raster_dsl.emp:644). toml:6 "the measured rows are upper bounds that include profiler instrumentation and exception entry (~2090 cyc/fire against a usable_cycles_after_entry of 60)" — no measured row in the file is within 3x of 2090 (they are 458/518/566/704); 2090 is the per-fire share of `sparse_tier_cycles_per_frame_SUPERSEDED = 8358`, which :36-40 marks "SUPERSEDED 2026-08-14 — DO NOT USE ... two handlers summed". None of these rows is in [symbols], so effects_budget_check cannot see the drift. Failure scenario: a seat or parcel sizing new content off "the ONE machine-readable budget" (line 1) prices a SetReg-bearing fire 16 cycles light and the OJZ water fire at 660 — the same understatement the ojz_effects density note makes — and concludes a boundary pair fits where the shipped guard's arithmetic says it is marginal.
findings.fix_sketch: Re-key the two rows to the current fixture pins (412, 676) with the R1 date, and replace the ~2090 parenthetical with a live figure (e.g. F8 704) or drop it, since the file itself retracts its source.

findings.title: VInt_Level/VInt_Lag headers omit Raster_VBlank from both the order and the callee union
findings.claim: Both handler headers enumerate the pipeline's execution order and the callee set the clobbers clause is the union of, and neither lists Raster_VBlank — the first thing each body calls.
findings.evidence: vblank.emp:101-107 — "Execution order: shadow flush -> dirty enqueue -> plane-buffer drain -> ... Clobbers: the union of the pipeline callees (Flush_VDP_Shadow d0-d3/a0-a1 · Enqueue_Dirty_Buffers d0/a1-a2 · ... Read_Controllers d0-d4/a0)"; the body calls `jbsr Raster_VBlank` (:157) BEFORE `jbsr Flush_VDP_Shadow` (:159), which the inline comment at :151 says is load-bearing ordering. Same omission in VInt_Lag's header (:268-271) against the `jbsr Raster_VBlank` at :291. Raster_VBlank declares clobbers(d0-d4/a0-a2) (raster.emp:516) — today inside the declared d0-d4/a0-a3/a5-a6, so the clause is still correct. Failure scenario: Raster_VBlank (or Raster_BuildSchedule, which it calls) widens to a3 or d5; someone re-deriving VInt_Level's union from this list does not see the contributor and leaves the clause unwidened, so a live register is clobbered inside VBlank on the crossing frames the builder runs.
findings.fix_sketch: Add "raster re-arm ->" to the order line and Raster_VBlank d0-d4/a0-a2 to both callee unions.

findings.title: Pal_Cycle_None's rationale rests on a deleted installer and is falsified by the live one
findings.claim: The sentinel's justification says NULL cannot mean "cycling off" because Palette_InstallCycleSection reads NULL as keep-current; that proc is deleted and the surviving installer, Palette_LoadCycle, clears the script and the active bit on a0 = 0.
findings.evidence: palette.emp:752-757 — "'no cycling here' has to be a value it can WRITE, not an absence. NULL cannot serve: Palette_InstallCycleSection reads NULL as 'keep whatever the last section installed'". Palette_InstallCycleSection no longer exists (parallax.emp:214-215: the three "keep whatever the previous section had" installers "are deleted"); the live path is Palette_LoadCycle, which on a0 = 0 does `move.l a0,Pal_Cycle_Script` + `andi.b #~PAL_ACT_CYCLE,Pal_Active` + `beq .done` (:299-316), i.e. off, not keep. preset.emp:185-186 states the opposite of this comment for the same call: "ep_cycle -> Palette_LoadCycle (its own a0=0 path already turns cycling off cleanly, so no redirect is needed there)". Same class of stale reference at :38 ("* base  Palette_LoadSection loads the section's 96-byte palette into Pal_Base" — the live proc is Palette_LoadPal), :250 ("Palette_ArmFade — the NEXT Palette_LoadSection cross-fades") and :677 ("proven at build time by the variant_word() ensure() vectors above" — those vectors are in palette_dsl.emp:74-81, not above). Failure scenario: a reader trusting :755 believes ep_cycle = 0 inherits the previous section's script and adds a redirect-to-Pal_Cycle_None in Effects_InstallPreset (harmless but wrong), or conversely treats Palette_LoadCycle's 0 path as keep-current when auditing total binding and reports a stale-cycling defect that cannot occur.
findings.fix_sketch: Re-ground the sentinel's rationale on the live rule (total binding wants a writable "off" value even though Palette_LoadCycle's 0 path is clean), and repoint :38/:250/:677 at Palette_LoadPal and palette_dsl.emp.

findings.title: Effects_InstallPreset's register-hazard note names a nonexistent callee and undercounts the callees
findings.claim: The a3 rationale lists "the six callees" including Raster_InstallPatchedWorldY, a proc that no longer exists (renamed when W0 dropped the anchor parameter); the body has seven distinct callees.
findings.evidence: preset.emp:168-170 — "the preset pointer is held in a3 instead — the only address register none of the six callees below (Palette_ArmFade/LoadPal/LoadCycle/SetVariant, Raster_Install/InstallPatchedWorldY) clobber."  The body calls Effects_LatchWorldLines (:247), Palette_ArmFade (:252), Palette_LoadPal (:257), Palette_LoadCycle (:261), Palette_SetVariant (:269, :278), Raster_InstallPatched (:288) and Raster_Install (:296) — seven, and the name is Raster_InstallPatched (grep finds no Raster_InstallPatchedWorldY anywhere). The same header's present tense at :191-193 ("Both sibling installers already guard this way — Raster_InstallSection (`cmp.l Raster_Program, d0 / beq .keep`) and Palette_InstallCycleSection") describes two deleted procs as live. Failure scenario: the a3 safety argument is a hand audit over an enumerated callee set; the set is missing Effects_LatchWorldLines, so a future widening of that proc to a3 passes the audit as written (it happens to clobber only d0-d2/a0-a1 today) and the preset pointer is destroyed mid-install.
findings.fix_sketch: List all seven callees with their current names and drop the deleted-installer precedent sentence (or mark it historical).

findings.title: Install-order rationale names the wrong RAM bank as the builder's input
findings.claim: The clear-before-seed argument says Raster_BuildSchedule "re-derives every arm gap from Effects_World_Y"; the builder reads the latched Effects_Screen_L, and the cited line reference points at unrelated prose.
findings.evidence: preset.emp:211-212 — "In that\n// VBlank Raster_BuildSchedule re-derives every arm gap from Effects_World_Y using\n// Raster_Patch_Tab ALONE as its liveness test (raster.emp:877-878)". Raster_BuildSchedule reads `lea Effects_Screen_L, a2` / `move.w (a2,d2.w),d2  // the LATCHED screen line` (raster.emp:1132-1133) and never touches Effects_World_Y; the liveness test is at raster.emp:1102-1103, while raster.emp:877-878 is the deleted-WATER_TEMPLATE_ARM0_OFF note. Failure scenario: the hazard window this comment protects is opened by the LATCH (:247), not by the seed (:228-233) — a reader modelling the race from this sentence can reorder the latch above the `clr.l Raster_Patch_Tab` (or drop the clear as unnecessary) and reintroduce exactly the one-frame boundary jump the comment exists to prevent.
findings.fix_sketch: Say the builder reads Effects_Screen_L (latched by Effects_LatchWorldLines from Effects_World_Y) and repoint the locator at Raster_BuildSchedule's liveness test.

findings.title: arm_at cites a constant (RASTER_FIRE_SPAN) that does not exist, in the wrong direction
findings.claim: arm_at's note defers its dropped range guard to "RASTER_FIRE_SPAN below"; no such name exists in the tree, and the module-level pin it means is above, not below.
findings.evidence: raster_dsl.emp:1268-1275 — "the fact it\n// was reaching for is asserted ONCE, at module level, against the bounds that make it true\n// (see RASTER_FIRE_SPAN below)."  `grep -rn RASTER_FIRE_SPAN` returns exactly this comment line and nothing else; the pin actually meant is :51 `ensure((RASTER_MAX_FIRE_LINE - 1) - 1 <= 255, ...)`, 1219 lines EARLIER. Same class at :456 — "(Constants DEFINED in this module, such as RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC above, are injected and are safe to name.)" — RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC is defined at :983, 527 lines below. Failure scenario: someone raising the screen-line ceiling follows this pointer, finds no RASTER_FIRE_SPAN, and concludes the per-call `gap <= 255` guard was deleted without a replacement — either restoring a dead guard or (worse) raising the ceiling believing nothing checks it.
findings.fix_sketch: Point at the :44-52 pin by its real spelling (RASTER_MIN_FIRE_LINE / RASTER_MAX_FIRE_LINE and the 255-span ensure) and drop the "above/below" direction words.

findings.title: Stale internal locators and a diagnostic naming the wrong file
findings.claim: Raster_GetChannelBand's cross-references point at the wrong lines, and the Raster_State span-guard message names hblank.emp for a layout that lives in ram.emp.
findings.evidence: raster.emp:1191-1192 — "so a SECOND consumer of that anchor clamps exactly where\n// Raster_BuildSchedule clamps it (:895-901)" — lines 895-901 are the Raster_WaterArm / RASTER_MIN_FIRE_LINE note; the clamp is at :1135-1139. :1215 cites ":894's coordinate system" for the fire-line convention, which lands in the same block by luck. :259-260 — `ensure(... , "Raster_State RAM block drifted from hblank.emp's raster layout")` — the twin layout is engine/ram.emp:277-369 (this module was split out of hblank.emp, which no longer contains any raster RAM). Failure scenario: the ensure's message sends whoever trips it to hblank.emp, an 83-line file with no `region`/`vars` block at all, while the drift to fix is in ram.emp.

findings.title: Two poison headers declare the retired non-discriminating EXPECTED FRAGMENT
findings.claim: poison_regset_8f and poison_direct_8f both state EXPECTED FRAGMENT "autoincrement", but the runner's rows expect the distinct fragments "assumes stride 2" and "cannot be dodged" — and the runner comment records that the split was made deliberately to remove exactly that ambiguity.

findings.title: Every poison header points at the README for a limitation the README contradicts
