findings.title: Dense-run constructors permit a LEAVE fire coincident with VINT (top+lines==224)
findings.claim: raster_gradient_program / raster_ramp_program admit `top + lines == 224`, which places the run's own extra LEAVE fire at screen line 224 — the HInt that fires at the end of the last active line, simultaneous with VINT — so the frame's record cursor and reg $0A are manipulated across the VBlank boundary.
findings.evidence:
Constructor bound (raster.emp:348, and the identical one for the ramp at :433):

    ensure(top + lines <= 224,
           "raster_gradient_program: run {top}..{top + lines - 1} runs past screen line 223")

The handler's own LEAVE contract (raster.emp:717-722 header text, body at :828):

    //   LEAVE: the LAST dense fire (Raster_Dense_Lines 1->0) still writes reg $0A=0,
    //     so one extra every-line fire happens after the run

    .dense_body:
        move.w  #RASTER_ARM_EVERY_LINE, (a2)       // reg $0A=0: fire every line

Walk with top=T, lines=L, T+L=224 (legal): fire j of the run lands on screen line T+j (the module's own measured ENTER schedule, raster.emp:300-320), so the last dense fire is at line T+L-1 = 223 and it re-arms $8A00 unconditionally. The LEAVE fire is therefore at line 224 — i.e. the HInt asserted at the end of line 223, which is exactly when VINT asserts. The 68000 services the higher level first: IRQ6 runs VInt_Level -> Raster_VBlank, which does `clr.w Raster_Dense_Lines` (raster.emp:608) and `move.l a1, Raster_Cursor` back to priming record 0, and HBlank_Install re-seeds reg $0A=0 through the shadow for the flush. The level-4 request is not acknowledged by that IACK, so on VBlank's rte the handler is entered with Dense_Lines==0, falls through to the record walk, and consumes priming record 0 for the NEW frame while writing that record's arm word straight onto the hardware reg $0A that the flush just set to 0. The new frame's line-0 fire then consumes priming record 1, so arm0 (the gap 1 -> first event) is never loaded and every event line in the frame is displaced. The coincidence is a fixed property of the schedule, so it repeats every frame rather than self-healing. If instead the pending level-4 is dropped by the emulator/VDP, the alternative outcome is that the LEAVE fire never runs at all and any record following the dense run never gets its arm word written — the tail of that frame's schedule is dead. Either branch makes top+lines==224 unsafe.

Contrast: the sparse tier cannot reach this. `fire`'s ensure is `line >= 3 && line <= 223` (raster_dsl.emp:297) on the SCREEN line, so its fire lines cap at 222, and the last real record's arm is RASTER_ARM_PARK. Only the dense constructors let a fire reach 224, and nothing in the file notes the asymmetry.

GATE BLINDNESS: `effects_gates.py` runs only the three committed scenes (`SCENES = ("mid_band", "suppressed", "above_screen")`, effects_gates.py:48) and the shipped dense fixtures sit well inside the bound (OJZ_GRAD_TOP=96 + OJZ_GRAD_LINES=96 = 192; OJZ_RAMP_TOP=112 + 96 = 208, ojz_effects.emp:303-304, :471-472), so no gate ever authors the boundary case. `raster_source_gate.py` breaks at `.region_loop` and observes a2 only — it never enters the dense path. `raster_cost_probe.py` reads per-routine cycle totals, which are indifferent to WHICH record a fire consumed. The comptime guards (check_density, check_band_layout) reason in screen lines with no notion of the VINT boundary at all.
findings.fix_sketch: Tighten both dense constructors to `top + lines <= 223` and say why in the message ("the run's own LEAVE fire lands at top+lines and must stay inside active display, off the VINT boundary"). Cheaper and more honest than a runtime guard, and it makes the dense ceiling agree with the sparse tier's fire-line cap of 222.

findings.title: Density guard admits 100% of a nominal scanline with no bus-contention or VDP-FIFO term
findings.claim: `check_density` admits any fire whose MODELLED cost is <= gap * 488, and the model is a pure 68000 instruction-timing model calibrated on a deliberately quiesced bus — it carries no term for VDP FIFO/external-slot waits on the data-port writes and none for Z80 bank-window bus theft, both of which are live during active display in every sound-ON build.
findings.evidence:
The guard (raster_dsl.emp:1240):

    ensure(cost <= gap * RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC,
           "raster program: the fire at screen line {...} models at {cost} cycles but only {gap} scanline(s) = {gap * RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC} cycles remain ...")

The ceiling is the whole nominal line (raster_dsl.emp:983):

    pub const RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC       = 488

The per-word term is instruction timing only (raster_dsl.emp:998):

    pub const RASTER_STREAM_WORD_CYC    = 30     // one streamed word: move.w to VDP_DATA + dbf

30 = move.w (a2)+,abs.l (20) + dbf taken (10). A `move.w` to $C00000 during active display is not a 20-cycle write: it is granted only in one of the VDP's external access slots (~16-18 per H40 active line vs ~200 during blanking), and the 4-entry FIFO means a burst can stall. Nothing in op_work_cyc / op_cost_cycles (raster_dsl.emp:1084-1100) prices that, and nothing prices the 68k bus holds the Z80 takes for its banked ROM read-ahead — the FILL path it runs on for the whole of active display, since SND_CTRL_DMA_ACTIVE is only raised around the VBlank window (vblank.emp:118-126).

The calibration is explicitly bus-quiesced, by the probe's own admission (tools/raster_cost_probe.py:36-40):

    THE PALETTE MASK IS FORCED CONSTANT across every fixture (PIN_MASK below) rather than
    derived from the ops. ... a mask that varied by fixture would vary the VBlank palette DMA
    between fixtures -- bus traffic that competes with the very handler being measured.
    Holding it fixed removes the confound

and the fitted numbers came back with "spread 0" across boots (raster_dsl.emp:1045-1050), the signature of a contention-free measurement.

Failure walk: author two fires whose worst-case gap is 1 line and whose modelled cost is 480 (e.g. a SetReg fire plus a 1-word stream at the fall-through depth). The guard passes at 480 <= 488. On hardware the two data-port writes plus the Z80's read-ahead push real elapsed time past 488, so the arm word for the NEXT record — which raster.emp:706 writes FIRST precisely because "it is the one write that must not be lost" — is written after the VDP has already reloaded from reg $0A, i.e. one event too late. Per Ruling 1b that mis-schedules gap(i+1 -> i+2) and, because arm words are RELATIVE, desynchronises the whole tail of the chain for that frame.

Today's shipped content is not at the ceiling — the worst admitted ratio in tree is the R1 restore at 704 against a height-2 band's 976 (72%), and OJZ channel 0's 526 against 976 (54%, ojz_effects.emp:616-620) — so this is latent, not a live wrong pixel. It becomes load-bearing the moment Aurora authors against the guard rather than against measured content.

GATE BLINDNESS: the only thing that checks the model against hardware is `raster_cost_probe`, and it is the same instrument that was calibrated with the bus deliberately quiesced; it also reports a per-routine cycle SUM, which cannot distinguish "the fire fit in its gap" from "the fire overran and the next fire was late". No gate varies Z80 load, runs a fire pair at the admitted ceiling, or observes sub-line write placement.
findings.fix_sketch: Either (a) derate the constant — keep RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC = 488 as the physical line and add a named RASTER_LINE_USABLE_CYC (= 488 - a measured contention allowance) that check_density and `band()` use — or (b) add a per-stream-word FIFO/slot term to op_cost_cycles. Whichever is taken, the margin must be a NAMED constant with the measurement behind it, not folded into 488, so the next re-measurement can move it.

findings.title: A patched program can be armed a frame before Pal_Variant_Stage is re-derived for the incoming section
findings.claim: Effects_InstallPreset publishes the incoming patched program (which makes it armable at the very next VBlank) while Pal_Variant_Stage still holds staging derived from the OUTGOING section's base palette — the re-derive is deferred to Palette_Compose, which runs after the whole state update. A VBlank in that window arms the new program and both readers of the staging (the handler's .op_region and the frame-top ship DMA) serve the previous section's colours for a frame.
findings.evidence:
Install order (preset.emp:257, :288) — the palette LOAD happens here, the DERIVE does not:

        jbsr    Palette_LoadPal          // :257 — writes Palette_Buffer, marks base dirty
        ...
        jbsr    Raster_InstallPatched    // :288 — publishes Patch_Tab + Raster_Program

The derive is a separate, later phase (game_loop.emp:41-49):

        jsr     (a0) as GameState       // the crossing (Parallax_CheckBoundary -> Effects_InstallPreset) happens in here
        ...
        jbsr    Palette_Compose

and Palette_SetVariant only MARKS (palette.emp:291): `ori.b #PAL_ACT_VARIANT | PAL_ACT_VARIANT_STALE, Pal_Active`; the work is Palette_DoVariants -> Palette_DeriveVariant, reached from Palette_Compose (palette.emp:383-385), ~19,332 cycles.

So between preset.emp:288 and game_loop.emp:49, Raster_Program/Raster_Patch_Tab name the NEW program while Pal_Variant_Stage is the OLD derivation. A VBlank there runs Raster_VBlank -> Raster_BuildSchedule (table is live), arms the handler, and Enqueue_Dirty_Buffers may queue Static_Pal_Ship, whose DMA source is `Pal_Variant_Stage + <stage off>` (raster.emp:1040-1043). Both then serve stale colours for that frame.

The variant POINTER guard does not cover this. Every OJZ preset carries the same variant (ojz_effects.emp:569-575, `variants: [Variant_Water_Deep, 0]`), so `cmp.l Pal_Variant_Ptr, d1 / beq .variant0_same` (preset.emp:265-266) skips the call — but the staging is derived FROM Palette_Buffer, and Palette_Compose's base arm re-marks it stale on any base change (palette.emp:342, `ori.b #PAL_ACT_VARIANT_STALE, Pal_Active   // the base copy moves lines 1-3`). OJZ_Preset_Sec2 loads a different base (`pal: OJZ_TestPal`, ojz_effects.emp:573), so crossing into or out of section 2 is exactly the case where the staging is stale relative to the base the same VBlank is DMAing to CRAM.

Reachability: GameLoop is VSync-locked, so on a non-lagging frame the main loop is parked in VSync_Wait when VBlank fires and the window is never crossed — which is what the D1-1 measurement recorded (DEFERRED_WORK.md:4734, "3/3 crossings, no VBlank"). It is reachable on a LAG frame, where VInt_Lag also calls Raster_VBlank (vblank.emp:291) and Enqueue_Dirty_Buffers, i.e. the whole arming + ship path runs. This is a NEW instance of the D1-1 window class, not the booked one: the adjudication's D1-1 concerns the anchor bank ("today that same VBlank is CORRECT — it derives from Effects_Screen_L, already re-latched at preset.emp:247"), which is true and is unrelated to the variant staging the same VBlank publishes.

GATE BLINDNESS: no gate induces a lag frame at a crossing. `effects_gates.py` gates on ab_runner determinism plus arm-word shape (`effects_scene_assert`) — arm words are correct here, only the colours are stale. `raster_source_gate` asserts the source ADDRESS a2, never its contents. And oracle CRAM reads cannot see the mid-frame writes at all, by this suite's own recorded finding (ojz_effects.emp:275-283: "emulator_read_cram cannot see a mid-scanline CRAM write during active display").
findings.fix_sketch: Make the derive part of the install rather than of the next compose: call Palette_DoVariants (or a single-slot derive) at the end of Effects_InstallPreset, after Palette_LoadPal and BEFORE Raster_InstallPatched publishes the program. That costs the ~19k cycles on crossing frames only (they already pay Palette_LoadPal + SetVariant) and makes 'staging matches the installed program' a publish-order invariant instead of a phase-order coincidence. Cheaper alternative if the cost is unacceptable: defer the ARM instead — have Raster_InstallPatched stage the program the way Raster_Install does, so the first VBlank that can arm it is the one after Palette_Compose.

findings.title: Stale safety premise: the deleted-autoinc-reassert argument asserts 'no VDP access' where two now exist
findings.claim: VInt_Lag's justification for deleting its `move.w #$8F02, VDP_CTRL` rests on the claim that nothing between Flush_VDP_Shadow and the plane drain touches the VDP. Two VDP writers have since landed in exactly that span, so the load-bearing premise is false — the conclusion still holds, but only by accident of which registers they happen to write.
findings.fix_sketch: Rewrite the paragraph to state the real invariant: 'two writers sit in this span (buffers.emp:429 .ship_reg, parallax.emp:518 reg $0B); neither can write reg $0F because raster_dsl.emp:1385-1387 forbids $8F in a fire's reg words and reg $0B is the only register Parallax_Active_Config drives.' Then, since the ship's reg list is the growable one, consider an ensure in ship_trailer mirroring the fire-level $8F/$8A refusal so the premise is enforced where the words are minted rather than asserted in prose two modules away.

findings.title: Dense tier writes CRAM with no blanking delay, so every dense line's burst lands mid-active-display
findings.claim: The row-119 blanking delay is applied to the sparse CRAM paths only; `.dense_body` issues its command and three colour words with no spin at all, so each dense line's write lands part-way across the row above its target — the same artifact class the sparse fix removed, applied to every line of every dense run, and structurally invisible to the instrument the dense tier is measured with.
findings.evidence:
Every sparse CRAM-class op parks its burst with a cycle-counted spin (raster.emp:750-754 .op_cram, :770-774 .op_region, :806-809 .op_pal_restore), e.g.

        move.l  (a1)+, (a2)             // full CRAM command in ONE move.l
        moveq   #EFX_BLANK_DELAY, d1
    .cram_delay:
        dbf     d1, .cram_delay

The dense body has no equivalent (raster.emp:828-841):

    .dense_body:
        move.w  #RASTER_ARM_EVERY_LINE, (a2)       // reg $0A=0: fire every line
        move.l  Raster_Dense_Cmd, (a2)             // constant command (sets the address)
        tst.w   Raster_Dense_Kind
        bne.s   .ramp_body
        movea.l Raster_Dense_Cursor, a1
        move.w  (a1)+, VDP_DATA
        move.w  (a1)+, VDP_DATA
        move.w  (a1)+, VDP_DATA

The magnitude anchor is this file's own R1 calibration datum (raster.emp:793-802): with ZERO delay the restore burst "completed at x~180 of the row ABOVE the authored edge (leading-early by ~150 cyc -- and the bare single-op cram ON fire spilled identically at x~170)". The dense body's pre-write path is strictly SHORTER than either of those (no op fetch, no 1- or 5-rung compare chain, no op_count read, no lea/adda source setup, no spin), so its colour words complete earlier than x~170 on the row above — i.e. the value intended for row R appears on row R-1 from roughly the left third onward, and row R carries the previous value across that same left third. For OJZ_TestGradient's 8 levels over 96 lines that is a visible horizontal step at each of the 8 level boundaries; for a per-line ramp it is a uniform horizontal shear.

The dense tier's own gate cannot see it, by construction. ojz_effects.emp:284-289 records the instrument: "Each row is classified by the ramp LEVEL recovered from the changed pixels' colour, so art coverage changes how many pixels carry the signal without changing what the signal says." A per-row level classifier reports the majority level and is therefore blind to a row carrying TWO levels — which is exactly the artifact. The recorded result ("8 distinct monotonic levels, band boundaries landing exactly on 96+12k") is fully consistent with a ~30-40% left-edge spill on every row.

GATE BLINDNESS, restated: `raster_source_gate` observes the region op's source pointer only and never enters the dense path; `raster_cost_probe` measures cycle totals, which are indifferent to where in the row a write lands; `effects_scene_assert` checks arm words and opcodes; and oracle screenshot capture is documented in this repo as non-deterministic and not usable as a gate. Only a pinned-camera framebuffer column-bucket capture — the same instrument that produced the row-119 '1 px -> 0 px' number — can settle it, and no gate runs one against a dense fixture.

STATED HONESTLY: the exact x is a prediction from the R1 datum plus an instruction-count comparison, not a measurement. What IS certain from the code is that the dense path carries no delay while every sparse CRAM path does, and that the difference is undocumented — the row-119 note (raster.emp:216-222) enumerates its residuals and names only the OP_SET_REG mixed-fire case.
findings.fix_sketch: First, document the asymmetry in the row-119 residual note so it stops looking like an oversight. Then measure a dense fixture with the row-119 column-bucket method; if the spill is confirmed, the fix is a per-line spin in .dense_body sized like EFX_BLANK_DELAY (40 cyc x L lines is ~3.8k/frame for a 96-line run) plus a compensating -1 in the dense constructors' `top`, since parking the write past the row end shifts value j from row top+j to top+j+1.

findings.title: Dense-tier CRAM bodies carry no blanking delay — writes land ~100 cyc (~88 px) earlier than the calibrated sparse landing
findings.claim: `.dense_body` (OP_RUN_GRADIENT) and `.ramp_body` (OP_RUN_RAMP with a CRAM target) issue their CRAM words with no EFX_BLANK_DELAY spin, so they land 100 and ~62 cycles respectively EARLIER in the line than the oracle-calibrated OP_CRAM landing — putting 2 of every 3 gradient words inside the preceding row's active display, and putting a CRAM ramp's single word exactly on the active-display edge with ~4 cycles of margin.
findings.evidence:
raster.emp:728-738 (sparse, calibrated): `move.l (a1)+,(a2)` / `moveq #EFX_BLANK_DELAY,d1` / `.cram_delay: dbf d1,.cram_delay` / `move.w (a1)+,d1` before the first `move.w (a1)+,VDP_DATA`. raster.emp:828-839 (dense): `move.w #RASTER_ARM_EVERY_LINE,(a2)` / `move.l Raster_Dense_Cmd,(a2)` / `tst.w Raster_Dense_Kind` / `beq.s .ramp_body` / `movea.l Raster_Dense_Cursor,a1` / `move.w (a1)+,VDP_DATA` — no spin anywhere.

CYCLE WALK from the shared divergence point (`tst.w Raster_Dense_Lines`, :695), using DENSITY-EVIDENCE.md's own hand-verified op terms where they apply:
  sparse: bne nt 8 + movea.l 16 + move.w (a1)+,(a2) 12 + move.w (a1)+,d0 8 + cmpi 8 + beq nt 8 + subq 4 + bmi nt 8 = 72, then FETCH 8 + DISPATCH_HIT 18 + command move.l 20 + moveq 4 + spin 54 + count read 8 = 112. First colour word at 184.
  dense gradient: bne taken 10 + move.w #imm,(a2) 12 + move.l abs,(a2) 24 + tst.w 12 + beq.s taken 10 + movea.l 16 = 84. First colour word at 84. DELTA = 100 cycles (>=90 under any abs.w/abs.l mix).
  dense ramp: 10+12+24+12+10 + move.l acc 16 + add.l step 18 + move.l acc 16 + swap 4 = 122. DELTA = 62 cycles.

ANCHOR: the sparse landing is calibrated, not free-floating — raster.emp:203-232 records that removing the spin (moveq 4 + dbf 54 = 58 cyc) moved the write from '1 px' inside row 119 to 0 px, so the calibrated write clears the active-display edge by AT MOST 58 cycles. A write issued 100 cycles earlier therefore lands at least 42 cycles (~37 px at 7 mclk/cyc vs 8 mclk/px) INSIDE the preceding row, and with RASTER_STREAM_WORD_CYC=30 the second word is still ~12 cycles short of the edge while the third clears it by only ~18 — which is exactly the alternating pattern the P2 gate measured and could not explain (docs/benchmarks/effects-p2/GATE-EVIDENCE.md:76-84: 'Boundary rows 132, 156 and 180 carry both the outgoing and incoming level; boundary rows 108, 120, 144 and 168 carry only the incoming one ... alternates with sub-line timing drift'). A ~18-cycle jitter in interrupt recognition flips it, which the arithmetic now names.

PARTIALLY KNOWN, and I say so explicitly: the gradient half is recorded as a measured residual in GATE-EVIDENCE.md:104 ('The dense body does not use OP_CRAM, so the blanking delay does not touch it — confirmed rather than assumed'). It is NOT booked in docs/BUGS.md or docs/DEFERRED_WORK.md, so it is not on the pre-freeze list. THREE things are new: (1) the quantification above (nobody has stated how far early, so nobody could see it is a fixable ~100 cycles rather than a hardware floor); (2) the blast radius reaches OP_RUN_RAMP, whose constructor explicitly admits a CRAM target (raster.emp:443 `if cmd == vdp_comm(addr, VdpTarget.Cram, VdpOp.Write) { is_cram = 1 }`) — the only ramp ever measured is VSRAM (games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp:483 `cmd: vdp_comm(2, VdpTarget.Vsram, VdpOp.Write)`), so the parameterised-CRAM-ramp path is unmeasured AND sits ~4 cycles from the edge, i.e. it will straddle it frame to frame; (3) a cheap closure exists and was never costed — the dense body's measured marginal is ~342 cyc/line against a 488-cycle line (docs/superpowers/notes/2026-08-14-effects-vocabulary-review.md:339), so ~146 cycles of per-line headroom are available, enough for the ~100-cycle spin that would put the dense landing exactly on the calibrated sparse one.
findings.fix_sketch: Give the dense bodies their own calibrated spin (a third knob beside EFX_BLANK_DELAY / EFX_RESTORE_DELAY — never share, same reasoning as :236-238): `moveq #EFX_DENSE_DELAY,d1 / dbf` between `move.l Raster_Dense_Cmd,(a2)` and the first VDP_DATA write, seeded at 10 for the gradient (10*10+14+4 = 118 ≈ the 100-cycle deficit) and ~5 for the ramp, then oracle-verify on the OJZ_TestGradient fixture's seven boundary rows (the artifact is the instrument: the alternating both-levels rows must go to incoming-only). If it is NOT fixed, book it in BUGS.md before the P1 identity freeze, because after the freeze it costs fix->repin->refreeze; and either way refuse a CRAM target in raster_ramp_program until it is measured.

findings.title: Frame-top HInt-entry slop is ~155 cycles, unguarded and unmeasured; each collapsed underflow shifts every boundary one line down
findings.claim: The two-priming-record design assumes priming record 0's handler completes before screen line 1's line-counter underflow; that gives only ~155 usable cycles of slop, the delay is set by how far the VBlank pipeline runs past the end of VBlank (load-dependent), and nothing measures or bounds it. Every collapsed underflow shifts every boundary in the frame down one scanline and can push the last record past line 223, where it never fires at all.
findings.evidence:
raster.emp:610-612 `moveq #0, d0` + :621-622 `lea Raster_HInt(pc), a0` / `jbsr HBlank_Install` — the arm is reg $0A = 0, and raster.emp:34-39 states the model: 'Raster_VBlank leaves reg $0A = 0, so cheap no-op fires land on lines 0 and 1 and load the first two real arm words; every fire from the third onward lands exactly on its authored line.'

MECHANISM. The line counter runs autonomously: it reloads from reg $0A at every underflow whether or not the interrupt was serviced, and IRQ4 is a level with a single pending flag, so two underflows inside one masked window deliver ONE handler invocation. Raster_HInt is reached only below IPL 6, and VBlank_Handler holds IPL 6 for the whole pipeline (vblank.emp:43-96, dispatching VInt_Level at :110-259). So:
  - pipeline exits inside line 0 or early line 1 -> P0's handler runs, and its `move.w (a1)+,(a2)` arm write (raster.emp:698) still precedes line 1's underflow. Schedule INTACT. Budget: 488 cycles from line 0's underflow, minus the priming record's measured 286 (DENSITY-EVIDENCE F0: 572/2) minus ~44 autovector entry = ~155 cycles of slop.
  - pipeline exits after line 1's underflow -> the line-0 and line-1 underflows collapse into one invocation. P0 runs during line 2, its arm reaches reg $0A before line 2's underflow, so P1 fires at line 2 and record 0 fires at fire line L0+1 instead of L0. Every later record inherits the +1 because the gaps are relative. Verified against the builder's own arithmetic (Raster_BuildSchedule :1144-1151: `sub.w d0,d3` / `subq.w #1,d3` / `move.b d3,1(a2)` with `moveq #1,d0` seeding prev = priming record 1).
  - the tail case is not cosmetic: a record whose shifted fire line exceeds 223 gets no underflow at all, so e.g. a band's OP_PAL_RESTORE OFF edge never runs and the ON tint runs to the bottom of the screen for that frame.

WHY THE TRIGGER IS REACHABLE. docs/ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md:854 derives DMA_BUDGET_NTSC = 6144 as '488.6 68k cyc/line x 38 blank lines ... x ~0.89 safety margin for the uncharged non-DMA VInt tail' — i.e. the entire allowance for everything the budget does not charge is ~11% of the window (~2040 cycles). That tail is: Raster_VBlank + Raster_BuildSchedule, Flush_VDP_Shadow (19 registers), Enqueue_Dirty_Buffers including its own '~704 cyc (4 dirty lines)' of snapshot splices (buffers.emp:298), the Critical charge walk, Vscroll_Write, Read_Controllers (6-button, both ports) and the 12-instruction press/held latch block (vblank.emp:238-256). On a fade frame that is plausibly over 2040 cycles, and DEFERRED_WORK.md already records '~100% budget, zero headroom' frames. Two lines of overrun is ~977 cycles.

Nothing in the tree measures the pipeline's exit line: check_density (raster_dsl.emp:1224-1246) models only inter-fire gaps, and the frame-top gap from priming record 1 to the first real fire is never checked at all.
findings.fix_sketch: Cheap and zero-byte in release: under DEBUG, sample the beam/HV counter at VInt_Level's exit and latch a high-water 'raster slip' line into a counter (the same shape as Lag_Frame_Count), so the slop is observable instead of theoretical. If it turns out non-zero on real content, the structural fix is to make the priming pair tolerant — e.g. a third priming record, or arm the first gap from a line-compare on the first fire rather than from a build-time relative gap. Also record the requirement in the module header, which currently states the priming model without stating that it needs IRQ4 unmasked before line 1's underflow.

findings.title: Two in-code sites still prescribe the retired six-consecutive-fire idiom that check_density refuses
findings.claim: The full-line-region authoring recipe in raster.emp's OP_PAL_REGION comment and in fire()'s own stream_words error message both tell authors to use consecutive stream fires on successive lines, which check_density in the same file refuses (3-word CRAM 518 > 488, region 566 > 488) and which docs/EFFECTS_AUTHORING.md has formally retired on measured evidence.
findings.evidence:
raster.emp:103-108: 'a region is a SCOPED swap ... A full-line region is authored as CONSECUTIVE OP_PAL_REGION fires on successive lines, so such a boundary takes ceil(N/3) lines to complete.' raster_dsl.emp:341-342, the ensure an author hits FIRST when they exceed three words: 'split the writes across consecutive fires — a full 16-colour line takes ceil(16/3) = 6 of them, one per scanline. That six-fire idiom is OURS...'.

Both are refused by raster_dsl.emp:1240 `ensure(cost <= gap * RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC, ...)` with the pinned costs 518 (F3, 3-word cram) and 566 (F4, 3-word region) against RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC = 488 and gap = 1 for successive lines. docs/EFFECTS_AUTHORING.md:755-770 says so in as many words: 'THE SIX-CONSECUTIVE-FIRE IDIOM IS RETIRED. It was measured, and it does not work ... raster_program now refuses such a schedule at build time'.

Failure scenario: an author (or Aurora, which will bind this authoring surface) writes a 16-colour line swap, trips the stream_words ensure at 4+ words, follows its instruction verbatim to six consecutive one-per-scanline fires, and hits a SECOND build error from check_density — with the first error's advice as the thing that caused it. Nothing is mis-rendered; the defect is that the guard message on the frozen substrate's authoring surface documents a shape the substrate rejects, and the same stale recipe is what a hand-author reading the runtime's opcode documentation would implement.
findings.fix_sketch: Re-point both texts at the dense tier, matching EFFECTS_AUTHORING.md's retirement note: in raster_dsl.emp:342 replace 'consecutive fires ... one per scanline' with 'fires at least two scanlines apart, or raster_gradient_program for per-line work'; in raster.emp:103-108 state that consecutive region fires are refused by the density guard and give the every-other-line count (2*ceil(N/3) lines). Zero bytes — both are comments/ensure strings.

findings.title: check_density's budget is inclusive at exactly one scanline and charges no interrupt-recognition latency
findings.claim: A 2-word stream_cram fire models at exactly 488 == 1 * RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC and is therefore ADMITTED on adjacent lines with zero margin, while the real elapsed cost of a fire additionally includes the interrupted instruction's retirement and the autovector entry the model cannot see — so the boundary shape the guard admits overruns, and the overrun accumulates across a run of adjacent fires.
findings.evidence:
raster_dsl.emp:1240 `ensure(cost <= gap * RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC, ...)` — inclusive. Cost of a 2-word stream_cram fire from the model's own pinned terms (raster_dsl.emp:991-1007, :1067): 302 + (8 + 18 + 90 + 2*30 + 10) = 488, i.e. exactly the limit, admitted at gap = 1. The model's constants are per-fire handler cycles fitted to oracle's per-routine profiler row (DENSITY-EVIDENCE.md, 'Read the per-routine row instead'); the 68000 additionally cannot take IRQ4 until the current main-loop instruction retires, which for the movem-heavy main loop is tens of cycles, and that latency is not in any term.

That the overrun accumulates rather than self-correcting is already measured for the next shape up: EFFECTS_AUTHORING.md:765-768 — 'Nothing is dropped ... but each write lands progressively later, inside active display ... rows 111-113 each carry two different authored colours, switching at x = 232/248/294 of 320' (the x positions marching right across three rows IS the accumulation). The only adjacent-fire shape ever measured clean is the 1-word one (458 modelled / '454' measured, EFFECTS_AUTHORING.md:778, 'six of them adjacent were verified clean'); the 488 boundary case has never been run.

Failure scenario: two `patchable` records whose bands abut with one scanline between their reachable edges, each carrying one 2-word stream_cram (a two-entry tint boundary — well inside RASTER_CRAM_MAX). Build passes at 488 <= 488. At runtime each fire finishes ~44+ cycles past the next underflow, so the second fire's colour words land ~40 px into their row and the artifact grows with every additional adjacent fire in the chain.
findings.fix_sketch: Make the comparison strict, or subtract a named entry-latency constant: `cost + RASTER_ENTRY_LATENCY_CYC <= gap * RASTER_SCANLINE_CYC` with RASTER_ENTRY_LATENCY_CYC seeded at 44 (autovector) and a comment that it also stands in for instruction-boundary latency. Add a which-side-of-the-line pin in the existing pair at :1156-1170 for the 2-word/adjacent case so the boundary is stated as a build-time fact in whichever direction is chosen.

findings.title: raster_ramp_program's screen-range bound uses the CRAM landing rule for VSRAM targets too, silently dropping the last line of a VSRAM ramp
findings.claim: The constructor documents that a VSRAM value lands on top+j+1 while a CRAM value lands on top+j, then bounds the run with a single `top + lines <= 224` derived from the CRAM rule — so a VSRAM ramp authored at the ceiling has its final computed value land on nonexistent screen line 224 and never display.
findings.evidence:
raster.emp:402-409 states the split explicitly: 'CRAM target — value j displays on screen line top + j; VSRAM target — value j displays on screen line top + j + 1 ... MEASURED, not assumed (docs/benchmarks/effects-p3/RAMP-EVIDENCE.md, 74 of 74 rows)'. The bound at :433-434 is target-blind: `ensure(top + lines <= 224, "raster_ramp_program: run {top}..{top + lines - 1} runs past screen line 223")`. For VSRAM the run actually occupies top+1..top+lines, so top+lines == 224 places the last value on line 224. The identical target-blind bound is at :348 for the gradient (CRAM-only, correct there).

Failure scenario: `raster_ramp_program(top: 128, lines: 96, cmd: vdp_comm(2, VdpTarget.Vsram, VdpOp.Write), ...)` builds green (128+96 = 224) and runs 96 dense lines, but only 95 of them are visible; the accumulator's last step is written to VSRAM during the last active line and displays nowhere. An author counting rows to match a horizon or a water surface is off by one at the bottom of the run with no diagnostic. The shipped fixture (ojz_effects.emp:472-484, top 112 / lines 96 -> 208) does not reach the edge, so this is latent.

This is the one place in the subject where the measured VSRAM N+1 / CRAM N split is stated and then not honoured; every other consumer I walked honours it (stream_vsram's -1 is the sparse rule and is measured correct, raster_dsl.emp:240-244; op_mask returns 0 for Vsram at :898; the ramp's landing is deliberately not bias-corrected, :411-415).
findings.fix_sketch: Make the bound target-aware with the flags the function already computes: `ensure(top + lines + is_vsram <= 224, ...)` placed after the is_cram/is_vsram election at :441-446, with the message naming the VSRAM landing rule. Comptime only, zero emitted bytes, and it cannot change the shipped fixture (208 + 1 <= 224).
